```
    23→// Pricing constants for video_enhance task (fal.ai rates)
    24→const VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING = {
    25→  // FILM (interpolation): $0.0013 per compute second
    26→  FILM_COST_PER_SECOND: 0.0013,
    27→  // FlashVSR (upscale): $0.0005 per megapixel (width × height × frames / 1,000,000)
    28→  FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL: 0.0005,
    29→};
    30→
    31→// Special cost calculation for video_enhance task
    32→// Combines FILM (time-based) and FlashVSR (megapixel-based) pricing
    33→function calculateVideoEnhanceCost(taskParams: any): { cost: number; breakdown: any } {
    34→  let totalCost = 0;
    35→  const breakdown: any = {};
    36→
    37→  // Get result data from task params (worker should populate this)
    38→  const result = taskParams?.result || taskParams;
    39→
    40→  // FILM interpolation cost: $0.0013 per compute second
    41→  if (result?.interpolation_compute_seconds && result.interpolation_compute_seconds > 0) {
    42→    const filmCost = VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FILM_COST_PER_SECOND * result.interpolation_compute_seconds;
    43→    totalCost += filmCost;
    44→    breakdown.interpolation = {
    45→      compute_seconds: result.interpolation_compute_seconds,
    46→      cost_per_second: VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FILM_COST_PER_SECOND,
    47→      cost: Math.round(filmCost * 1000000) / 1000000,
    48→    };
    49→  }
    50→
    51→  // FlashVSR upscale cost: $0.0005 per megapixel
    52→  if (result?.output_width && result?.output_height && result?.output_frames) {
    53→    const megapixels = (result.output_width * result.output_height * result.output_frames) / 1_000_000;
    54→    const upscaleCost = VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL * megapixels;
    55→    totalCost += upscaleCost;
    56→    breakdown.upscale = {
    57→      output_width: result.output_width,
    58→      output_height: result.output_height,
    59→      output_frames: result.output_frames,
    60→      megapixels: Math.round(megapixels * 100) / 100,
    61→      cost_per_megapixel: VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL,
    62→      cost: Math.round(upscaleCost * 1000000) / 1000000,
    63→    };
    64→  }
    65→
    66→  return {
    67→    cost: Math.round(totalCost * 1000000) / 1000000,
    68→    breakdown,
    69→  };
    70→}
    71→
    72→// Calculate cost based on billing type and task configuration
    73→function calculateTaskCost(
    74→  taskType: string,
    75→  billingType: string,
    76→  baseCostPerSecond: number,
    77→  unitCost: number,
    78→  durationSeconds: number,
    79→  costFactors: any,
    80→  taskParams: any
    81→): { cost: number; breakdown?: any } {
    82→  // Special case: video_enhance has compound pricing (FILM + FlashVSR)
    83→  if (taskType === 'video_enhance') {
    84→    return calculateVideoEnhanceCost(taskParams);
    85→  }
    86→
    87→  let totalCost;
    88→  if (billingType === 'per_unit') {
    89→    totalCost = unitCost || 0;
    90→  } else {
    91→    totalCost = baseCostPerSecond * durationSeconds;
    92→  }
    93→
    94→  // Apply cost factors regardless of billing type
    95→  if (costFactors) {
    96→    if (costFactors.resolution && taskParams.resolution) {
    97→      const resolutionMultiplier = costFactors.resolution[taskParams.resolution] || 1;
    98→      totalCost *= resolutionMultiplier;
    99→    }
   100→    if (costFactors.frameCount && taskParams.frame_count) {
   101→      if (billingType === 'per_unit') {
   102→        totalCost += costFactors.frameCount * taskParams.frame_count;
   103→      } else {
   104→        totalCost += costFactors.frameCount * taskParams.frame_count * durationSeconds;
   105→      }
   106→    }
   107→    if (costFactors.modelType && taskParams.model_type) {
   108→      const modelMultiplier = costFactors.modelType[taskParams.model_type] || 1;
   109→      totalCost *= modelMultiplier;
   110→    }
   111→  }
   112→
   113→  return { cost: Math.round(totalCost * 1000) / 1000 };
   114→}
   115→
   116→serve(async (req) => {
   117→  const supabaseUrl = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL');
   118→  const serviceKey = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY');
   119→
   120→  if (!supabaseUrl || !serviceKey) {
   121→    console.error("[CALCULATE-TASK-COST] Missing required environment variables");
   122→    return jsonResponse({ error: 'Server configuration error' }, 500);
   123→  }
   124→
   125→  const supabaseAdmin = createClient(supabaseUrl, serviceKey, {
   126→    auth: {
   127→      autoRefreshToken: false,
   128→      persistSession: false
   129→    }
   130→  });
   131→
   132→  // Create logger (task_id will be set after parsing body)
   133→  const logger = new SystemLogger(supabaseAdmin, 'calculate-task-cost');
   134→
   135→  // Handle CORS preflight requests
   136→  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
   137→    return jsonResponse({ ok: true });
   138→  }
   139→
   140→  if (req.method !== 'POST') {
   141→    logger.warn("Method not allowed", { method: req.method });
   142→    await logger.flush();
   143→    return jsonResponse({ error: 'Method not allowed' }, 405);
   144→  }
   145→
   146→  // Verify service role authentication - this function should only be called internally
   147→  const authHeader = req.headers.get("Authorization");
   148→  if (!authHeader?.startsWith("Bearer ") || authHeader.slice(7) !== serviceKey) {
   149→    logger.warn("Unauthorized - service role required");
   150→    await logger.flush();
   151→    return jsonResponse({ error: "Unauthorized - service role required" }, 401);
   152→  }
   153→
   154→  try {
   155→    const { task_id } = await req.json();
   156→
   157→    if (!task_id) {
   158→      logger.error("Missing task_id in request");
   159→      await logger.flush();
   160→      return jsonResponse({ error: 'task_id is required' }, 400);
   161→    }
   162→
   163→    // Set task_id for all subsequent logs
   164→    logger.setDefaultTaskId(task_id);
   165→    logger.info("Calculating task cost", { task_id });
   166→
   167→    // Get task details
   168→    const { data: task, error: taskError } = await supabaseAdmin
   169→      .from('tasks')
   170→      .select(`
   171→        id,
   172→        task_type,
   173→        params,
   174→        status,
   175→        generation_started_at,
   176→        generation_processed_at,
   177→        project_id,
   178→        projects(user_id)
   179→      `)
   180→      .eq('id', task_id)
   181→      .single();
   182→
   183→    if (taskError || !task) {
   184→      logger.error("Task not found", { error: taskError?.message });
   185→      await logger.flush();
   186→      return jsonResponse({ error: 'Task not found' }, 404);
   187→    }
   188→
   189→    logger.debug("Task found", { 
   190→      task_type: task.task_type, 
   191→      status: task.status,
   192→      has_timestamps: !!(task.generation_started_at && task.generation_processed_at)
   193→    });
   194→
   195→    // Check if task has both start and end times
   196→    if (!task.generation_started_at || !task.generation_processed_at) {
   197→      logger.error("Missing timestamps", { 
   198→        has_started_at: !!task.generation_started_at, 
   199→        has_processed_at: !!task.generation_processed_at 
   200→      });
   201→      await logger.flush();
   202→      return jsonResponse({
   203→        error: 'Task must have both generation_started_at and generation_processed_at timestamps'
   204→      }, 400);
   205→    }
   206→
   207→    // Check if task is a sub-task of an orchestrator - skip billing if so (parent will be billed)
   208→    // Uses shared detection: checks all param paths, validates UUID, guards against self-reference
   209→    const subTaskOrchestratorId = getSubTaskOrchestratorId(task.params, task.id);
   210→
   211→    if (subTaskOrchestratorId) {
   212→      logger.info("Skipping cost calculation (sub-task)", {
   213→        orchestrator_task_id: subTaskOrchestratorId
   214→      });
   215→      await logger.flush();
   216→      return jsonResponse({
   217→        success: true,
   218→        skipped: true,
   219→        reason: 'Task is sub-task of orchestrator, parent task will be billed',
   220→        orchestrator_task_id: subTaskOrchestratorId,
   221→        task_id: task.id
   222→      });
   223→    }
   224→
   225→    // Check if this is an orchestrator task - calculate cost based on sub-task durations
   226→    const { data: subTasks, error: subTasksError } = await supabaseAdmin
   227→      .from('tasks')
   228→      .select(`
   229→        id,
   230→        generation_started_at,
   231→        generation_processed_at,
   232→        status
   233→      `)
   234→      .or(buildSubTaskFilter(task_id))
   235→      .eq('status', 'Complete');
   236→
   237→    let durationSeconds;
   238→    if (subTasks && subTasks.length > 0) {
   239→      // This is an orchestrator task with sub-tasks - sum their durations
   240→      logger.info("Orchestrator task detected", { sub_task_count: subTasks.length });
   241→
   242→      let totalSubTaskDuration = 0;
   243→      for (const subTask of subTasks) {
   244→        if (subTask.generation_started_at && subTask.generation_processed_at) {
   245→          const subStartTime = new Date(subTask.generation_started_at);
   246→          const subEndTime = new Date(subTask.generation_processed_at);
   247→          const subDuration = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((subEndTime.getTime() - subStartTime.getTime()) / 1000));
   248→          totalSubTaskDuration += subDuration;
   249→        }
   250→      }
   251→
   252→      durationSeconds = totalSubTaskDuration;
   253→      logger.debug("Orchestrator duration calculated", { 
   254→        sub_task_count: subTasks.length, 
   255→        total_duration_seconds: durationSeconds 
   256→      });
   257→    } else {
   258→      // Regular task - use its own duration
   259→      const startTime = new Date(task.generation_started_at);
   260→      const endTime = new Date(task.generation_processed_at);
   261→      durationSeconds = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((endTime.getTime() - startTime.getTime()) / 1000));
   262→    }
   263→
   264→    // Idempotency: avoid double-billing if this function is called multiple times for the same task.
   265→    // The credits ledger is intended to be immutable, so we should skip if a spend entry already exists.
   266→    const { data: existingSpendEntries, error: existingSpendError } = await supabaseAdmin
   267→      .from('credits_ledger')
   268→      .select('id, amount, created_at')
   269→      .eq('task_id', task.id)
   270→      .eq('type', 'spend')
   271→      .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
   272→      .limit(1);
   273→
   274→    if (existingSpendError) {
   275→      logger.error("Failed to check existing credit ledger entries", { error: existingSpendError.message });
   276→      await logger.flush();
   277→      return jsonResponse({ error: 'Failed to check existing cost records' }, 500);
   278→    }
   279→
   280→    if (existingSpendEntries && existingSpendEntries.length > 0) {
   281→      const existing = existingSpendEntries[0];
   282→      logger.info("Cost already recorded - skipping", {
   283→        ledger_id: existing.id,
   284→        existing_amount: existing.amount
   285→      });
   286→      await logger.flush();
   287→      return jsonResponse({
   288→        success: true,
   289→        skipped: true,
   290→        reason: 'Cost already recorded for this task',
   291→        task_id: task.id,
   292→        ledger_id: existing.id,
   293→        existing_amount: existing.amount
   294→      });
   295→    }
   296→
   297→    // Get task type configuration
   298→    const { data: taskType, error: taskTypeError } = await supabaseAdmin
   299→      .from('task_types')
   300→      .select('*')
   301→      .eq('name', task.task_type)
   302→      .eq('is_active', true)
   303→      .single();
   304→
   305→    if (taskTypeError || !taskType) {
   306→      logger.warn("No task type config found, using defaults", { task_type: task.task_type });
   307→
   308→      // Use default cost if no config found
   309→      const defaultCostPerSecond = 0.01;
   310→      const cost = defaultCostPerSecond * durationSeconds;
   311→
   312→      const { error: ledgerError } = await supabaseAdmin.from('credits_ledger').insert({
   313→        user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id,
   314→        task_id: task.id,
   315→        amount: -cost,
   316→        type: 'spend',
   317→        metadata: {
   318→          task_type: task.task_type,
   319→          duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   320→          base_cost_per_second: defaultCostPerSecond,
   321→          billing_type: 'per_second',
   322→          calculated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   323→          note: 'Default cost used - no task type configuration found'
   324→        }
   325→      });
   326→
   327→      if (ledgerError) {
   328→        logger.error("Failed to insert into credit ledger (default)", { error: ledgerError.message });
   329→        await logger.flush();
   330→        return jsonResponse({ error: 'Failed to record cost in ledger' }, 500);
   331→      }
   332→
   333→      logger.info("Cost calculated (default rates)", { 
   334→        cost,
   335→        duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   336→        billing_type: 'per_second'
   337→      });
   338→      await logger.flush();
   339→
   340→      return jsonResponse({
   341→        success: true,
   342→        cost: cost,
   343→        duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   344→        base_cost_per_second: defaultCostPerSecond,
   345→        billing_type: 'per_second',
   346→        note: 'Default cost used - no task type configuration found'
   347→      });
   348→    }
   349→
   350→    // Calculate cost based on task type configuration
   351→    const costResult = calculateTaskCost(
   352→      task.task_type,
   353→      taskType.billing_type,
   354→      taskType.base_cost_per_second,
   355→      taskType.unit_cost,
   356→      durationSeconds,
   357→      taskType.cost_factors,
   358→      task.params
   359→    );
   360→    const cost = costResult.cost;
   361→    const costBreakdown = costResult.breakdown;
   362→
   363→    // Validate cost calculation
   364→    if (isNaN(cost) || cost < 0) {
   365→      logger.error("Invalid cost calculated", {
   366→        cost,
   367→        billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   368→        base_cost_per_second: taskType.base_cost_per_second,
   369→        unit_cost: taskType.unit_cost,
   370→        duration: durationSeconds,
   371→        breakdown: costBreakdown
   372→      });
   373→      await logger.flush();
   374→      return jsonResponse({ error: 'Invalid cost calculation' }, 500);
   375→    }
   376→
   377→    // Ensure user exists before inserting credit ledger entry
   378→    const { data: user, error: userError } = await supabaseAdmin
   379→      .from('users')
   380→      .select('id')
   381→      .eq('id', (task as any).projects.user_id)
   382→      .single();
   383→
   384→    if (userError || !user) {
   385→      logger.error("User not found for credit ledger", { 
   386→        user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id, 
   387→        error: userError?.message 
   388→      });
   389→      await logger.flush();
   390→      return jsonResponse({ error: 'User not found for credit calculation' }, 400);
   391→    }
   392→
   393→    // Insert cost into credit ledger
   394→    const { error: ledgerError } = await supabaseAdmin.from('credits_ledger').insert({
   395→      user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id,
   396→      task_id: task.id,
   397→      amount: -cost,
   398→      type: 'spend',
   399→      metadata: {
   400→        task_type: task.task_type,
   401→        billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   402→        duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   403→        base_cost_per_second: taskType.base_cost_per_second,
   404→        unit_cost: taskType.unit_cost,
   405→        cost_factors: taskType.cost_factors,
   406→        task_params: task.params,
   407→        calculated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   408→        task_type_id: taskType.id,
   409→        // Include breakdown for compound pricing (e.g., video_enhance)
   410→        ...(costBreakdown ? { cost_breakdown: costBreakdown } : {})
   411→      }
   412→    });
   413→
   414→    if (ledgerError) {
   415→      logger.error("Failed to insert into credit ledger", { 
   416→        error: ledgerError.message,
   417→        user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id,
   418→        cost
   419→      });
   420→      await logger.flush();
   421→      return jsonResponse({ error: `Failed to record cost in ledger: ${ledgerError.message}` }, 500);
   422→    }
   423→
   424→    logger.info("Cost calculated and recorded", {
   425→      cost,
   426→      billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   427→      duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   428→      user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id,
   429→      ...(costBreakdown ? { breakdown: costBreakdown } : {})
   430→    });
   431→    await logger.flush();
   432→
   433→    return jsonResponse({
   434→      success: true,
   435→      cost: cost,
   436→      billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   437→      duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   438→      base_cost_per_second: taskType.base_cost_per_second,
   439→      unit_cost: taskType.unit_cost,
   440→      cost_factors: taskType.cost_factors,
   441→      task_type: task.task_type,
   442→      task_id: task.id,
   443→      // Include breakdown for compound pricing (e.g., video_enhance)
   444→      ...(costBreakdown ? { cost_breakdown: costBreakdown } : {})
   445→    });
   446→
   447→  } catch (error: any) {
   448→    logger.critical("Unexpected error", { error: error?.message, stack: error?.stack?.substring(0, 500) });
   449→    await logger.flush();
   450→    return jsonResponse({ error: error?.message || 'Unknown error occurred' }, 500);
   451→  }
   452→});
```

```
// deno-lint-ignore-file
import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.224.0/http/server.ts";
import { createClient } from "https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.39.7";
import { authenticateRequest } from "../_shared/auth.ts";
import { SystemLogger } from "../_shared/systemLogger.ts";

// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
declare const Deno: any;

/**
 * Edge function: update-task-status
 * 
 * Updates a task's status and optionally sets output_location.
 * - Service-role key: can update any task across all users
 * - User token: can only update tasks for that specific user's projects
 * 
 * POST /functions/v1/update-task-status
 * Headers: Authorization: Bearer <JWT or PAT>
 * Body: {
 *   "task_id": "uuid-string",
 *   "status": "Queued" | "In Progress" | "Failed" | "Complete" | "Cancelled",
 *   "output_location": "optional-string",
 *   "attempts": "optional-number (for tracking retry count)",
 *   "error_details": "optional-string (stores last error message)",
 *   "clear_worker": "optional-boolean (when true, clears worker_id and generation_started_at for requeue)"
 * }
 * 
 * Returns:
 * - 200 OK with success message
 * - 400 Bad Request if missing required fields
 * - 401 Unauthorized if no valid token
 * - 403 Forbidden if token invalid or user not found
 * - 404 Not Found if task doesn't exist or user can't access it
 * - 500 Internal Server Error
 */

/**
 * Trigger cost calculation for an orchestrator task.
 * Used when an orchestrator is cancelled to bill for completed work.
 */
async function triggerOrchestratorBilling(
  supabaseUrl: string,
  serviceKey: string,
  orchestratorTaskId: string,
  logger: SystemLogger
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    logger.info("Triggering billing for cancelled orchestrator", { 
      orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId 
    });
    
    const costResp = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/functions/v1/calculate-task-cost`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Authorization": `Bearer ${serviceKey}`,
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ task_id: orchestratorTaskId })
    });

    if (costResp.ok) {
      const costData = await costResp.json();
      if (costData.skipped) {
        logger.debug("Cost calculation skipped", { reason: costData.reason });
      } else if (typeof costData.cost === 'number') {
        logger.info("Cost calculated for cancelled orchestrator", { 
          cost: costData.cost,
          duration_seconds: costData.duration_seconds
        });
      }
    } else {
      const errTxt = await costResp.text();
      logger.error("Cost calculation failed", { error: errTxt });
    }
  } catch (err: any) {
    logger.error("Error triggering billing", { error: err?.message });
  }
}

/**
 * Handles billing for cancelled orchestrator tasks.
 * When an orchestrator is cancelled, we should still bill for any completed segments.
 */
async function handleOrchestratorCancellationBilling(
  supabaseAdmin: any,
  supabaseUrl: string,
  serviceKey: string,
  logger: SystemLogger,
  cancelledTaskId: string,
  cancelledTaskData: any
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    // Check if this is an orchestrator task (has orchestrator_details but no orchestrator reference to another task)
    if (!cancelledTaskData.params) {
      return;
    }
    
    const params = typeof cancelledTaskData.params === 'string' 
      ? JSON.parse(cancelledTaskData.params) 
      : cancelledTaskData.params;
    
    // Check if this task references another orchestrator (meaning it's a child, not an orchestrator)
    const orchestratorRef = params.orchestrator_task_id_ref || 
                            params.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
                            params.originalParams?.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
                            params.orchestrator_task_id;
    
    // Validate if orchestratorRef is a UUID (child tasks have UUID refs, orchestrators have human-readable IDs)
    const uuidRegex = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
    const isChildTask = orchestratorRef && uuidRegex.test(orchestratorRef) && orchestratorRef !== cancelledTaskId;
    
    if (isChildTask) {
      // This is a child task - billing will be handled by the orchestrator
      logger.debug("Cancelled task is a child, skipping billing", { 
        task_id: cancelledTaskId,
        orchestrator_ref: orchestratorRef 
      });
      return;
    }
    
    // Check if this task has orchestrator_details (indicating it IS an orchestrator)
    if (!params.orchestrator_details) {
      logger.debug("Cancelled task is not an orchestrator, skipping billing", { 
        task_id: cancelledTaskId 
      });
      return;
    }
    
    logger.info("Cancelled task is an orchestrator, checking for completed work", { 
      task_id: cancelledTaskId 
    });
    
    // Check if there are any completed child segments
    // Query for segments that reference this orchestrator
    const { data: completedSegments, error: segmentsError } = await supabaseAdmin
      .from('tasks')
      .select('id, generation_started_at, generation_processed_at')
      .or(`params->>orchestrator_task_id_ref.eq.${cancelledTaskId},params->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${cancelledTaskId},params->originalParams->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${cancelledTaskId},params->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${cancelledTaskId}`)
      .eq('status', 'Complete');
    
    if (segmentsError) {
      logger.error("Error checking for completed segments", { error: segmentsError.message });
      return;
    }
    
    if (!completedSegments || completedSegments.length === 0) {
      logger.info("No completed segments found, no billing needed", { 
        task_id: cancelledTaskId 
      });
      return;
    }
    
    logger.info("Found completed segments for cancelled orchestrator", { 
      task_id: cancelledTaskId,
      completed_segment_count: completedSegments.length
    });
    
    // Set timestamps on the orchestrator so cost calculation can work
    // Use the earliest start time from segments and current time as processed time
    let earliestStartTime: string | null = null;
    for (const segment of completedSegments) {
      if (segment.generation_started_at) {
        if (!earliestStartTime || segment.generation_started_at < earliestStartTime) {
          earliestStartTime = segment.generation_started_at;
        }
      }
    }
    
    if (earliestStartTime) {
      // Update orchestrator with timestamps so cost calculation can proceed
      await supabaseAdmin
        .from('tasks')
        .update({
          generation_started_at: earliestStartTime,
          generation_processed_at: new Date().toISOString()
        })
        .eq('id', cancelledTaskId);
    }
    
    // Trigger cost calculation for the orchestrator
    await triggerOrchestratorBilling(supabaseUrl, serviceKey, cancelledTaskId, logger);
    
  } catch (error: any) {
    logger.error("Error in orchestrator cancellation billing", { error: error?.message });
  }
}

/**
 * Handles cascading task failures/cancellations for orchestrated tasks.
 * When a task fails or is cancelled, this function:
 * 1. Finds the orchestrator task (if the failed task references one)
 * 2. Finds all sibling tasks that reference the same orchestrator
 * 3. Marks them all as Failed/Cancelled appropriately
 */
async function handleCascadingTaskFailure(
  supabaseAdmin: any,
  logger: SystemLogger,
  failedTaskId: string,
  failureStatus: string,
  failedTaskData: any
) {
  try {
    logger.info("Processing cascading failure", { 
      task_id: failedTaskId, 
      status: failureStatus 
    });
    
    // Extract orchestrator reference from the failed task's params
    // Must check all possible paths where orchestrator_task_id might be stored
    let orchestratorTaskId: string | null = null;
    let isOrchestratorTask = false;
    
    if (failedTaskData.params) {
      const params = typeof failedTaskData.params === 'string' 
        ? JSON.parse(failedTaskData.params) 
        : failedTaskData.params;
      
      // Check all paths (matching extractOrchestratorTaskId in complete_task)
      orchestratorTaskId = params.orchestrator_task_id_ref || 
                           params.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
                           params.originalParams?.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
                           params.orchestrator_task_id;
      
      // Check if this task IS the orchestrator (has orchestrator_details but no orchestrator reference)
      if (!orchestratorTaskId && params.orchestrator_details) {
        orchestratorTaskId = failedTaskId;
        isOrchestratorTask = true;
        logger.debug("Task is the orchestrator itself", { task_id: failedTaskId });
      }
    }
    
    if (!orchestratorTaskId) {
      logger.debug("No orchestrator reference found, skipping cascade", { task_id: failedTaskId });
      return;
    }
    
    logger.info("Found orchestrator task", { 
      orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
      is_orchestrator_task: isOrchestratorTask
    });
    
    // Find all tasks that reference this orchestrator (including the orchestrator itself)
    // Must check all paths where orchestrator reference might be stored
    let query;
    
    if (isOrchestratorTask) {
      // If the failed task IS the orchestrator, find all children that reference it
      query = supabaseAdmin
        .from("tasks")
        .select("id, task_type, status, params")
        .or(`params->>orchestrator_task_id_ref.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->originalParams->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId}`)
        .neq("id", failedTaskId)
        .neq("status", "Failed")
        .neq("status", "Cancelled")
        .neq("status", "Complete");
    } else {
      // If a child task failed, find orchestrator + all siblings
      query = supabaseAdmin
        .from("tasks")
        .select("id, task_type, status, params")
        .or(`id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->>orchestrator_task_id_ref.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->originalParams->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},params->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId}`)
        .neq("status", "Failed")
        .neq("status", "Cancelled")
        .neq("status", "Complete");
    }
    
    const { data: relatedTasks, error: fetchError } = await query;
    
    if (fetchError) {
      logger.error("Error fetching related tasks for cascade", { error: fetchError.message });
      return;
    }
    
    if (!relatedTasks || relatedTasks.length === 0) {
      logger.debug("No related tasks found for cascade");
      return;
    }
    
    // Update all related tasks to Failed/Cancelled
    const tasksToUpdate = relatedTasks.filter((task: any) => task.id !== failedTaskId);
    
    if (tasksToUpdate.length === 0) {
      logger.debug("No additional tasks to cascade to after filtering");
      return;
    }
    
    logger.info("Cascading failure to related tasks", {
      task_id: failedTaskId,
      related_task_count: tasksToUpdate.length,
      related_task_ids: tasksToUpdate.map((t: any) => t.id.substring(0, 8))
    });
    
    const updatePromises = tasksToUpdate.map(async (task: any) => {
      const updatePayload = {
        status: failureStatus,
        updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
        error_message: `Cascaded ${failureStatus.toLowerCase()} from related task ${failedTaskId}`
      };
      
      const { error } = await supabaseAdmin
        .from("tasks")
        .update(updatePayload)
        .eq("id", task.id);
      
      if (error) {
        logger.error("Failed to cascade to task", { 
          cascaded_task_id: task.id, 
          error: error.message 
        });
      }
      
      return { taskId: task.id, error };
    });
    
    const results = await Promise.all(updatePromises);
    const failedUpdates = results.filter(r => r.error);
    
    if (failedUpdates.length > 0) {
      logger.warn("Some cascade updates failed", { 
        failed_count: failedUpdates.length,
        total_count: tasksToUpdate.length
      });
    } else {
      logger.info("Cascade complete", { 
        cascaded_count: tasksToUpdate.length,
        status: failureStatus
      });
    }
    
  } catch (error: any) {
    logger.error("Unexpected error in cascade handler", { error: error?.message });
  }
}

serve(async (req) => {
  const serviceKey = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY");
  const supabaseUrl = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL");

  if (!serviceKey || !supabaseUrl) {
    console.error("[UPDATE-TASK-STATUS] Missing required environment variables");
    return new Response("Server configuration error", { status: 500 });
  }

  // Create admin client for database operations
  const supabaseAdmin = createClient(supabaseUrl, serviceKey);

  // Create logger (task_id will be set after parsing body)
  const logger = new SystemLogger(supabaseAdmin, 'update-task-status');

  // Only accept POST requests
  if (req.method !== "POST") {
    logger.warn("Method not allowed", { method: req.method });
    await logger.flush();
    return new Response("Method not allowed", { status: 405 });
  }

  // Parse request body
  let requestBody: any = {};
  try {
    const bodyText = await req.text();
    if (bodyText) {
      requestBody = JSON.parse(bodyText);
    }
  } catch (e) {
    logger.error("Invalid JSON body");
    await logger.flush();
    return new Response("Invalid JSON body", { status: 400 });
  }

  // Validate required fields
  const { 
    task_id, 
    status, 
    output_location,
    // Support for task retry/requeue
    attempts,
    error_details,
    clear_worker 
  } = requestBody;

  // Set task_id for all subsequent logs
  if (task_id) {
    logger.setDefaultTaskId(task_id);
  }

  if (!task_id || !status) {
    logger.error("Missing required fields", { has_task_id: !!task_id, has_status: !!status });
    await logger.flush();
    return new Response("Missing required fields: task_id and status", { status: 400 });
  }

  // Validate status values
  const validStatuses = ["Queued", "In Progress", "Complete", "Failed", "Cancelled"];
  if (!validStatuses.includes(status)) {
    logger.error("Invalid status value", { status, valid_statuses: validStatuses });
    await logger.flush();
    return new Response(`Invalid status. Must be one of: ${validStatuses.join(", ")}`, { status: 400 });
  }

  logger.info("Processing status update", { task_id, status });

  // Authenticate using shared auth module
  const auth = await authenticateRequest(req, supabaseAdmin, "[UPDATE-TASK-STATUS]");

  if (!auth.success) {
    logger.error("Authentication failed", { error: auth.error });
    await logger.flush();
    return new Response(auth.error || "Authentication failed", { status: auth.statusCode || 403 });
  }

  const isServiceRole = auth.isServiceRole;
  const callerId = auth.userId;

  try {
    // SAFETY CHECK: Prevent overwriting Complete tasks with terminal statuses
    const { data: currentTask, error: currentTaskError } = await supabaseAdmin
      .from("tasks")
      .select("status")
      .eq("id", task_id)
      .single();

    if (currentTaskError) {
      logger.error("Error checking current task status", { error: currentTaskError.message });
      await logger.flush();
      return new Response(`Failed to check current task status: ${currentTaskError.message}`, { status: 500 });
    }

    // Don't overwrite Complete tasks with terminal statuses
    if (currentTask?.status === "Complete" && (status === "Failed" || status === "Cancelled")) {
      logger.warn("Refusing to update completed task to a terminal status", { 
        task_id, 
        current_status: currentTask.status 
      });
      await logger.flush();
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({
        success: false,
        task_id: task_id,
        current_status: currentTask.status,
        requested_status: status,
        message: "Cannot update a completed task to Failed/Cancelled"
      }), {
        status: 400,
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
      });
    }

    // Don't overwrite Cancelled tasks - once cancelled, status should not change
    // This prevents workers from "uncancelling" tasks by continuing to update status
    if (currentTask?.status === "Cancelled") {
      logger.warn("Refusing to update cancelled task", { 
        task_id, 
        current_status: currentTask.status,
        requested_status: status
      });
      await logger.flush();
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({
        success: false,
        task_id: task_id,
        current_status: currentTask.status,
        requested_status: status,
        message: "Cannot update cancelled task"
      }), {
        status: 400,
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
      });
    }

    // Build update payload
    const updatePayload: any = {
      status: status,
      updated_at: new Date().toISOString()
    };

    if (status === "In Progress") {
      updatePayload.generation_started_at = new Date().toISOString();
    }

    // Reset generation_started_at when explicitly requested (after model loading)
    // This allows billing to start from when actual work begins, not when task was claimed
    if (requestBody.reset_generation_started_at === true) {
      updatePayload.generation_started_at = new Date().toISOString();
    }
    
    if (status === "Complete") {
      updatePayload.generation_processed_at = new Date().toISOString();
    }

    // Handle output_location for Failed/Complete statuses
    if (output_location !== undefined) {
      updatePayload.output_location = output_location;
    }

    // Handle retry-related fields
    if (attempts !== undefined) {
      updatePayload.attempts = attempts;
    }

    if (error_details !== undefined) {
      updatePayload.error_message = error_details;
    }
```

## Over-Engineering Audit Results

### 1. `useMobileTimeoutFallback` hook
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useMobileTimeoutFallback.ts`

**Consumers:** 2 -- `UserSettingsContext.tsx` and `useProjectDefaults.ts`

**Verdict: GOOD**

This is 50 lines including the interface, JSDoc, and the ref-stability pattern. It replaces inline `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` + `isMobileUA()` boilerplate that would otherwise be duplicated in two contexts. The hook does one thing, the API is minimal (isLoading + onTimeout + optional timeouts + enabled), and the `onTimeoutRef` pattern correctly avoids stale closure bugs. Two consumers is enough to justify extraction -- the alternative is two copies of the same timer/cleanup/ref logic. No issues.

### 2. `createPaneLockSetter` factory in PanesContext
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/contexts/PanesContext.tsx`

**Consumers:** Internal only -- creates 3 setters (gens, shots, tasks) at lines 143-145.

**Verdict: GOOD**

The factory (lines 115-141) replaces three nearly-identical functions that each needed: (a) check for no-op, (b) exclusive mobile locking, (c) conditional persistence, (d) tasks pane sync. That is real logic with real branching. Having three copies would mean three places to update if the locking rules change. The factory is parameterized by a single key and returns a setter -- straightforward. The `useMemo` wrapping at lines 143-145 is correct (stable references per key). Clean extraction.

### 3. PaymentSuccessPage state machine
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/pages/PaymentSuccessPage.tsx`

**Verdict: GOOD, borderline unnecessary formalism but net positive**

The "state machine" is really just a `useState<PaymentState>` with 4 states and 2 timers. There is no reducer, no transition table, no external library. The type comment at lines 9-17 documents the transitions, and the actual code uses `setState(prev => prev === 'polling' ? 'verified' : prev)` guards to prevent invalid transitions. This is the right amount of structure for what it does: loading spinner for 1.5s minimum, then success, with a 30s hard timeout. The previous code (if it existed) would have needed the same timers and guards, just with less clarity about what states are possible. 203 lines for a full page with three visual states (error, loading, success) is fine.

### 4. Shared billing module
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/_shared/billing.ts`

**Consumers:** 3 edge functions -- `complete_task`, `update-task-status`, `calculate-task-cost`. Plus a local `complete_task/billing.ts` wrapper.

**Verdict: GOOD**

The shared module extracts exactly the right things:
- `extractOrchestratorRef` (4 param paths to check -- real complexity that was duplicated)
- `getSubTaskOrchestratorId` (UUID validation + self-reference guard)
- `buildSubTaskFilter` (4-path PostgREST filter string)
- `triggerCostCalculation` (fire-and-forget HTTP with logging)

These are pure functions with no shared state. The `complete_task/billing.ts` wrapper adds one function (`triggerCostCalculationIfNotSubTask`) that combines a DB query with the shared logic -- appropriate for a function-specific helper. No coupling problems.

### 5. AuthGate component
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/AuthGate.tsx`

**Consumer:** 1 -- `App.tsx` line 246.

**Verdict: GOOD**

6 lines. Reads `isLoading` from `useAuth()`, returns null while loading, renders children after. This is exactly the right abstraction: it names the intent ("gate data providers until auth is resolved") and keeps App.tsx from needing inline conditionals. Minimal as it gets.

### 6. ProjectContext decomposition
**Files:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/contexts/ProjectContext.tsx` (thin provider, 128 lines)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectSelection.ts` (150 lines)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectCRUD.ts` (327 lines)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectDefaults.ts` (65 lines)

**Verdict: OVER-ENGINEERED -- mild**

The decomposition itself is reasonable in principle. The original context was presumably 500+ lines doing selection, CRUD, and side-effects. Splitting into three hooks is defensible. However, there are concrete problems:

**Problem 1: Circular dependency between hooks.** `useProjectSelection` imports `determineProjectIdToSelect` from `useProjectCRUD` (line 6). Two hooks that extract from the same context should not depend on each other. `determineProjectIdToSelect` is a pure helper function; it should live in a shared utility or in the context file itself.

**Problem 2: Callback ceremony.** The three hooks communicate through a 7-prop options interface (`useProjectDefaults`) and callback props (`onProjectsLoaded`, `onProjectCreated`, `onProjectDeleted`). The thin provider at lines 38-63 is doing what a single hook body could do -- wiring three sub-hooks together via callbacks. This is the "thin shell" anti-pattern where the decomposition creates more wiring code than it saves in readability.

**Problem 3: `useProjectDefaults` is a bag of side-effects.** It triggers fetches, applies cross-device sync, prefetches tool settings, and runs a mobile timeout fallback. These are 4 unrelated concerns grouped by "they are effects related to projects." The hook name "defaults" does not describe what it does.

**Suggested simplification:** Move `determineProjectIdToSelect` to a shared util. Consider merging `useProjectDefaults` back into the provider (it is only 65 lines and its only consumer is the provider). That leaves a clean two-hook split: selection logic and CRUD logic, composed in the provider.

### 7. `useDeviceInfo()` composite hook
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/use-mobile.tsx`

**Consumers of `useDeviceInfo`:** 3 -- `useLayoutMode.ts`, `ShotEditor/index.tsx`, `SharedGenerationView.tsx`

**Verdict: OVER-ENGINEERED**

**Problem 1: Redundant event listeners.** `useDeviceInfo` calls `useIsMobile()` and `useIsTablet()` internally, which each set up their own resize/matchMedia listeners. Then `useDeviceInfo` adds *another* resize listener (line 219) for `isTabletOrLarger` and `isPortraitMode`. That is 3 resize event listeners per component that uses `useDeviceInfo`. The compute functions (`computeIsMobile`, `computeIsTablet`, etc.) also repeat the same iPad/tablet UA detection logic 3+ times with slightly different formulations.

**Problem 2: `isTouchDevice` is computed wrong in the composite.** At line 198-201, `isTouchDevice` is a `useMemo` that depends on `isMobile` -- but `computeIsTouchDevice()` reads from `window` directly. So it recomputes when `isMobile` changes, but not when the actual touch capability changes (which it never will mid-session anyway). Meanwhile, `useIsTouchDevice()` (the standalone hook) adds a resize listener. These are two different behaviors for the same concept.

**Problem 3: Exports nobody uses.** `useIsPhone()` has zero external consumers. `useIsTouchDevice()` has 1 consumer. These were added speculatively.

**Problem 4: Consumers don't need the composite.** Looking at actual usage:
- `useLayoutMode.ts` uses `isTabletOrLarger`, `isPortraitMode`, `isTouchDevice` -- could use individual hooks or inline checks
- `ShotEditor` uses `isPhone`, `mobileColumns` -- already calls `useIsMobile()` separately on the same line
- `SharedGenerationView` uses only `mobileColumns` -- already calls `useIsMobile()` separately

The `mobileColumns` computation is the only thing the composite actually provides that the individual hooks don't. That could be a 5-line `useMobileColumns()` hook instead of a 60-line god hook.

**Suggested simplification:** Delete `useDeviceInfo`, `useIsPhone`, and the standalone `useIsTouchDevice` (1 consumer can inline it). Extract `useMobileColumns(isMobile, isTablet, orientation)` if needed. Keep the individual hooks (`useIsMobile`, `useIsTablet`) that have real consumers. Deduplicate the iPad detection logic in the compute functions.

## Behavioral Regression Audit Report

### 1. Task Status Transition Guards (`update-task-status/index.ts`)

**Verdict: RISK -- Minor behavioral tightening, intentional but worth noting**

The refactoring replaced two ad-hoc guards with a comprehensive `validTransitions` lookup table. Here is what changed:

**Old code** had exactly two guards:
- `Complete -> Failed` or `Complete -> Cancelled`: blocked (400)
- `Cancelled -> *anything*`: blocked (400)

Everything else was allowed, including:
- `Failed -> Queued` (allowed -- no guard)
- `Failed -> In Progress` (allowed -- no guard)
- `Failed -> Cancelled` (allowed -- no guard)
- `Complete -> In Progress` (allowed -- no guard)
- `Complete -> Queued` (allowed -- no guard)

**New code** locks down all terminal states:
```
Queued      -> [In Progress, Failed, Cancelled]
In Progress -> [Complete, Failed, Cancelled, Queued]
Complete    -> []      (no transitions)
Failed      -> []      (no transitions)
Cancelled   -> []      (no transitions)
```

**Newly blocked transitions**:
- `Failed -> *anything*`: Previously allowed (a worker could theoretically update a Failed task to Queued or In Progress). Now blocked. The comment says "retries create NEW tasks" which is the intended pattern, confirmed by the `func_reset_orphaned_tasks` migration that resets stuck In Progress tasks back to Queued (not Failed ones). **This is intentional and correct.**
- `Complete -> Queued` / `Complete -> In Progress`: Previously allowed (nonsensical but possible). Now blocked. **Correct.**
- `Queued -> Complete`: Previously allowed (skip straight to complete). Now blocked. This should never happen in practice since tasks go through In Progress first, but it is technically a behavioral change. **Very low risk -- no legitimate use case.**

**Key positive**: `In Progress -> Queued` is correctly allowed for requeue scenarios. The `clear_worker` flag still works as expected.

**Status code change**: Invalid transitions now return 409 (Conflict) instead of 400 (Bad Request). This is a better HTTP semantic but could theoretically affect client error handling if clients match on status code 400 specifically. **Low risk**.

**Overall**: This is a **tightening** of the state machine that removes previously-open loopholes. All legitimate transitions are preserved. The only potential issue is if some external system was relying on `Failed -> *` being allowed, but the codebase design says retries create new tasks, so this is correct.

---

### 2. Rate Limiting Change (`ai-prompt/index.ts`)

**Verdict: SAFE**

The code flow at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/ai-prompt/index.ts` (lines 36-71):

1. **Auth header check** (line 47): Missing `Bearer` token returns 401 immediately
2. **JWT verification** (line 55): `supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser(token)` -- if auth fails, returns 401 immediately (line 58)
3. **Rate limit** (line 62): Only reached after successful auth, uses `user.id`

The order is correct: authentication happens before rate limiting. Unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401 before any rate limit check occurs. This means:
- Unauthenticated requests do **not** consume rate limit budget
- Rate limiting is now per-user instead of per-IP, which is a deliberate improvement (prevents shared-IP rate limit collisions; also means a single user can't evade limits by rotating IPs)

Note: `ai-prompt` does **not** use the shared `authenticateRequest()` module. It uses its own inline JWT verification via `supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser()`. This is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase but is not a regression since this function was not part of the auth standardization wave (it uses Supabase's native JWT verification which is actually more secure than the manual JWT decode in `authenticateRequest`).

---

### 3. Auth Standardization

**Verdict: SAFE**

I examined multiple functions that were migrated to `authenticateRequest()`:

**`claim-next-task/index.ts`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/claim-next-task/index.ts`):
- Auth at line 81, before any DB work -- correct placement
- Error response uses `auth.statusCode || 403` -- matches expected behavior
- `auth.isServiceRole` and `auth.userId` properly used downstream

**`create-task/index.ts`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/create-task/index.ts`):
- Auth at line 120 with `{ allowJwtUserAuth: true }` -- enables frontend JWT auth
- Properly separates service-role vs user-token paths
- Rate limiting correctly skipped for service role (line 140)

**`get-task-status/index.ts`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/get-task-status/index.ts`):
- Auth at line 55, after body parsing but before DB queries -- correct
- Error handling delegates to `auth.statusCode` -- correct

**`generate-upload-url/index.ts`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/generate-upload-url/index.ts`):
- Auth at line 84, uses both `verifyTaskOwnership` and `getTaskUserId` helpers from shared auth module -- clean delegation

**`authenticateRequest()` itself** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts`):
- Checks in order: (1) service-role key exact match, (2) JWT decode (optional), (3) PAT lookup
- Returns appropriate status codes: 401 for missing header, 500 for config issues, 403 for invalid token
- Importantly: JWT user auth is **opt-in** via `allowJwtUserAuth` flag, so functions that only expect PAT/service-key won't accidentally accept JWTs
- **Security note**: The JWT decode at line 90-106 only decodes the payload without cryptographic verification (`atob` of the payload section). This is acceptable because: (a) service_role/supabase_admin claims are explicitly rejected, and (b) Supabase's gateway already validates JWTs before they reach edge functions. But it's worth noting that this is a weaker verification than `supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser(token)`.

**One subtlety**: The old inline auth patterns typically returned 401 for both missing and invalid tokens. The shared module returns 401 for missing headers but 403 for invalid tokens (failed PAT lookup). This is actually more semantically correct (401 = "who are you?" vs 403 = "I know who you are and you don't have access"), but could theoretically affect clients that rely on specific status codes. **Very low risk**.

### 4. ProjectContext Decomposition

**Verdict: SAFE**

The `ProjectContext` (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/contexts/ProjectContext.tsx`) was decomposed into three hooks:

- **`useProjectSelection`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectSelection.ts`): Manages `selectedProjectId`, localStorage fast-resume, cross-device sync
- **`useProjectCRUD`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectCRUD.ts`): Manages projects list, fetch, create, update, delete
- **`useProjectDefaults`** (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectDefaults.ts`): Side effects -- fetch trigger, cross-device sync, prefetch, mobile fallback

**Context shape verification** -- The `ProjectContextType` interface at line 15-29 exposes:
- `projects`, `selectedProjectId`, `setSelectedProjectId`, `isLoadingProjects`, `fetchProjects`
- `addNewProject`, `isCreatingProject`, `updateProject`, `isUpdatingProject`
- `deleteProject`, `isDeletingProject`, `userId`

All 46 consumers use `useProject()` which returns this exact shape. The shape has not changed.

**Project selection persistence**: `handleSetSelectedProjectId` (line 86 of `useProjectSelection.ts`) still writes to both `localStorage` and server preferences (`updateUserSettings`). Fast resume from localStorage is preserved. Cross-device sync is preserved.

**One subtle concern in the decomposition**: In `useProjectCRUD.ts` line 300-303, `deleteProject` calls `onProjectDeleted(updated)` inside a `setProjects` updater function. This means the parent's `handleProjectDeleted` callback runs synchronously during a React state update, which can work but is a React anti-pattern (calling external callbacks during state updates). However, this pattern was likely present in the original monolithic component too, and React batches updates, so in practice this works fine. **Not a regression**.

### 5. Billing Extraction

**Verdict: SAFE**

The shared billing module (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/_shared/billing.ts`) extracts three key functions:

**`extractOrchestratorRef(params)`** (line 31-41): Checks all 4 param paths:
1. `params.orchestrator_task_id_ref` -- travel_segment
2. `params.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id` -- join_clips_segment
3. `params.originalParams?.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id` -- legacy
4. `params.orchestrator_task_id` -- some legacy tasks

**Verified against old inline code**: The old `handleOrchestratorCancellationBilling` (from the pre-refactor version) had the same 4 paths in the same order:
```typescript
const orchestratorRef = params.orchestrator_task_id_ref || 
                        params.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
                        params.originalParams?.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
                        params.orchestrator_task_id;
```
This is an exact match with `extractOrchestratorRef`.

**`getSubTaskOrchestratorId(params, taskId)`** (line 56-62): Wraps `extractOrchestratorRef` with two additional guards:
1. UUID validation (`UUID_REGEX.test(ref)`) -- prevents human-readable IDs from being treated as orchestrator refs
2. Self-reference guard (`ref === taskId`) -- prevents orchestrators from being identified as their own sub-tasks

Both guards were present inline in the old code (UUID regex check and `orchestratorRef !== cancelledTaskId`). **Exact behavioral match**.

**`buildSubTaskFilter(orchestratorTaskId)`** (line 75-82): Generates the PostgREST `.or()` filter string for all 4 param paths. The old code had this same filter inlined in multiple places (the `.or(...)` call in `handleOrchestratorCancellationBilling` and `handleCascadingTaskFailure`). **Exact match**.

**Consumers verified**:
- `calculate-task-cost/index.ts` (line 209): Uses `getSubTaskOrchestratorId` to skip billing for sub-tasks, and `buildSubTaskFilter` to find sub-tasks of orchestrators
- `update-task-status/index.ts` (line 63): Uses `getSubTaskOrchestratorId` in cancellation billing; uses `extractOrchestratorRef` in cascade handler; uses `buildSubTaskFilter` for queries
- `complete_task/billing.ts` (line 37): Re-exports and wraps `getSubTaskOrchestratorId` + `triggerCostCalculation`

The extraction is a clean refactor with no behavioral change.

## What to specifically look for

```
   314→    } catch (orchErr) {
   315→      console.error("[COMPLETE-TASK] Error checking orchestrator completion:", orchErr);

   319→    if (isServiceRole) {

   322→
   323→    // 15) Return success
   324→    console.log(`[COMPLETE-TASK] Successfully completed task ${taskIdString}`);
   325→    const responseData = {

   328→      thumbnail_url: thumbnailUrl,
   329→      message: "Task completed and file uploaded successfully"

   332→    logger.info("Task completed successfully", {

   334→      output_location: publicUrl,
   335→      has_thumbnail: !!thumbnailUrl
   336→    });
   337→    await logger.flush();
   338→
   339→    return new Response(JSON.stringify(responseData), {
   340→      status: 200,
   341→      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
   342→    });
   343→
   344→  } catch (error: any) {
   345→    logger.critical("Unexpected error", { 
   346→      task_id: taskIdString, 
   347→      error: error?.message,
   348→      stack: error?.stack?.substring(0, 500)
   349→    });
   350→    console.error("[COMPLETE-TASK] Edge function error:", error);
   351→    await logger.flush();
   352→    return new Response(`Internal error: ${error?.message}`, { status: 500 });
   353→  }
   354→}

   356→// Some TS envs don't know about import.meta.main; Deno does.
   357→if ((import.meta as any).main) {
   358→  serve((req) => completeTaskHandler(req));
   359→}

   361→
```

1. **"Missing required environment variables"** -- these happen BEFORE the supabase client/logger can be created (since the env vars are needed to create the client). These must stay as `console.error` since there's no logger available yet.

```
   248→  if (projectError || !projectData) {
   249→    console.error(`${logPrefix} Project lookup error:`, projectError);
   250→    return {
   251→      success: false,
   252→      error: "Project not found",
   253→      statusCode: 404
   254→    };
   255→  }
   256→
   257→  if (projectData.user_id !== userId) {
   258→    console.error(`${logPrefix} Shot ${shotId} belongs to project ${shotData.project_id} owned by ${projectData.user_id}, not user ${userId}`);
   259→    return {
   260→      success: false,
   261→      error: "Forbidden: Shot does not belong to user",
   262→      statusCode: 403
   263→    };
   264→  }
   265→
   266→  console.log(`${logPrefix} Shot ${shotId} ownership verified: user ${userId} owns project ${shotData.project_id}`);
   267→  return {
   268→    success: true,
   269→    projectId: shotData.project_id
   270→  };
   271→}
   272→
   273→/**
   274→ * Gets the user ID for a task (for service role requests)
   275→ * 
   276→ * @param supabaseAdmin - Supabase admin client
   277→ * @param taskId - Task ID
   278→ * @param logPrefix - Optional prefix for log messages
   279→ * @returns Object with userId or error
   280→ */
   281→export async function getTaskUserId(
   282→  supabaseAdmin: any,
   283→  taskId: string,
   284→  logPrefix: string = "[AUTH]"
   285→): Promise<{ userId: string | null; error?: string; statusCode?: number }> {
   286→  console.log(`${logPrefix} Looking up user for task ${taskId}`);
   287→
   288→  const { data: taskData, error: taskError } = await supabaseAdmin
   289→    .from("tasks")
   290→    .select("project_id")
   291→    .eq("id", taskId)
   292→    .single();
   293→
   294→  if (taskError || !taskData) {
   295→    console.error(`${logPrefix} Task lookup error:`, taskError);
   296→    return {
   297→      userId: null,
   298→      error: "Task not found",
   299→      statusCode: 404
   300→    };
   301→  }
   302→
   303→  const { data: projectData, error: projectError } = await supabaseAdmin
   304→    .from("projects")
   305→    .select("user_id")
   306→    .eq("id", taskData.project_id)
   307→    .single();
   308→
   309→  if (projectError || !projectData) {
   310→    console.error(`${logPrefix} Project lookup error:`, projectError);
   311→    // Fallback to system folder
   312→    return {
   313→      userId: 'system'
   314→    };
   315→  }
   316→
   317→  console.log(`${logPrefix} Task ${taskId} belongs to user ${projectData.user_id}`);
   318→  return {
   319→    userId: projectData.user_id
   320→  };
   321→}
   322→
```

```
1→import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
     2→import { isMobileUA } from '@/shared/hooks/use-mobile';
     3→
     4→interface UseMobileTimeoutFallbackOptions {
     5→  /** Whether the operation is currently in a loading state */
     6→  isLoading: boolean;
     7→  /** Called when the timeout fires while still loading (e.g. retry fetch, set defaults) */
     8→  onTimeout: () => void;
     9→  /** Timeout duration on mobile devices (default: 15000ms) */
    10→  mobileTimeoutMs?: number;
    11→  /** Timeout duration on desktop (default: 10000ms) */
    12→  desktopTimeoutMs?: number;
    13→  /** Whether the fallback is enabled (default: true) */
    14→  enabled?: boolean;
    15→}
    16→
    17→/**
    18→ * Shared mobile stall recovery hook.
    19→ *
    20→ * When `isLoading` becomes true, starts a timer (longer on mobile).
    21→ * If loading hasn't finished by the time the timer fires, calls `onTimeout`.
    22→ * Timer is cleared when loading finishes or the component unmounts.
    23→ *
    24→ * Replaces inline [MobileStallFix] patterns in ProjectContext and UserSettingsContext.
    25→ */
    26→export function useMobileTimeoutFallback({
    27→  isLoading,
    28→  onTimeout,
    29→  mobileTimeoutMs = 15000,
    30→  desktopTimeoutMs = 10000,
    31→  enabled = true,
    32→}: UseMobileTimeoutFallbackOptions): void {
    33→  const onTimeoutRef = useRef(onTimeout);
    34→  onTimeoutRef.current = onTimeout;
    35→
    36→  useEffect(() => {
    37→    if (!enabled || !isLoading) return;
    38→
    39→    const isMobile = isMobileUA();
    40→    const timeoutMs = isMobile ? mobileTimeoutMs : desktopTimeoutMs;
    41→
    42→    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    43→      onTimeoutRef.current();
    44→    }, timeoutMs);
    45→
    46→    return () => {
    47→      clearTimeout(timer);
    48→    };
    49→  }, [isLoading, enabled, mobileTimeoutMs, desktopTimeoutMs]);
    50→}
    51→
```

```
   111→  // - inCloud: false, onComputer: false (explicitly disabled, used for warnings)
   112→  // Not allowed:
   113→  // - inCloud: true, onComputer: true → normalize to cloud by default
   114→  const normalizeIfGenerationMethods = (val: UISettings[K]): UISettings[K] => {
   115→    if ((key as string) !== 'generationMethods') return val;
   116→    if (!val || typeof val !== 'object') return val;
   117→    const valObj = val as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
   118→    const inCloud = Boolean(valObj.inCloud);
   119→    const onComputer = Boolean(valObj.onComputer);
   120→    if (inCloud && onComputer) {
   121→      return { inCloud: true, onComputer: false } as UISettings[K];
   122→    }
   123→    return { inCloud, onComputer } as UISettings[K];
   124→  };
   125→  const [value, setValue] = useState<UISettings[K]>(fallback);
   126→  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
   127→  const userIdRef = useRef<string>();
   128→  const debounceRef = useRef<NodeJS.Timeout>();
   129→
   130→  // Helper function to save fallback values to database (preserves all existing settings)
   131→  // This automatically backfills existing users with default values when they first load the app
   132→  // IMPORTANT: Only runs when the key is completely missing from database (undefined)
   133→  // Does NOT override explicit user choices (including both options set to false)
   134→  const saveFallbackToDatabase = async (userId: string, _currentSettings: Record<string, unknown>) => {
   135→    try {
   136→      const fallbackToSave = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(fallback);
   137→      
   138→      // Use the global queue to save - it handles merging
   139→      await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   140→        scope: 'user',
   141→        id: userId,
   142→        toolId: 'ui',
   143→        patch: { [key]: fallbackToSave },
   144→      }, undefined, 'immediate');
   145→      
   146→      // Invalidate cache so other components see the backfilled values
   147→      const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
   148→      settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   149→      setValue(fallbackToSave); // Update local state after successful save
   150→    } catch (error) {
   151→      handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.saveFallbackToDatabase', showToast: false });
   152→    }
   153→  };
   154→
   155→  // Load initial value from database
   156→  useEffect(() => {
   157→    const loadUserSettings = async () => {
   158→      try {
   159→        const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
   160→        if (!user) {
   161→          // Skip loading for unauthenticated users (e.g., on public share pages)
   162→          setIsLoading(false);
   163→          return;
   164→        }
   165→
   166→        userIdRef.current = user.id;
   167→
   168→        const { data, error } = await loadUserSettingsCached(user.id);
   169→
   170→        if (error) {
   171→          handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.loadSettings', showToast: false });
   172→          setIsLoading(false);
   173→          return;
   174→        }
   175→
   176→        const uiSettings = data?.settings?.ui;
   177→        const keyValue = uiSettings?.[key];
   178→        
   179→        if (keyValue !== undefined) {
   180→          // Key exists in database - merge with fallback to backfill any missing fields
   181→          const mergedValue = (typeof fallback === 'object' && fallback !== null)
   182→            ? ({ ...fallback, ...(keyValue as object) } as UISettings[K])
   183→            : (keyValue as UISettings[K]);
   184→
   185→          const normalizedValue = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(mergedValue);
   186→          setValue(normalizedValue);
   187→
   188→          // If any fields from the fallback are missing in the stored value OR
   189→          // normalization changed the value, backfill them in DB
   190→          if (
   191→            (typeof keyValue === 'object' && keyValue !== null &&
   192→            typeof fallback === 'object' && fallback !== null &&
   193→            Object.keys(fallback as object).some((k) => (keyValue as Record<string, unknown>)[k] === undefined)) ||
   194→            JSON.stringify(normalizedValue) !== JSON.stringify(keyValue)
   195→          ) {
   196→            // Use the global queue to save - it handles merging
   197→            updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   198→              scope: 'user',
   199→              id: user.id,
   200→              toolId: 'ui',
   201→              patch: { [key]: normalizedValue },
   202→            }, undefined, 'immediate').then(() => {
   203→              const cacheKey = `user_settings_${user.id}`;
   204→              settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   205→            }).catch(e => {
   206→              handleError(e, { context: 'useUserUIState.backfillFields', showToast: false });
   207→            });
   208→          }
   209→        } else {
   210→          // Key doesn't exist in database - this is an existing user who hasn't set preferences yet
   211→          // Save fallback values to backfill them (only runs when completely empty)
   212→          const normalizedFallback = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(fallback);
   213→          setValue(normalizedFallback); // Set normalized fallback immediately for responsive UI
   214→          
   215→          // Save to database in background (don't block loading)
   216→          saveFallbackToDatabase(user.id, data?.settings || {}).catch(error => {
   217→            handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.saveFallback', showToast: false });
   218→          });
   219→        }
   220→        
   221→        setIsLoading(false);
   222→      } catch (error) {
   223→        handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.loadUserSettings', showToast: false });
   224→        setIsLoading(false);
   225→      }
   226→    };
   227→
   228→    loadUserSettings();
   229→  }, [key]); // Remove fallback from deps to prevent unnecessary re-runs
   230→
   231→  // Debounced update function
   232→  // Uses the global settings write queue (via updateToolSettingsSupabase) to prevent
   233→  // race conditions with other hooks that write to users.settings (e.g., useToolSettings
   234→  // writing user-preferences). The write queue serializes writes and uses an atomic RPC.
   235→  const update = (patch: Partial<UISettings[K]>) => {
   236→    // Immediately update local state for responsive UI (with normalization)
   237→    const normalizedPatch = normalizeIfGenerationMethods({
   238→      ...(value as object),
   239→      ...(patch as object)
   240→    } as UISettings[K]);
   241→    setValue(normalizedPatch);
   242→
   243→    // Clear existing timeout
   244→    if (debounceRef.current) {
   245→      clearTimeout(debounceRef.current);
   246→    }
   247→
   248→    // Debounce the database write via the global settings write queue
   249→    debounceRef.current = setTimeout(async () => {
   250→      const userId = userIdRef.current;
   251→      if (!userId) return;
   252→
   253→      try {
   254→        // Use the write queue which handles atomic DB updates and merging.
   255→        // This prevents race conditions with other hooks writing to users.settings.
   256→        await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   257→          scope: 'user',
   258→          id: userId,
   259→          toolId: 'ui',
   260→          patch: { [key]: normalizedPatch },
   261→        });
   262→
   263→        // Invalidate local cache so other useUserUIState instances see the update
   264→        const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
   265→        settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   266→      } catch (error) {
   267→        handleError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.update', showToast: false });
   268→      }
   269→    }, 200);
   270→  };
   271→
   272→  // Cleanup timeout on unmount
   273→  useEffect(() => {
   274→    return () => {
   275→      if (debounceRef.current) {
   276→        clearTimeout(debounceRef.current);
   277→      }
   278→    };
   279→  }, []);
   280→
   281→  return { 
   282→    value, 
   283→    update, 
   284→    isLoading 
   285→  };
   286→}
```

```
import { useSearchParams, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';

import { Button } from '@/shared/components/ui/button';
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/shared/components/ui/card';
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';

const PaymentSuccessPage: React.FC = () => {
  const [searchParams] = useSearchParams();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const [verificationStatus, setVerificationStatus] = useState<'loading' | 'success' | 'error'>('loading');
  const [sessionDetails, setSessionDetails] = useState<{
    amount?: string;
    sessionId?: string;
  } | null>(null);

  const sessionId = searchParams.get('session_id');

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!sessionId) {
      setVerificationStatus('error');
      return;
    }

    // Set a timeout to automatically redirect if verification takes too long
    const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
      if (verificationStatus === 'loading') {
        setVerificationStatus('success');
      }
    }, 5000);

    // Invalidate credits queries to trigger a refetch
    // This will update the user's balance once the webhook processes
    const refreshCredits = () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED] });
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED] });
    };

    // Initial refresh
    refreshCredits();

    // Set up polling to check for credit updates
    const pollInterval = setInterval(refreshCredits, 2000);

    // Clean up after 30 seconds
    const cleanupTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      clearInterval(pollInterval);
      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
      setVerificationStatus('success');
    }, 30000);

    setSessionDetails({
      sessionId,
      amount: searchParams.get('amount') || undefined,
    });

    // Mark as success after a short delay to show loading state
    setTimeout(() => {
      setVerificationStatus('success');
    }, 1500);

    return () => {
      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
      clearTimeout(cleanupTimeout);
      clearInterval(pollInterval);
    };
  }, [sessionId, queryClient, searchParams, verificationStatus]);

  const handleContinue = () => {
    navigate('/tools');
  };

  const handleViewTransactions = () => {
    navigate('/tools', { state: { openSettings: true, creditsTab: 'history' } });
  };

  if (!sessionId || verificationStatus === 'error') {
    return (
      <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-gradient-to-br from-wes-cream via-white to-wes-mint/10">
        <Card className="w-full max-w-md mx-4">

  );
};

export default PaymentSuccessPage;
```

```
// deno-lint-ignore-file
// @ts-ignore
import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.224.0/http/server.ts";
// @ts-ignore
import { createClient } from "npm:@supabase/supabase-js@2";
import { authenticateRequest, verifyTaskOwnership, getTaskUserId } from "../_shared/auth.ts";
import { SystemLogger } from "../_shared/systemLogger.ts";

// Import from refactored modules
import { parseCompleteTaskRequest, validateStoragePathSecurity } from './request.ts';
import { handleStorageOperations, verifyFileExists, cleanupFile } from './storage.ts';
import { setThumbnailInParams } from './params.ts';
import { createGenerationFromTask } from './generation.ts';
import { checkOrchestratorCompletion } from './orchestrator.ts';
import { validateAndCleanupShotId } from './shotValidation.ts';
import { triggerCostCalculationIfNotSubTask } from './billing.ts';

// Provide a loose Deno type for local tooling
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
declare const Deno: any;

/**
 * Task context containing all task data needed throughout the completion flow.
 * Fetched once and passed to all functions that need it.
 * Exported for use by orchestrator.ts and other modules.
 */
export interface TaskContext {
  id: string;
  task_type: string;
  project_id: string;
  params: Record<string, any>;
  tool_type: string;
  category: string;
  content_type: 'image' | 'video';
  variant_type: string | null;
}

/**
 * Fetch task context with all required fields for the completion flow.
 * Uses a single query with FK join (tasks.task_type -> task_types.name).
 * Returns null if task not found or on error.
 */
async function fetchTaskContext(
  supabase: any,
  taskId: string
): Promise<TaskContext | null> {
  const { data: task, error } = await supabase
    .from("tasks")
    .select(`id, task_type, project_id, params, task_types!tasks_task_type_fkey(tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type)`)
    .eq("id", taskId)
    .single();

  if (error || !task) {
    console.error(`[TaskContext] Failed to fetch task ${taskId}:`, error);
    return null;
  }

  const taskTypeInfo = task.task_types || {};

  return {
    id: task.id,
    task_type: task.task_type,
    project_id: task.project_id,
    params: task.params || {},
    tool_type: taskTypeInfo.tool_type || 'unknown',
    category: taskTypeInfo.category || 'unknown',
    content_type: taskTypeInfo.content_type || 'image',
    variant_type: taskTypeInfo.variant_type || null,
  };
}

/**
 * Edge function: complete-task
 * 
 * Completes a task by uploading file data and updating task status.
 * - Service-role key: can complete any task
 * - User token: can only complete tasks they own
 * 
 * POST /functions/v1/complete-task
 * Headers: Authorization: Bearer <JWT or PAT>
 * 
 * SUPPORTS THREE UPLOAD MODES:
 * 
 * MODE 1 (LEGACY - JSON with base64): 
 *   Body: { task_id, file_data: "base64...", filename: "image.png", ... }
 * 
 * MODE 3 (PRE-SIGNED URL - Zero Memory):
 *   Body: { task_id, storage_path: "user_id/tasks/{task_id}/filename", ... }
 * 
 * MODE 4 (REFERENCE EXISTING PATH):
 *   Body: { task_id, storage_path: "user_id/filename", ... }
 */
export interface CompleteTaskDeps {
  /**
   * Override Supabase client factory for tests.
   */
  createClient?: (supabaseUrl: string, serviceKey: string) => any;
  /**
   * Provide a pre-constructed Supabase client (bypasses createClient).
   */
```

```
// deno-lint-ignore-file
// @ts-ignore
import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std@0.224.0/http/server.ts";
// @ts-ignore
import { createClient } from "npm:@supabase/supabase-js@2";
import { authenticateRequest, verifyTaskOwnership, getTaskUserId } from "../_shared/auth.ts";
import { SystemLogger } from "../_shared/systemLogger.ts";

// Import from refactored modules
import { parseCompleteTaskRequest, validateStoragePathSecurity } from './request.ts';
import { handleStorageOperations, verifyFileExists, cleanupFile } from './storage.ts';
import { setThumbnailInParams } from './params.ts';
import { createGenerationFromTask } from './generation.ts';
import { checkOrchestratorCompletion } from './orchestrator.ts';
import { validateAndCleanupShotId } from './shotValidation.ts';
import { triggerCostCalculationIfNotSubTask } from './billing.ts';

// Provide a loose Deno type for local tooling
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
declare const Deno: any;

/**
 * Task context containing all task data needed throughout the completion flow.
 * Fetched once and passed to all functions that need it.
 * Exported for use by orchestrator.ts and other modules.
 */
export interface TaskContext {
  id: string;
  task_type: string;
  project_id: string;
  params: Record<string, any>;
  tool_type: string;
  category: string;
  content_type: 'image' | 'video';
  variant_type: string | null;
}

/**
 * Fetch task context with all required fields for the completion flow.
 * Returns null if task not found or on error.
 */
async function fetchTaskContext(
  supabase: any,
  taskId: string
): Promise<TaskContext | null> {
  // Fetch task first
  const { data: task, error } = await supabase
    .from("tasks")
    .select(`id, task_type, project_id, params`)
    .eq("id", taskId)
    .single();

  if (error || !task) {
    console.error(`[TaskContext] Failed to fetch task ${taskId}:`, error);
    return null;
  }

  // Fetch task_types metadata separately (no FK relationship exists)
  let taskTypeInfo: { tool_type?: string; category?: string; content_type?: string; variant_type?: string | null } = {};
  if (task.task_type) {
    const { data: typeData } = await supabase
      .from("task_types")
      .select("tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type")
      .eq("name", task.task_type)
      .single();
    if (typeData) {
      taskTypeInfo = typeData;
    }
  }

  return {
    id: task.id,
    task_type: task.task_type,
    project_id: task.project_id,
    params: task.params || {},
    tool_type: taskTypeInfo?.tool_type || 'unknown',
    category: taskTypeInfo?.category || 'unknown',
    content_type: taskTypeInfo?.content_type || 'image',
    variant_type: taskTypeInfo?.variant_type || null,
  };
```
