```
    94→            tasks: firstLocked === 'tasks',
    95→            gens: firstLocked === 'gens',
    96→          };
    97→        }
    98→      }
    99→      setLocks(newLocks);
   100→
   101→      // IMPORTANT: Sync isTasksPaneOpen with isTasksPaneLocked on hydration
   102→      // This ensures lightboxes (which read isTasksPaneOpen from context) correctly
   103→      // account for a locked pane even after page refresh
   104→      if (newLocks.tasks) {
   105→        setIsTasksPaneOpenState(true);
   106→      }
   107→    }
   108→  }, [isLoading, paneLocks, isSmallMobile, isTablet]);
   109→
   110→
   111→  // Factory for pane lock setters — each pane follows the same logic:
   112→  // 1. On mobile/tablet + locking: unlock all OTHER panes (exclusive locking)
   113→  // 2. On small phone: skip persistence to DB
   114→  // 3. On desktop: standard toggle
   115→  const createPaneLockSetter = useCallback(
   116→    (lockKey: 'gens' | 'shots' | 'tasks') => (isLocked: boolean) => {
   117→      setLocks(prev => {
   118→        if (prev[lockKey] === isLocked) return prev;
   119→
   120→        // On mobile/tablets, unlock other panes when locking this one (only one pane can be locked at a time)
   121→        const exclusiveLock = (isMobile || isTablet) && isLocked;
   122→        return exclusiveLock
   123→          ? { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false, [lockKey]: isLocked }
   124→          : { ...prev, [lockKey]: isLocked };
   125→      });
   126→
   127→      // Save to database (desktop and tablet only, not small phones)
   128→      // Kept outside setLocks updater to avoid side effects in state updater functions
   129→      if (!isSmallMobile) {
   130→        const exclusiveLock = (isMobile || isTablet) && isLocked;
   131→        savePaneLocks(exclusiveLock
   132→          ? { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false, [lockKey]: isLocked }
   133→          : { [lockKey]: isLocked });
   134→      }
   135→
   136→      // IMPORTANT: Sync isTasksPaneOpen with isTasksPaneLocked
   137→      // This ensures lightboxes correctly account for locked pane state
   138→      if (lockKey === 'tasks' && isLocked) {
   139→        setIsTasksPaneOpenState(true);
   140→      }
   141→    },
   142→    [savePaneLocks, isSmallMobile, isMobile, isTablet]
   143→  );
   144→
   145→  const setIsGenerationsPaneLocked = useMemo(() => createPaneLockSetter('gens'), [createPaneLockSetter]);
   146→  const setIsShotsPaneLocked = useMemo(() => createPaneLockSetter('shots'), [createPaneLockSetter]);
   147→  const setIsTasksPaneLocked = useMemo(() => createPaneLockSetter('tasks'), [createPaneLockSetter]);
   148→
   149→  // Open state setters
   150→  const setIsGenerationsPaneOpen = useCallback((isOpen: boolean) => {
   151→    setIsGenerationsPaneOpenState(isOpen);
   152→  }, []);
   153→  
   154→  const setIsTasksPaneOpen = useCallback((isOpen: boolean) => {
   155→    // Works on desktop and tablets - only small phones use hover/tap behavior exclusively
   156→    if (!isSmallMobile) {
   157→      setIsTasksPaneOpenState(isOpen);
   158→    }
   159→  }, [isSmallMobile]);
   160→
   161→  // Reset all pane locks immediately (used by ProductTour)
   162→  // This updates local state, useUserUIState value, and database without debounce
   163→  const resetAllPaneLocks = useCallback(async () => {
   164→    const unlockedState = { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false };
   165→
   166→    // Update local locks state immediately
   167→    setLocks(unlockedState);
   168→
   169→    // Update the useUserUIState local value (prevents sync effect from restoring old value)
   170→    savePaneLocks(unlockedState);
   171→
   172→    // Also save to database immediately (no debounce) for reliability
   173→    try {
   174→      const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
   175→      if (user) {
   176→        await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   177→          scope: 'user',
   178→          id: user.id,
   179→          toolId: 'ui',
   180→          patch: { paneLocks: unlockedState },
   181→        }, undefined, 'immediate');
   182→      }
   183→    } catch (error) {
   184→      handleError(error, { context: 'PanesContext', showToast: false });
   185→    }
   186→  }, [savePaneLocks]);
   187→
   188→  // Dimension setters
   189→  const setGenerationsPaneHeight = useCallback((height: number) => {
   190→    setGenerationsPaneHeightState(height);
   191→  }, []);
   192→
   193→  const setShotsPaneWidth = useCallback((width: number) => {
   194→    setShotsPaneWidthState(width);
   195→  }, []);
   196→
   197→  const setTasksPaneWidth = useCallback((width: number) => {
   198→    setTasksPaneWidthState(width);
   199→  }, []);
   200→
   201→  const value = useMemo(
   202→    () => ({
   203→      // Return actual lock state for all device types (mobile locking is now supported)
   204→      isGenerationsPaneLocked: locks.gens,
   205→      setIsGenerationsPaneLocked,
   206→      isGenerationsPaneOpen: isGenerationsPaneOpenState,
   207→      setIsGenerationsPaneOpen,
   208→      generationsPaneHeight,
   209→      setGenerationsPaneHeight,
   210→      isShotsPaneLocked: locks.shots,
   211→      setIsShotsPaneLocked,
   212→      shotsPaneWidth,
   213→      setShotsPaneWidth,
   214→      isTasksPaneLocked: locks.tasks,
   215→      setIsTasksPaneLocked,
   216→      tasksPaneWidth,
   217→      setTasksPaneWidth,
   218→      activeTaskId,
   219→      setActiveTaskId,
   220→      isTasksPaneOpen: isTasksPaneOpenState,
   221→      setIsTasksPaneOpen,
   222→      resetAllPaneLocks,
   223→    }),
   224→    [
   225→      locks.gens,
   226→      locks.shots,
   227→      locks.tasks,
   228→      setIsGenerationsPaneLocked,
   229→      setIsShotsPaneLocked,
   230→      setIsTasksPaneLocked,
   231→      isGenerationsPaneOpenState,
   232→      setIsGenerationsPaneOpen,
   233→      generationsPaneHeight,
   234→      setGenerationsPaneHeight,
   235→      shotsPaneWidth,
   236→      setShotsPaneWidth,
   237→      tasksPaneWidth,
   238→      setTasksPaneWidth,
   239→      activeTaskId,
   240→      setActiveTaskId,
   241→      isTasksPaneOpenState,
   242→      setIsTasksPaneOpen,
   243→      resetAllPaneLocks,
   244→    ]
   245→  );
   246→
   247→  return (
   248→    <PanesContext.Provider value={value}>
   249→      {children}
   250→    </PanesContext.Provider>
   251→  );
   252→};
   253→
   254→export const usePanes = () => {
   255→  const context = useContext(PanesContext);
   256→  if (context === undefined) {
   257→    throw new Error('usePanes must be used within a PanesProvider');
   258→  }
   259→  return context;
   260→};
```

```
    15→
    16→/**
    17→ * usePairSettingsHandler - Builds the pair click handler for SegmentOutputStrip
    18→ * and TrailingEndpoint components.
    19→ *
    20→ * Handles three cases:
    21→ * 1. Single-image mode (trailing segment is the only segment)
    22→ * 2. Multi-image trailing segment (after all regular pairs)
    23→ * 3. Regular pair segments
    24→ */
    25→export function usePairSettingsHandler({
    26→  images,
    27→  imagePositions,
    28→  trailingEndFrame,
    29→  currentPositions,
    30→  pairInfo,
    31→  pairDataByIndex,
    32→  onPairClick,
    33→}: UsePairSettingsHandlerProps) {
    34→  const handleOpenPairSettings = useCallback((pairIndex: number, passedFrameData?: { frames: number; startFrame: number; endFrame: number }) => {
    35→
    36→    if (!onPairClick) return;
    37→
    38→    // Handle single-image mode (trailing segment is the only segment)
    39→    if (images.length === 1 && trailingEndFrame !== undefined) {
    40→      const entry = [...imagePositions.entries()][0];
    41→      if (entry) {
    42→        const [imageId, imageFrame] = entry;
    43→        const image = images[0];
    44→        const frames = passedFrameData?.frames ?? (trailingEndFrame - imageFrame);
    45→        const startFrame = passedFrameData?.startFrame ?? imageFrame;
    46→        const endFrame = passedFrameData?.endFrame ?? trailingEndFrame;
    47→        onPairClick(pairIndex, {
    48→          index: 0,
    49→          frames,
    50→          startFrame,
    51→          endFrame,
    52→          startImage: {
    53→            id: imageId,
    54→            generationId: image.generation_id,
    55→            url: image.imageUrl || image.thumbUrl,
    56→            thumbUrl: image.thumbUrl,
    57→            position: 1,
    58→          },
    59→          endImage: null,
    60→        });
    61→      }
    62→      return;
    63→    }
    64→
    65→    // Handle multi-image trailing segment (pairIndex is after all regular pairs)
    66→    if (pairIndex === pairInfo.length && trailingEndFrame !== undefined && imagePositions.size > 0) {
    67→      const sortedEntries = [...imagePositions.entries()].sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);
    68→      const lastEntry = sortedEntries[sortedEntries.length - 1];
    69→      if (lastEntry) {
    70→        const [imageId, imageFrame] = lastEntry;
    71→        const lastImage = images.find(img => {
    72→          const imgId = img.shot_generation_id || img.id;
    73→          return imgId === imageId;
    74→        }) || images[images.length - 1];
    75→
    76→        const defaultOffset = 9; // Same as multi-image default

    78→        const frames = passedFrameData?.frames ?? (effectiveEndFrame - imageFrame);
    79→        const startFrame = passedFrameData?.startFrame ?? imageFrame;
    80→        const endFrame = passedFrameData?.endFrame ?? effectiveEndFrame;
    81→
    82→        const pairData = {
    83→          index: pairIndex,
    84→          frames,
    85→          startFrame,
    86→          endFrame,
    87→          startImage: lastImage ? {
    88→            id: imageId,
    89→            generationId: lastImage.generation_id,
    90→            url: lastImage.imageUrl || lastImage.thumbUrl,
    91→            thumbUrl: lastImage.thumbUrl,
    92→            position: sortedEntries.length,
    93→          } : null,
    94→          endImage: null,
    95→        };
    96→        onPairClick(pairIndex, pairData);
    97→      }
    98→      return;
    99→    }
   100→
   101→    const pairData = pairDataByIndex.get(pairIndex);
   102→    const frameData = passedFrameData ?? pairInfo[pairIndex];
   103→    if (frameData) {
   104→      const mergedPairData = {
   105→        index: pairIndex,
   106→        frames: frameData.frames,
   107→        startFrame: frameData.startFrame,
   108→        endFrame: frameData.endFrame,
   109→        startImage: pairData?.startImage ?? null,
   110→        endImage: pairData?.endImage ?? null,
   111→      };
   112→      onPairClick(pairIndex, mergedPairData);
   113→    } else if (pairData) {
   114→      onPairClick(pairIndex, pairData);
   115→    }
   116→  }, [onPairClick, images, trailingEndFrame, currentPositions, pairDataByIndex, pairInfo, imagePositions]);
   117→
   118→  return { handleOpenPairSettings };
   119→}
```

```
    30→ * Sub-hooks:

    36→export const useGenerationActions = ({

    49→
```

```
    23→  aspectRatio?: string;

    54→
    55→// ============================================================================

    58→
    59→/**
    60→ * Crop images to match the shot's aspect ratio
    61→ * @returns Processed files (cropped or original if cropping fails/disabled)
    62→ */
    63→export const cropImagesToShotAspectRatio = async (
    64→  files: File[],
    65→  selectedShot: Shot | undefined,
    66→  projectId: string,
    67→  projects: Project[],
    68→  uploadSettings: UploadSettings | undefined
    69→): Promise<File[]> => {
    70→  // Skip cropping if disabled
    71→  if (uploadSettings?.cropToProjectSize === false) {
    72→    return files;
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  // Determine aspect ratio (prioritize shot over project)
    76→  const currentProject = projects.find(p => p.id === projectId);
    77→  const aspectRatioStr = selectedShot?.aspect_ratio || 
    78→                        currentProject?.aspectRatio || 
    79→                        currentProject?.settings?.aspectRatio;
    80→  
    81→  if (!aspectRatioStr) {
    82→    return files;
    83→  }
    84→
    85→  const targetAspectRatio = parseRatio(aspectRatioStr);
    86→  
    87→  if (isNaN(targetAspectRatio)) {
    88→    return files;
    89→  }
    90→
    91→  // Crop each file
    92→  const cropPromises = files.map(async (file) => {
    93→    try {
    94→      const result = await cropImageToProjectAspectRatio(file, targetAspectRatio);
    95→      if (result) {
    96→        return result.croppedFile;
    97→      }
    98→      return file; // Return original if cropping fails
    99→    } catch (error) {
   100→      handleError(error, { context: 'ImageCrop', showToast: false });
   101→      return file; // Return original on error
   102→    }
   103→  });
   104→
   105→  return await Promise.all(cropPromises);
   106→};
   107→
   108→// ============================================================================
   109→// Position Calculation
   110→// ============================================================================
   111→
   112→// Note: ensureUniqueFrame is now imported from @/shared/utils/timelinePositionCalculator
   113→
   114→export const calculateNextAvailableFrame = async (
   115→  shotId: string,
   116→  targetFrame: number | undefined
   117→): Promise<number> => {
   118→  
   119→  // Query shot_generations directly from database to get current positions
   120→  const { data: shotGenerationsData, error } = await supabase
   121→    .from('shot_generations')
   122→    .select(`
   123→      id,
   124→      generation_id,
   125→      timeline_frame,
   126→      generation:generations!shot_generations_generation_id_generations_id_fk (
   127→        id,
   128→        location,
   129→        type
   130→      )
   131→    `)
   132→    .eq('shot_id', shotId)
   133→    .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true });
   134→
   135→  if (error) {
   136→    handleError(error, { context: 'AddImagesDebug', showToast: false });
   137→    // Default to 0 if query fails
   138→    return targetFrame !== undefined ? targetFrame : 0;
   139→  }
   140→
   141→  if (!shotGenerationsData) {
   142→    return targetFrame !== undefined ? targetFrame : 0;
   143→  }
   144→
   145→  // Filter out videos using canonical function from typeGuards
   146→  const filteredShotGenerations = shotGenerationsData.filter(shotGen =>
   147→    shotGen.generation && !isVideoShotGenerations(shotGen as ShotGenerationsLike)
   148→  );
   149→
   150→  // Get positions only from items with valid timeline_frame
   151→  const existingPositions = filteredShotGenerations
   152→    .filter(shotGen => shotGen.timeline_frame !== null && shotGen.timeline_frame !== undefined && shotGen.timeline_frame !== -1)
   153→    .map(shotGen => shotGen.timeline_frame!);
   154→  
   155→  // If target frame provided, ensure it's unique
   156→  if (targetFrame !== undefined) {
   157→    const uniqueFrame = ensureUniqueFrame(targetFrame, existingPositions);
   158→    return uniqueFrame;
   159→  }
   160→
   161→  // Use centralized function to calculate next available frame (50 frames after highest)
   162→  const calculatedTargetFrame = calculateNextAvailableFrameSync(existingPositions);
   163→  return calculatedTargetFrame;
   164→};
   165→
   166→// ============================================================================
   167→// Database Operations
   168→// ============================================================================
   169→
   170→/**
   171→ * Query shot_generation records for the given generation IDs
   172→ * Includes retry logic with 500ms delay
   173→ */
   174→const queryShotGenerationRecords = async (
   175→  shotId: string,
   176→  generationIds: string[]
   177→): Promise<ShotGenerationRecord[]> => {
   178→  
   179→  const { data: shotGenRecords, error: queryError } = await supabase
   180→    .from('shot_generations')
   181→    .select('id, generation_id, timeline_frame')
   182→    .eq('shot_id', shotId)
   183→    .in('generation_id', generationIds);
   184→  
   185→  if (queryError) {
   186→    handleError(queryError, { context: 'AddImagesDebug', showToast: false });
   187→    throw queryError;
   188→  }
   189→  
   190→  // If no records found, retry once after 500ms
   191→  if (!shotGenRecords || shotGenRecords.length === 0) {
   192→    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
   193→    
   194→    const { data: retryRecords, error: retryQueryError } = await supabase
   195→      .from('shot_generations')
   196→      .select('id, generation_id, timeline_frame')
   197→      .eq('shot_id', shotId)
   198→      .in('generation_id', generationIds);
   199→    
   200→    if (retryQueryError) {
   201→      handleError(retryQueryError, { context: 'AddImagesDebug', showToast: false });
   202→      throw retryQueryError;
   203→    }
   204→
   205→    if (!retryRecords || retryRecords.length === 0) {
   206→      handleError(new Error('Still no records found after retry'), { context: 'AddImagesDebug', showToast: false });
   207→      throw new Error('Shot generation records not found after retry');
   208→    }
   209→
   210→    return retryRecords;
   211→  }
   212→  
   213→  return shotGenRecords;
   214→};
   215→
   216→/**
   217→ * Batch update timeline_frame values for shot_generation records
   218→ */
   219→const batchUpdateTimelineFrames = async (
   220→  shotGenRecords: ShotGenerationRecord[],
   221→  generationIds: string[],
   222→  calculatedTargetFrame: number,
   223→  batchVideoFrames: number
   224→): Promise<PositionUpdateResult[]> => {
   225→  
   226→  const updatePromises = generationIds.map(async (genId, index) => {
   227→    const shotGenRecord = shotGenRecords.find(r => r.generation_id === genId);
   228→    
   229→    if (!shotGenRecord) {
   230→      return { 
   231→        success: false, 
   232→        genId, 
   233→        error: 'Record not found' 
   234→      };
   235→    }
   236→    
   237→    const framePosition = calculatedTargetFrame + (index * batchVideoFrames);
   238→    
   239→    const updateResult = await supabase
   240→      .from('shot_generations')
   241→      .update({ timeline_frame: framePosition })
   242→      .eq('id', shotGenRecord.id);
   243→    
   244→    return { 
   245→      success: !updateResult.error, 
   246→      genId, 
   247→      shotGenId: shotGenRecord.id,
   248→      framePosition,
   249→      error: updateResult.error 
   250→    };
   251→  });
   252→  
   253→  const results = await Promise.all(updatePromises);
   254→  
   255→  return results;
   256→};
   257→
   258→/**
   259→ * Verify that timeline positions were correctly written to database
   260→ */
   261→const verifyPositionUpdates = async (
   262→  shotId: string,
   263→  generationIds: string[]
   264→): Promise<void> => {
   265→  
   266→  const { data: verifyData, error: verifyError } = await supabase
   267→    .from('shot_generations')
   268→    .select('id, generation_id, timeline_frame')
   269→    .eq('shot_id', shotId)
   270→    .in('generation_id', generationIds);
   271→  
   272→};
   273→
   274→/**
   275→ * Persist timeline positions to database
   276→ * This is the main orchestrator for database operations
   277→ */
   278→export const persistTimelinePositions = async (
   279→  shotId: string,
   280→  generationIds: string[],
   281→  calculatedTargetFrame: number,
   282→  batchVideoFrames: number
   283→): Promise<void> => {
   284→  
   285→  try {
   286→    // 1. Query shot_generation records (with retry)
   287→    const shotGenRecords = await queryShotGenerationRecords(shotId, generationIds);
   288→    
   289→    // 2. Batch update timeline_frame values
   290→    const results = await batchUpdateTimelineFrames(
   291→      shotGenRecords,
   292→      generationIds,
   293→      calculatedTargetFrame,
   294→      batchVideoFrames
   295→    );
   296→    
   297→    // 3. Check for errors
   298→    const errors = results.filter(r => !r.success);
   299→    
   300→    if (errors.length > 0) {
   301→      handleError(new Error(`Failed to update ${errors.length} position(s)`), {
   302→        context: 'AddImagesDebug',
   303→        toastTitle: `Failed to set ${errors.length} timeline position(s)`
   304→      });
   305→      throw new Error(`Failed to update ${errors.length} position(s)`);
   306→    }
   307→    
   308→    // 4. Verify updates
   309→    await verifyPositionUpdates(shotId, generationIds);
   310→    
   311→  } catch (dbError) {
   312→    handleError(dbError, { context: 'AddImagesDebug', showToast: false });
   313→    throw dbError;
   314→  }
   315→};
   316→
   317→
```

   221→**Agent S (ProjectContext decomposition):** Good decomposition. ProjectContext 653→128 lines (thin provider). Three extracted hooks:
   222→- `useProjectCRUD.ts` (327 lines): project list state, fetch/create/update/delete. `determineProjectIdToSelect` exported as utility.
   223→- `useProjectSelection.ts` (150 lines): selectedProjectId state, localStorage persistence, cross-device sync.
   224→- `useProjectDefaults.ts` (65 lines): side-effect orchestrator — fetch trigger, cross-device sync, prefetch, mobile timeout fallback.
   225→
   226→Context shape is unchanged — all consumers (`useProject()`) get the exact same `ProjectContextType`. The callback pattern (onProjectsLoaded/Created/Deleted) is necessary for CRUD→selection communication. Not circular — `useProjectSelection` provides callbacks, `useProjectCRUD` calls them.
   227→
   228→**Agent T (App.tsx auth gate):** Clean. `AuthGate` is a 6-line component that returns `null` during auth check, preventing data-dependent providers (UserSettings, Project, Realtime, etc.) from rendering before auth state is known. This is NOT an auth wall — unauthenticated users still render normally once auth check completes.
   229→
   230→**Agent U (Edge function logging + CORS):** Mechanical. Added `SystemLogger` (buffered DB logging) to 18 edge functions. Changes are consistent: import → create logger → replace console.log/error → add `await logger.flush()` before error responses. Console output is preserved (SystemLogger writes to both console and DB). Functions that already had SystemLogger were skipped.
   231→
   232→**Post-wave review fixes applied:**
   233→1. **BUG FIX:** `window.__PROJECT_CONTEXT__` was incorrectly DEV-gated on write (by Wave 3 Agent R) but read in production by `useProjectGenerations`, `useTasks`, and `ImageGenerationToolPage`. Removed DEV gate — this is a `[structural]` global, not debug-only.
   234→2. **Anti-pattern fix:** PanesContext `savePaneLocks` moved outside `setLocks` state updater to avoid side effects in updater functions (React StrictMode double-invocation safe).
   235→3. **Stale comments:** Updated 3 references to deleted `useDeviceDetection` → `useDeviceInfo`.
   236→
   237→**Sense check:** The ProjectContext decomposition is the largest structural change. Reviewed for over-engineering — the hook boundaries are clean and each hook has a single responsibility. `useProjectDefaults` is a bag of side effects by design (the orchestrator pattern keeps the other hooks pure). `tsc --noEmit` passes clean.
   238→
   239→### Wave 5a — Evaluation
   240→
   241→**Agent V (ImageEditContext → 3 sub-contexts):** Clean decomposition. Original 319-line monolithic context split into:
   242→- `ImageEditCanvasContext.tsx` (182 lines): mode, brush, annotation, canvas, reposition, display refs. Consumers: LightboxLayout, FloatingToolControls, MediaDisplayWithCanvas, InfoPanel.
   243→- `ImageEditFormContext.tsx` (105 lines): prompts, strengths, LoRA, model, advanced settings. Consumer: EditModePanel only.
   244→- `ImageEditStatusContext.tsx` (76 lines): 10 generation loading/success booleans. Consumer: EditModePanel only.
   245→- `ImageEditContext.tsx` (234 lines): composed provider with `useMemo` slices. Backward-compatible `useImageEditSafe()` preserved.
   246→
   247→Split strategy was 3 contexts instead of planned 4 — correct decision since mode/brush/annotation/canvas/reposition are always consumed together by canvas components. The natural boundary is canvas vs. form vs. status. Consumers migrated to specific hooks. `tsc --noEmit` passes clean.
   248→
   249→**Pre-existing issue found:** InlineEditView renders FloatingToolControls without wrapping in ImageEditProvider. FloatingToolControls reads from context (gets defaults), and the props InlineEditView passes are silently ignored. This predates our changes — FloatingToolControls was already context-only before Wave 5a.
   250→
   251→**Agent W (SegmentSettingsForm → 3 sub-components):** Good extraction. Original 1044 lines → parent 376 lines + 3 extracted components:
   252→- `AdvancedSettingsSection.tsx` (396 lines): collapsible advanced panel with motion/LoRA/structure video. Owns its own `savingField` state and LoRA handlers.
   253→- `PromptSection.tsx` (116 lines): prompt textarea with enhanced/default badges and field controls.
   254→- `StructureVideoSection.tsx` (429 lines): video upload, preview, treatment selector, strength/percent sliders, DatasetBrowser modal.
   255→
   256→Total is 1334 lines (up from 1044) due to interface definitions and imports — expected overhead of decomposition. Each file has a clear single responsibility. No new contexts or abstractions — pure prop drilling at 1 level.
   257→
   258→**Agent X (MediaGallery GalleryConfig object):** Clean. 17 individual boolean props → single `config?: Partial<GalleryConfig>` prop with `DEFAULT_GALLERY_CONFIG` defaults. Migrated 8 callers across 7 files. Internal components (Grid, Header, Lightbox) still accept individual props — correct since they're internal, and a second level of config-object indirection would add complexity for no benefit. `tsc --noEmit` passes clean. Net prop count: MediaGalleryProps went from ~50 fields to ~35.
   259→
   260→**Sense check:** No over-engineering. All three decompositions are justified — each addressed a genuine monolith (>300 LOC or >40 props). The ImageEditContext split is the most impactful (re-render reduction for canvas components). SegmentSettingsForm extraction makes the code navigable. MediaGallery config object is a standard pattern. `tsc --noEmit` passes clean.

```
1→/**
     2→ * ImageEditContext — Composed provider for all image edit state.
     3→ *
     4→ * Splits state into three sub-contexts by concern:
     5→ *   - ImageEditCanvasContext: mode, brush, annotation, canvas, reposition, display
     6→ *   - ImageEditFormContext: prompts, strengths, LoRA, model, advanced settings
     7→ *   - ImageEditStatusContext: generation loading/success flags
     8→ *
     9→ * The split reduces re-renders: canvas components don't re-render when the user
    10→ * types in a prompt field, and form components don't re-render on brush strokes.
    11→ *
    12→ * For backward compatibility, ImageEditState and useImageEditSafe() still exist
    13→ * and return the full merged state. Components should migrate to the specific
    14→ * sub-context hooks (useImageEditCanvasSafe, useImageEditFormSafe,
    15→ * useImageEditStatusSafe) for optimal performance.
    16→ */
    17→
    18→import React, { useMemo } from 'react';
    19→import type { LoraMode } from '../hooks/editSettingsTypes';
    20→
    21→// Sub-contexts
    22→import {
    23→  ImageEditCanvasProvider,
    24→  useImageEditCanvasSafe,
    25→  type ImageEditCanvasState,
    26→  type ImageEditMode,
    27→} from './ImageEditCanvasContext';
    28→import {
    29→  ImageEditFormProvider,
    30→  useImageEditFormSafe,
    31→  type ImageEditFormState,
    32→} from './ImageEditFormContext';
    33→import {
    34→  ImageEditStatusProvider,
    35→  useImageEditStatusSafe,
    36→  type ImageEditStatusState,
    37→} from './ImageEditStatusContext';
    38→
    39→// Re-export sub-context types and hooks for direct consumption
    40→export type { ImageEditCanvasState, ImageEditFormState, ImageEditStatusState, ImageEditMode };
    41→export { useImageEditCanvasSafe, useImageEditFormSafe, useImageEditStatusSafe };
    42→export type { LoraMode };
    43→
    44→// ============================================================================
    45→// Composed Type (backward-compatible)
    46→// ============================================================================
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * Full image edit state, composed from the three sub-contexts.
    50→ * Consumers that need fields from only one concern should use the
    51→ * sub-context hooks directly for better performance.
    52→ */
    53→export type ImageEditState =
    54→  ImageEditCanvasState &
    55→  ImageEditFormState &
    56→  ImageEditStatusState;
    57→
    58→// ============================================================================
    59→// Composed Provider
    60→// ============================================================================
    61→
    62→interface ImageEditProviderProps {
    63→  children: React.ReactNode;
    64→  value: ImageEditState;
    65→}
    66→
    67→/**
    68→ * Provides all three sub-contexts from a single ImageEditState value.
    69→ * The value is split into sub-context slices via useMemo.
    70→ */
    71→export const ImageEditProvider: React.FC<ImageEditProviderProps> = ({
    72→  children,
    73→  value,
    74→}) => {
    75→  // Split the composed value into sub-context slices.
    76→  // Each useMemo depends only on the fields for that sub-context,
    77→  // so unchanged slices keep the same reference.
    78→
    79→  const canvasValue = useMemo<ImageEditCanvasState>(() => ({
    80→    // Edit mode
    81→    isInpaintMode: value.isInpaintMode,
    82→    isMagicEditMode: value.isMagicEditMode,
    83→    isSpecialEditMode: value.isSpecialEditMode,
    84→    editMode: value.editMode,
    85→    setIsInpaintMode: value.setIsInpaintMode,
    86→    setIsMagicEditMode: value.setIsMagicEditMode,
    87→    setEditMode: value.setEditMode,
    88→    handleEnterInpaintMode: value.handleEnterInpaintMode,
    89→    handleExitInpaintMode: value.handleExitInpaintMode,
    90→    handleEnterMagicEditMode: value.handleEnterMagicEditMode,
    91→    handleExitMagicEditMode: value.handleExitMagicEditMode,
    92→    // Brush tool
    93→    brushSize: value.brushSize,
    94→    setBrushSize: value.setBrushSize,
    95→    isEraseMode: value.isEraseMode,
```

```
    35→      video.onloadedmetadata = () => {
    36→        resolve(video.duration);

    47→
    48→  /** Upload a single video file to storage + DB. Returns the new video's ID. */
    49→  const uploadVideoFile = async (file: File, userId: string): Promise<string> => {
    50→    const duration = await getVideoDuration(file);
    51→
    52→    const fileExt = file.name.split('.').pop();
    53→    const fileName = `${userId}/${Date.now()}.${fileExt}`;

   119→  const uploadVideo = async (file: File): Promise<string> => {

   123→      if (!user) throw new Error('User not authenticated');

   125→      if (!selectedBatchId) {

   139→  const uploadVideosWithSplitModes = async (videoFiles: Array<{

   172→              }
   173→            } else {
```

   300→      const updated = { ...prev, ...updates };
   301→
   302→      // Always track pending settings - this protects user input from being overwritten by DB load
   303→      debouncedSave.trackPendingUpdate(updated, entityId ?? null);
   304→
   305→      // Schedule auto-save (no-ops during loading - just keeps pending tracking)
   306→      debouncedSave.scheduleSave(entityId ?? null);

   308→      return updated;
   309→    });
   310→  }, [entityId, debouncedSave]);
   311→
   312→  // Revert to last saved settings
   313→  const revert = useCallback(() => {
   314→    if (loadedSettingsRef.current) {
   315→      setSettings(loadedSettingsRef.current);
   316→      debouncedSave.clearPending();
   317→    }
   318→  }, [debouncedSave]);
   319→
   320→  // Manual save - flushes debounce immediately
   321→  const save = useCallback(async () => {
   322→    debouncedSave.cancelPendingSave();
   323→    await saveImmediate();
   324→  }, [saveImmediate, debouncedSave]);
   325→
   326→  // Reset to defaults (or provided settings)
   327→  const reset = useCallback((newDefaults?: T) => {
   328→    const resetTo = newDefaults || defaults;
   329→
   330→    setSettings(resetTo);
   331→    loadedSettingsRef.current = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(resetTo));
   332→    debouncedSave.clearPending();

   335→  // Initialize from external source (e.g., "last used" settings) - custom mode only

   338→    // Only apply if we don't have persisted data and aren't loading
   339→    if (hasPersistedData || isLoadingRef.current) {

   341→    }
   342→
   343→    setSettings(prev => ({ ...prev, ...data }));

   345→
   346→  // Handle entity changes - flush and reset
   347→  useEffect(() => {

   349→
   350→    if (!entityId) {

   352→      currentEntityIdRef.current = null;
   353→      setSettings(defaults);
   354→      setStatus('idle');
   355→      setHasPersistedData(false);
   356→      loadedSettingsRef.current = null;

   359→    }

   365→      setStatus('idle');
   366→      setHasPersistedData(false);

   380→
   381→    // Don't reload if we have pending edits for this entity

   384→      // Schedule save for pending edits
   385→      debouncedSave.cancelPendingSave();

   390→        } catch (err) {
   391→          handleError(err, { context: 'useAutoSaveSettings.pendingSave', showToast: false });
   392→        }
   393→      }, debounceMs);
   394→      return;
   395→    }
   396→
   397→    setStatus('loading');
   398→    isLoadingRef.current = true;
   399→
   400→    customLoadRef.current!(entityId)
   401→      .then(loaded => {
   402→        // Check if entity changed during load
   403→        if (currentEntityIdRef.current !== entityId) {
   404→          return;
   405→        }
   406→
   407→        // Check again for pending edits (user may have typed during load)
   408→        if (debouncedSave.hasPendingFor(entityId)) {
   409→          setStatus('ready');
   410→          isLoadingRef.current = false;
   411→          return;
   412→        }
   413→
   414→        if (loaded) {
   415→          const mergedState = { ...defaults, ...loaded };
   416→          const cloned = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(mergedState));
   417→
   418→          setSettings(cloned);
   419→          loadedSettingsRef.current = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(cloned));
   420→          setHasPersistedData(true);
   421→        } else {
   422→          setSettings(defaults);
   423→          loadedSettingsRef.current = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(defaults));
   424→          setHasPersistedData(false);
   425→        }

   427→        setStatus('ready');
   428→        isLoadingRef.current = false;
   429→        setError(null);
   430→      })
   431→      .catch(err => {

   433→        setStatus('error');
   434→        isLoadingRef.current = false;
   435→        setError(err as Error);
   436→      });
   437→  }, [isCustomMode, entityId, enabled, status, defaults, debounceMs, debouncedSave]);
   438→
   439→  // Load settings - React Query mode (reactive from useToolSettings)
   440→  useEffect(() => {
   441→    if (isCustomMode) return;
   442→    if (!entityId || !enabled) return;
   443→
   444→    // Show loading state while fetching
   445→    if (rqIsLoading) {
   446→      if (status === 'idle') {
   447→        setStatus('loading');
   448→      }
   449→      return;
   450→    }
   451→
   452→    // Don't overwrite if we're in the middle of saving
   453→    if (status === 'saving') {
   454→      return;
   455→    }
   456→
   457→    // Don't overwrite if user has pending edits for THIS entity (debounce hasn't fired yet)
   458→    // This prevents React Query refetches from "unwriting" user input
   459→    // IMPORTANT: We now protect pending edits even on first load - losing user's typing

   461→    if (debouncedSave.hasPendingFor(entityId)) {
   462→      // Still transition to ready and schedule save for pending edits
   463→      if (status !== 'ready') {
   464→        setStatus('ready');
   465→        // Schedule save for input that happened during loading
   466→        debouncedSave.cancelPendingSave();
   467→        const toSave = debouncedSave.pendingSettingsRef.current!;
   468→        debouncedSave.saveTimeoutRef.current = setTimeout(async () => {
   469→          try {
   470→            await saveImmediateRef.current(toSave);
   471→          } catch (err) {
   472→            handleError(err, { context: 'useAutoSaveSettings.pendingSave', showToast: false });
   473→          }
   474→        }, debounceMs);
   475→      }
   476→      return;
   477→    }
   478→
   479→    // Apply settings from DB
   480→    // Note: dbSettings comes from useToolSettings which already merges in priority order:
   481→    // defaults -> user -> project -> shot (via deepMerge). We layer local defaults on top
   482→    // only as a fallback for fields not present in the merged settings.
   483→    const loadedSettings: T = {
   484→      ...defaults,
   485→      ...(dbSettings || {}),
   486→    };
   487→
   488→    // Deep clone to prevent React Query cache reference sharing
   489→    const clonedSettings = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(loadedSettings));

   491→    // Avoid setState loops when dbSettings identity changes but values don't.
   492→    if (loadedSettingsRef.current && deepEqual(clonedSettings, loadedSettingsRef.current)) {
   493→      if (status !== 'ready') {
   494→        setStatus('ready');
   495→      }
   496→      return;
   497→    }
   498→
   499→    // No pending edits for this entity - safe to apply DB settings
   500→
   501→    setSettings(clonedSettings);
   502→    loadedSettingsRef.current = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(clonedSettings));
   503→    setStatus('ready');
   504→    setError(null);
   505→  }, [isCustomMode, entityId, rqIsLoading, dbSettings, defaults, enabled, status, debounceMs, debouncedSave]);

   507→  // Memoize return value to prevent object recreation on every render
   508→  // NOTE: entityId uses currentEntityIdRef.current which is a ref value, so it updates
   509→  // without triggering memo recalculation. Consumers should check status === 'ready'
   510→  // alongside entityId to ensure settings are actually loaded for that entity.
   511→  return useMemo(() => ({
   512→    settings,
   513→    status,
   514→    entityId: currentEntityIdRef.current,
   515→    isDirty,
   516→    error,
   517→    hasShotSettings: isCustomMode ? hasPersistedData : hasShotSettings,
   518→    hasPersistedData: isCustomMode ? hasPersistedData : hasShotSettings,
   519→    updateField,
   520→    updateFields,
   521→    save,
   522→    saveImmediate,
   523→    revert,
   524→    reset,
   525→    initializeFrom,
   526→  }), [settings, status, isDirty, error, isCustomMode, hasPersistedData, hasShotSettings, updateField, updateFields, save, saveImmediate, revert, reset, initializeFrom]);
   527→}

    20→### 1. imagesPerPrompt Silent Change
    21→
    22→**Location:** `src/shared/components/ImageGenerationForm/ImageGenerationForm.tsx` lines 70-76
    23→
    24→```tsx
    25→form.setEffectivePromptMode(mode);
    26→if (mode === 'automated') {
    27→  form.setImagesPerPrompt(8);
    28→} else if (mode === 'managed') {
    29→  form.setImagesPerPrompt(1);
    30→}
    31→```
    32→
    33→**Problem:** Switching prompt mode silently resets `imagesPerPrompt` without telling the user. If they had manually set it to 4, switching to managed drops it to 1 with no indication.
    34→
    35→**Fix options:**
    36→- **A (Minimal):** Add a toast or inline note: "Images per prompt set to {n} for {mode} mode"
    37→- **B (Better):** Remember per-mode values — store `automatedImagesPerPrompt` and `managedImagesPerPrompt` separately, restore on switch
    38→- **C (Best):** Don't auto-set at all; just change the default for new sessions
    39→
    40→**Recommendation:** Option B — store separate values per mode.
    41→
    42→### 2. Hardcoded Colors
    43→
    44→**OnboardingModal:** Need to locate and replace hardcoded hex/rgb values with Tailwind theme tokens (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `border-border`, etc.)
    45→
    46→**DatasetBrowserModal:** Same treatment.
    47→
    48→**Action:** Search each component for hardcoded color values, replace with semantic tokens from the design system.
    49→
    50→### 3. complete_task Double Query
    51→
    52→**Location:** `supabase/functions/complete_task/index.ts` lines 42-81
    53→
    54→```ts
    55→// Query 1: Fetch task
    56→const { data: task } = await supabase
    57→  .from("tasks")
    58→  .select(`id, task_type, project_id, params`)
    59→  .eq("id", taskId)
    60→  .single();
    61→
    62→// Query 2: Fetch task_types metadata (comment: "no FK relationship exists")
    63→const { data: typeData } = await supabase
    64→  .from("task_types")
    65→  .select("tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type")
    66→  .eq("name", task.task_type)
    67→  .single();
    68→```
    69→
    70→**The comment says "no FK" but you CAN join on string columns.** The `task_type` column holds the task type name, and `task_types.name` is the PK.
    71→
    72→**Fix:** Single query with embedded select:
    73→```ts
    74→const { data: task } = await supabase
    75→  .from("tasks")
    76→  .select(`id, task_type, project_id, params, task_types!tasks_task_type_fkey(tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type)`)
    77→  .eq("id", taskId)
    78→  .single();
    79→```
    80→
    81→**Or** if no FK constraint exists, add one in a migration first (or use `.select()` with a manual join via RPC). Either way, this saves a round-trip on every task completion.
    82→
    83→### 4. ReferenceSectionProps Prop Drilling
    84→
    85→**Problem:** 35 fields drilled through `ReferenceSection` → 5 child components, when `ImageGenerationFormContext` already provides `FormReferenceState`, `FormReferenceHandlers`, `FormLoraState`, and `FormLoraHandlers`.

    87→**File:** `src/shared/components/ImageGenerationForm/components/reference/types.ts` (lines 61-96)
    88→
    89→**Drilling chain:** `ImageGenerationForm.tsx` → `ReferenceSection` → `ReferenceModeControls` (16 props), `ReferenceGrid` (9 props), `LoraGrid` (4 props), etc.
    90→
    91→**Fix:** Have child components consume `useImageGenerationFormContext()` directly instead of receiving props. The context already contains all the reference/LoRA state and handlers.
    92→
    93→**Approach:**
    94→1. In `ReferenceModeControls`, `ReferenceGrid`, `LoraGrid` — import and use context directly
    95→2. Remove context-sourced props from `ReferenceSectionProps` interface
    96→3. Keep only truly local/override props in the interface
    97→4. `ReferenceSection` itself becomes a thin layout wrapper
    98→
    99→### 5. ImageLightbox State Mirroring
   100→
   101→**Problem:** ImageLightbox creates local state that mirrors hook returns via useEffect sync, causing a one-frame delay.
   102→
   103→**Root cause:** Hook ordering — some state isn't available during the render where it's needed, so it's "pushed" via useEffect into local state.
   104→
   105→**Action for now:** Add a code comment explaining the workaround and what the proper fix would be (likely restructuring the hook dependency chain). Full fix deferred to P6 (ImageLightbox decomposition).
   106→
   107→### 6. useGenerationActions 14 Refs
   108→
   109→**Location:** `src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/useGenerationActions.ts` (727 lines)
   110→
   111→**Problem:** 14 `useRef` declarations to work around stale closures. The callbacks need stable references but the data they read changes frequently.
   112→
   113→**Root cause:** The component boundary is wrong — too many concerns in one hook, with data flowing through refs instead of through React's render cycle.
   114→
   115→**Action for now:** Document as architectural note for P6. The proper fix is decomposing useGenerationActions into smaller hooks with narrower data dependencies (e.g., separate hooks for add/remove/duplicate/position operations).

    56→const timeout = isMobile ? 15000 : 10000;

    61→

    64→function useMobileTimeoutFallback({

    96→        return { gens: false, shots: false, tasks: false, [paneName]: true };

    98→      return { ...prev, [paneName]: isLocked };

   107→
   108→**Current:** 4 overlapping timeouts with unclear coordination:
   109→1. 5000ms — force success if verification still loading
   110→2. 2000ms interval — poll credit queries
   111→3. 30000ms — cleanup everything
   112→4. 1500ms — show loading briefly before success
   113→
   114→**Problem:** Timeouts 1 and 4 can fire in either order. Timeout 3 clears timeout 1 but also forces success, creating redundancy.
   115→
   116→**Fix: State machine approach:**
   117→```
   118→loading → polling (2s interval) → verified | timeout(30s) → success → redirect
   119→```
   120→
   121→States: `loading` | `polling` | `verified` | `timed_out` | `redirecting`
   122→
   123→Transitions:
   124→- `loading` → `polling`: on mount, start credit poll
   125→- `polling` → `verified`: when credits reflect payment
   126→- `polling` → `timed_out`: after 30s, assume success anyway
   127→- `verified`/`timed_out` → `redirecting`: after 1.5s display delay

    79→

    81→1. QueryClientProvider → 2. TaskTypeConfigInitializer → 3. AuthProvider → 4. UserSettingsProvider → 5. ProjectProvider → 6. RealtimeProvider → 7. ShotsProvider → 8. GenerationTaskProvider → 9. IncomingTasksProvider → 10. PanesProvider → 11. LastAffectedShotProvider → 12. CurrentShotProvider → 13. ToolPageHeaderProvider
    82→

   106→
   107→Three edge functions with duplicated sub-task detection logic. Need to identify which functions and extract a shared billing module.
   108→
   109→**Key concern:** Sub-task detection (orchestrator tasks that spawn child tasks) determines credit charging. If this logic diverges across functions, users could be over/under-charged.

   111→### F. Task Status Guards
   112→
   113→**Current:** Frontend TasksPane can change task status. No server-side validation prevents invalid transitions (e.g., Completed → Queued).

   117→Valid: Queued → In Progress → Completed

   105→   ```ts

   108→     showDownload?: boolean;
   109→     showShare?: boolean;
   110→     showEdit?: boolean;
   111→     showStar?: boolean;
   112→     showAddToShot?: boolean;

   119→### 4. ImageEditContext (319 lines, 70+ fields)
   120→**File:** `src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/contexts/ImageEditContext.tsx`
   121→
   122→**Problem:** Any mutation in any of 70+ fields triggers re-renders in all consumers.
   123→
   124→**Split into:**
   125→```
   126→ImageEditContext (thin, composes sub-contexts)
   127→├── EditModeContext        — 8 fields (current mode, mode switcher)
   128→├── BrushToolContext       — 6 fields (size, opacity, color, tool type)
   129→├── AnnotationToolContext  — 4 fields (annotation mode, shapes)
   130→├── CanvasInteractionContext — 8 fields (zoom, pan, transform)

   132→├── EditFormContext        — 10+ fields (prompt, params, submit)
   133→└── GenerationStatusContext — 8+ fields (loading, progress, results)
   134→```
   135→
   136→Each sub-context only re-renders its consumers when relevant state changes.
   137→
   138→---
   139→
   140→## General Decomposition Rules
   141→
   142→1. **Extract when a section has its own state** — if a group of fields change together but independently of other groups, it's a natural boundary
   143→2. **Props → Context when drilling >2 levels** — but split contexts by concern (don't create another mega-context)
   144→3. **Hooks → smaller hooks when they have >5 useRef** — refs are a code smell for wrong boundaries
   145→4. **Components → smaller components at ~300 LOC** — the sweet spot for readability
   146→5. **Don't share what doesn't need sharing** — if only one consumer uses a field, it doesn't belong in shared context
   147→6. **Config objects for boolean flag groups** — `{ showDelete, showDownload, showShare }` → `GalleryConfig`

```
+/**
+ * Shared billing utilities for edge functions
+ *
+ * Centralizes:
+ *  - Orchestrator/sub-task detection (extractOrchestratorRef, isSubTask)
+ *  - Sub-task query filter for Supabase `.or()` calls
+ *  - Cost calculation HTTP trigger
+ *
+ * Consumers: calculate-task-cost, update-task-status, complete_task
+ */
+
+// ===== Constants =====
+
+/** UUID v4 regex — used to distinguish real orchestrator FK refs from human-readable IDs */
+export const UUID_REGEX = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
+
+// ===== Orchestrator reference extraction =====
+
+/**
+ * Extract orchestrator_task_id from task params.
+ *
+ * Sub-tasks can store the orchestrator reference in multiple param paths
+ * depending on the task type and how they were created:
+ *  - params.orchestrator_task_id_ref          (travel_segment)
+ *  - params.orchestrator_details.orchestrator_task_id  (join_clips_segment)
+ *  - params.originalParams.orchestrator_details.orchestrator_task_id (legacy)
+ *  - params.orchestrator_task_id              (some legacy tasks)
+ *
+ * Returns the raw string value (may not be a valid UUID) or null.
+ */
+export function extractOrchestratorRef(params: any): string | null {
+  if (!params || typeof params !== 'object') return null;
+
+  return (
+    params.orchestrator_task_id_ref ||
+    params.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
+    params.originalParams?.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
+    params.orchestrator_task_id ||
+    null
+  );
+}
+

+ * Determine whether a task is a sub-task of an orchestrator.
```

## Extraction Over-Engineering Review

### 1. SegmentSettingsForm PromptSection (116L) -- Rating: **MILD**

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/SegmentSettingsForm/components/PromptSection.tsx`

**Consumers:** 1 (SegmentSettingsForm only). The grep hit in PromptEditorModal is a false positive -- it uses a local variable `isAIPromptSectionExpanded`, not this component.

**What it does:** Renders a prompt textarea with enhanced/default badges, voice input, "Enhance Prompt" toggle, and "Make Primary" variant switch. It accepts 11 props, most of which are pass-through from the parent.

**Assessment:** This is borderline. At 116 lines it is not trivial -- it has real conditional rendering logic (3 badge types, optional enhance toggle), and it does carve out a coherent "prompt section" concern from the parent form. However, with only 1 consumer and the fact that the parent (SegmentSettingsForm at 377L) is not particularly large even with it inlined, the extraction adds navigational overhead without a clear win. The prop interface (11 props, many pass-throughs) is a code smell of an extraction that does not have clean boundaries.

**Verdict:** Slightly over-done but harmless. The parent is already well under the 300L threshold. Not worth reverting because it does group a coherent UI section, but it did not need to happen.

---

### 2. ImageEditContext 3-Way Split -- Rating: **GOOD**

**Files:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/contexts/ImageEditCanvasContext.tsx` (182L, 5+ consumers: LightboxLayout, FloatingToolControls, MediaDisplayWithCanvas, InfoPanel, useEditModePanelState)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/contexts/ImageEditFormContext.tsx` (105L, 1 consumer: useEditModePanelState)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/contexts/ImageEditStatusContext.tsx` (76L, 1 consumer: useEditModePanelState)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/contexts/ImageEditContext.tsx` (234L, composed provider + backward-compat hook)

**Assessment:** The flag was that FormContext and StatusContext each have a single consumer (EditModePanel via useEditModePanelState). That is true. However, the split is justified by render optimization, not consumer count. The composed context had ~50+ fields in a single context value. The Canvas context has brush strokes that change on every paint stroke; the Form context has prompt text that changes on every keystroke; the Status context has loading booleans that change on task completion. Without the split, every canvas component re-renders when the user types a prompt, and every form field re-renders on brush strokes. The `useMemo` slicing in the composed provider (lines 79-203 of ImageEditContext.tsx) confirms this was intentional render isolation.

The fact that Form and Status currently have only 1 consumer each does not matter -- Canvas has 5+ consumers, and the split prevents those 5 components from re-rendering on keystroke/status changes. The architecture is correct.

**Would a 2-way split (Canvas vs Everything) be better?** No. Form changes (keystrokes) and Status changes (task completion flags) are completely independent triggers. Merging them would mean EditModePanel re-renders on typing even though only the prompt field changed -- and the EditModePanel at 557L is complex enough that unnecessary renders matter.

**Verdict:** Justified. The 3-way split follows standard React context optimization patterns. Consumer count is the wrong metric here; render boundary isolation is the right one.

---

### 3. useEditModePanelState (302L extracted from EditModePanel 557L) -- Rating: **MILD**

**Files:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useEditModePanelState.ts` (302L)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/components/EditModePanel.tsx` (557L)

**Assessment:** The hook extracts: (a) props-first state resolution with context fallback (lines 76-141), (b) two effects for tracking prompt editing and LoRA reset on mode change (lines 153-171), (c) mode selector item configuration (lines 186-224), (d) responsive style helpers (lines 230-235). The component at 557L is still substantial -- it is almost all JSX rendering.

The extraction does create a clean separation: the hook owns all state resolution + effects, the component owns all rendering. But the hook's return value (lines 237-301) is essentially a 40+ field bag that gets destructured immediately in the component (lines 155-216). This is the "context forwarding" anti-pattern -- the hook does not compute or derive much; it mostly reads from 4 contexts and re-exposes the same fields. The actual logic (2 effects + 1 handler + mode selector config) is about 80 lines of real work; the rest is boilerplate destructuring and re-export.

Combined, the two files total 859L. Inlined, it would be around 650L (eliminating interface duplication and the return/destructure handoff). That is above 300L but not egregiously so for a component of this complexity.

**Verdict:** Slightly over-done. The hook does not earn its weight -- it is more a "move code to another file" than a meaningful abstraction. It does not simplify testing (the state is all context-dependent), does not enable reuse (single consumer), and adds navigational overhead. However, it is not harmful and does keep the component focused on JSX. Not worth reverting.

### 4. useVideoEditContextValue (225L extracted from VideoLightbox 803L) -- Rating: **GOOD**

**Files:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useVideoEditContextValue.ts` (225L)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/VideoLightbox.tsx` (803L)

**Assessment:** VideoLightbox at 803L is already large and would be ~1000L without this extraction. The hook does real work: (a) it has a non-trivial effect for routing variant params to edit modes (lines 118-145), with task-type detection and settings hydration; (b) it builds a memoized context value from scattered inputs (lines 151-222). The variant params routing logic is self-contained business logic that genuinely benefits from isolation -- it has its own effect dependencies, error paths, and conditional routing.

Unlike useEditModePanelState, this hook actually computes and transforms data rather than just forwarding context values. The input interface is focused (7 props), and the output is a single typed context value. The extraction keeps VideoLightbox (already the largest component in the codebase at 800L) from growing further.

**Verdict:** Justified. The hook encapsulates real business logic (variant param routing), reduces VideoLightbox from ~1000L to 800L, and has a clean input/output boundary.

### 5. useDebouncedSettingsSave (281L extracted from useAutoSaveSettings 527L) -- Rating: **GOOD**

**Files:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useDebouncedSettingsSave.ts` (281L)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useAutoSaveSettings.ts` (527L)

**Consumers:** 1 (useAutoSaveSettings only)

**Assessment:** Despite having a single consumer, this extraction is well-justified. The hook encapsulates a coherent, complex subsystem: debounce scheduling (with edit-version race condition protection), pending state tracking, and three distinct flush lifecycle effects (entity change, unmount, beforeunload). Lines 140-267 contain three separate `useEffect` hooks with careful cleanup logic, captured variables, and fire-and-forget async patterns. This is exactly the kind of tricky lifecycle code that benefits from isolation.

The parent hook (useAutoSaveSettings at 527L) would be ~800L without this extraction, with mixed concerns: settings loading, dirty tracking, React Query integration, AND debounce/flush lifecycle. The extraction creates two files with clear responsibilities: useAutoSaveSettings handles the what (load, merge, save, dirty), useDebouncedSettingsSave handles the when (schedule, debounce, flush).

The comment says the extraction "eliminates duplication between updateField and updateFields" -- looking at the parent (lines 279-310), both now call `debouncedSave.incrementEditVersion()`, `debouncedSave.trackPendingUpdate()`, and `debouncedSave.scheduleSave()`. Without the extraction, each of those would need to inline the scheduling/tracking logic, creating genuine duplication or requiring inline helpers.

**Verdict:** Justified. Complex lifecycle logic with race condition handling is exactly what should be extracted. Clean interface, clear responsibility split, eliminates real duplication.

### 6. useTrainingData Decomposition -- Rating: **GOOD**

**Files:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/training-data-helper/hooks/useTrainingData.ts` (237L, orchestrator)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/training-data-helper/hooks/useTrainingDataBatches.ts` (124L, batch CRUD)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/training-data-helper/hooks/useTrainingDataUpload.ts` (205L, upload + split modes)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/training-data-helper/hooks/transforms.ts` (74L, DB row transforms)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/training-data-helper/hooks/types.ts` (38L, shared types)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/training-data-helper/hooks/useVideoUrlCache.ts` (79L, URL caching)

**Total:** 757L across 6 files (vs original 715L monolith)

**Assessment:** The original 715L hook was doing genuinely separate things:
1. **Batch CRUD** (fetch/create/update/delete batches, selectedBatchId state) -- now 124L in useTrainingDataBatches
2. **Upload pipeline** (file upload, video duration detection, segment creation with split modes) -- now 205L in useTrainingDataUpload
3. **Video/segment CRUD** (fetch/create/update/delete videos and segments) -- remains in useTrainingData at 237L
4. **Transforms** (DB row to client types) -- 74L in transforms.ts
5. **URL caching** -- 79L in useVideoUrlCache

These are genuinely distinct concerns. The batch operations have their own state (batches, selectedBatchId) and their own CRUD cycle. The upload logic has its own state (isUploading) and complex async workflow (duration detection, split modes, sequential uploads). The transforms are pure functions shared across files.

The orchestrator (useTrainingData at 237L) composes them cleanly: it owns videos/segments state, delegates batch management to useTrainingDataBatches, delegates upload to useTrainingDataUpload, and exposes a unified public API. The total code grew only 42 lines (from 715L to 757L) for the interface overhead, which is reasonable.

**Was it a natural monolith?** No. A monolith is justified when the pieces are tightly coupled and share significant state. Here, batches have their own state, uploads have their own state, and transforms are stateless. The only coupling is that uploads need `createSegment` and `selectedBatchId` from the parent, which is handled cleanly via props.

**Verdict:** Justified. Clean separation of genuinely distinct concerns, minimal overhead, each piece is independently understandable.

Actually, wait -- I need to re-examine. In browsers, when `window.supabase = client` is set, and the code is NOT in strict mode at the function level, bare `supabase` would actually resolve to `window.supabase` through the scope chain. But ES modules are always strict mode. However, TypeScript with `noImplicitAny: false` compiles this to... let me think.

The bundler (Vite) would see `supabase` as an undeclared variable. In the browser, within a module scope (strict mode), accessing an undeclared variable throws ReferenceError. The fact that `window.supabase` exists doesn't help because strict mode doesn't chain to the global object for bare names.

So this IS a bug -- it would throw a ReferenceError at runtime when the fallback code path is hit. However, if the upload mutation always sets positions correctly, this fallback path might never be reached, which is why it hasn't been caught yet.

Now let me compile the full report. Let me do one final check on the `handleProjectDeleted` localStorage gap.

Looking at `useProjectSelection.ts` lines 129-138:

```typescript
const handleProjectDeleted = useCallback((remainingProjects: Project[]) => {
    const nextProjectId = determineProjectIdToSelect(remainingProjects, null, null);
    setSelectedProjectIdState(nextProjectId);  // <-- direct state setter, NOT handleSetSelectedProjectId

    if (nextProjectId) {
      updateUserSettings('user', { lastOpenedProjectId: nextProjectId });
    } else {
      updateUserSettings('user', { lastOpenedProjectId: undefined });
    }
  }, [updateUserSettings]);
```

It uses `setSelectedProjectIdState` directly instead of `handleSetSelectedProjectId`. The latter (lines 86-106) writes to both state AND localStorage. So `handleProjectDeleted` updates state and server settings, but skips the localStorage write. This means after deleting a project, if you refresh the page before selecting another project, the fast resume from localStorage would try to load the deleted project's ID.

This IS a bug, but low severity -- `determineProjectIdToSelect` in `handleProjectsLoaded` would handle the stale ID gracefully on next fetch since it checks `projectIds.has(preferredId)`.

Now the `useProjectCRUD` side effect concern:

```typescript
setProjects(prevProjects => {
    const updated = prevProjects.filter(p => p.id !== projectId);
    onProjectDeleted(updated);  // <-- side effect in state updater
    return updated;
});
```

This calls `onProjectDeleted` (which is `handleProjectDeleted` from useProjectSelection) inside a `setProjects` updater function. React state updater functions should be pure -- side effects can cause issues with StrictMode double-invocation and Concurrent Mode. `onProjectDeleted` calls `setSelectedProjectIdState` (another state setter) and `updateUserSettings` (an async operation) -- both are side effects. In React 18 StrictMode, the updater would be called twice in development, causing `onProjectDeleted` to run twice.

## Refactoring Wave Bug Audit Report

### 1. window.__PROJECT_CONTEXT__ DEV gate -- FIXED

**Status: FIXED** (resolved in Wave 4, commit `e66565ee`)

The write in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/contexts/ProjectContext.tsx` (lines 68-75) is now unconditional:

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
      window.__PROJECT_CONTEXT__ = {
        selectedProjectId: selection.selectedProjectId,
        projects: crud.projects,
      };
    }
  }, [selection.selectedProjectId, crud.projects]);
```

No `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` guard. The comment on line 66-67 explicitly notes this is structural, not debug-only. Consumers in `useProjectGenerations.ts` (line 400), `useTasks.ts` (line 117), and `ImageGenerationToolPage.tsx` (line 43) all read it the same way.

---

### 2. useProjectCRUD side effect in state updater -- BUG

**Status: BUG** (introduced in Wave 4)

File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectCRUD.ts`, lines 300-304:

```typescript
setProjects(prevProjects => {
    const updated = prevProjects.filter(p => p.id !== projectId);
    onProjectDeleted(updated);  // side effect inside state updater
    return updated;
});
```

`onProjectDeleted` calls `setSelectedProjectIdState()` (another React state setter) and `updateUserSettings()` (an async network call). React state updater functions must be pure. In React 18 StrictMode, this updater is invoked twice in development, which would call `onProjectDeleted` twice -- triggering a double `updateUserSettings` call.

**Fix:** Move the side effect outside the updater:

```typescript
setProjects(prevProjects => prevProjects.filter(p => p.id !== projectId));
// Get the filtered list for the callback
const updated = projects.filter(p => p.id !== projectId);
onProjectDeleted(updated);
```

Or use a `useEffect` that watches `projects` after deletion.

---

### 3. useProjectSelection localStorage gap -- BUG (low severity)

**Status: BUG** (introduced in Wave 4)

File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/useProjectSelection.ts`, lines 129-138:

```typescript
const handleProjectDeleted = useCallback((remainingProjects: Project[]) => {
    const nextProjectId = determineProjectIdToSelect(remainingProjects, null, null);
    setSelectedProjectIdState(nextProjectId);  // bypasses handleSetSelectedProjectId
    // ...
}, [updateUserSettings]);
```

`handleProjectDeleted` uses `setSelectedProjectIdState` directly instead of `handleSetSelectedProjectId`, which also writes to localStorage. After deleting a project, localStorage retains the old (now-deleted) project ID. On page refresh, fast resume will attempt to restore the deleted project ID.

**Mitigated** by `determineProjectIdToSelect` in `handleProjectsLoaded`, which validates the ID against the actual project list. So the stale localStorage value is overwritten on next fetch. But there's a brief flash/delay where the wrong project is "selected" before fetch completes.

**Fix:** Either call `handleSetSelectedProjectId(nextProjectId)` instead, or add the localStorage write explicitly:

```typescript
setSelectedProjectIdState(nextProjectId);
if (nextProjectId) {
    localStorage.setItem('lastSelectedProjectId', nextProjectId);
} else {
    localStorage.removeItem('lastSelectedProjectId');
}
```


The empty middle column means it is not present on the remote.

Meanwhile, the `complete_task` edge function was modified in Wave 1 (and further in Wave 3) to use the FK join syntax:

```typescript
.select(`id, task_type, project_id, params, task_types!tasks_task_type_fkey(tool_type, category, content_type, variant_type)`)
```

If `complete_task` was deployed (via `npx supabase functions deploy complete_task`) without first deploying the migration, PostgREST would fail to resolve `!tasks_task_type_fkey` and the query would error. This would break ALL task completions in production.

**However:** If `complete_task` has NOT been redeployed since Wave 1, the old version (which uses two separate queries) is still running and production is fine. The risk is that the next deployment of the function without first pushing the migration would break production.

**Fix:** Deploy the migration first: `npx supabase db push --linked`, then deploy the function.

### 5. PanesContext side effect in state updater -- FIXED

**Status: FIXED** (resolved in Wave 2, commit `9a79450f`)

File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/contexts/PanesContext.tsx`, lines 115-143.

The `savePaneLocks` call is now OUTSIDE the `setLocks` updater. The code has an explicit comment on line 128:

```typescript
// Save to database (desktop and tablet only, not small phones)
// Kept outside setLocks updater to avoid side effects in state updater functions
if (!isSmallMobile) {
    const exclusiveLock = (isMobile || isTablet) && isLocked;
    savePaneLocks(exclusiveLock
      ? { shots: false, tasks: false, gens: false, [lockKey]: isLocked }
      : { [lockKey]: isLocked });
}
```

The pattern computes the new lock state inline (duplicating the logic) rather than reading from the updater. This is slightly redundant but correct -- the `savePaneLocks` call is a side effect that belongs outside the updater.

### 6. useDropActions bare supabase -- BUG

**Status: BUG** (introduced in Wave 5b, commit `d4a4ea75`)

File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotEditor/hooks/useDropActions.ts`, lines 122 and 291.

`supabase` is used directly without being imported:

```typescript
const { data } = await supabase        // line 122
    .from('shot_generations')
    // ...

const { data: checkData } = await supabase  // line 291
    .from('shot_generations')
    // ...
```

The file imports from `@/shared/components/ui/sonner`, `@/shared/lib/errorHandler`, etc., but NOT from `@/integrations/supabase/client`. With `noImplicitAny: false` in `tsconfig.json`, TypeScript does not flag this.

At runtime, ES modules run in strict mode. In strict mode, bare `supabase` as an undeclared variable throws `ReferenceError: supabase is not defined`. While `window.supabase` is set in the Supabase client init, that does not make `supabase` available as a bare name in strict mode.

This bug is in a fallback code path (checking whether timeline positions were set by the upload mutation), so it may not have been triggered yet. But when the fallback IS needed (upload mutation doesn't set positions), it will crash with a ReferenceError.

**Fix:** Add the import:

```typescript
import { supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
```

Note: the helper file `timelineDropHelpers.ts` correctly imports supabase (line 10). This was likely an oversight during the extraction in Wave 5b.

---

### 7. usePairSettingsHandler unnecessary dep -- KNOWN (acceptable tech debt)

**Status: KNOWN**

File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/Timeline/hooks/usePairSettingsHandler.ts`, line 116:

```typescript
}, [onPairClick, images, trailingEndFrame, currentPositions, pairDataByIndex, pairInfo, imagePositions]);
```

`currentPositions` is in the dependency array but is not referenced in the callback body. It's declared in the props interface (line 10) and passed through, but the callback only uses `imagePositions`, `images`, `trailingEndFrame`, `pairInfo`, `pairDataByIndex`, and `onPairClick`.

This is technically harmless -- it causes unnecessary re-creation of the callback when `currentPositions` changes, which could trigger unnecessary re-renders downstream. However, `currentPositions` is likely a `Map` that changes frequently (on drag), so this could cause performance issues in the timeline.

**Severity:** Low. Unnecessary re-renders during drag operations could cause jank, but the Map reference may already be stable if it's memoized upstream.

**Fix:** Remove `currentPositions` from the dependency array.

```
1→/**
     2→ * useEditSettingsSync Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Handles bidirectional sync between persisted edit settings and
     5→ * the active inpainting UI state. Syncs on initial load and on changes.
     6→ *
     7→ * Includes prompt race-condition protection: if the inpainting hook resets
     8→ * its prompt to empty while persistence has a value, the prompt is restored
     9→ * from persistence after a short delay.
    10→ */
    11→
    12→import { useRef, useEffect } from 'react';
    13→import type { EditMode } from './useGenerationEditSettings';
    14→
    15→interface UseEditSettingsSyncProps {
    16→  /** Current generation ID for tracking changes */
    17→  actualGenerationId: string | undefined;
    18→  /** Whether edit settings are ready to use */
    19→  isEditSettingsReady: boolean;
    20→  /** Whether there are persisted settings for this generation */
    21→  hasPersistedSettings: boolean;
    22→
    23→  // Persisted values
    24→  persistedEditMode: EditMode | undefined;
    25→  persistedNumGenerations: number | undefined;
    26→  persistedPrompt: string | undefined;
    27→
    28→  // Current UI values
    29→  editMode: EditMode;
    30→  inpaintNumGenerations: number;
    31→  inpaintPrompt: string;
    32→
    33→  // Setters for UI values
    34→  setEditMode: (mode: EditMode) => void;
    35→  setInpaintNumGenerations: (num: number) => void;
    36→  setInpaintPrompt: (prompt: string) => void;
    37→
    38→  // Setters for persisted values
    39→  setPersistedEditMode: (mode: EditMode) => void;
    40→  setPersistedNumGenerations: (num: number) => void;
    41→  setPersistedPrompt: (prompt: string) => void;
    42→}
    43→
    44→interface UseEditSettingsSyncReturn {
    45→  /** Whether initial sync from persistence to UI has completed */
    46→  hasInitializedFromPersistence: boolean;
    47→}
    48→
    49→/**
    50→ * Syncs edit settings bidirectionally between persistence layer and UI state.
    51→ * - On load: applies persisted settings to UI (once per generation)
    52→ * - On change: syncs UI changes back to persistence
    53→ * - Protects against prompt race conditions (empty-reset while persistence has a value)
    54→ */
    55→export function useEditSettingsSync({
    56→  actualGenerationId,
    57→  isEditSettingsReady,
    58→  hasPersistedSettings,
    59→  persistedEditMode,
    60→  persistedNumGenerations,
    61→  persistedPrompt,
    62→  editMode,
    63→  inpaintNumGenerations,
    64→  inpaintPrompt,
    65→  setEditMode,
    66→  setInpaintNumGenerations,
    67→  setInpaintPrompt,
    68→  setPersistedEditMode,
    69→  setPersistedNumGenerations,
    70→  setPersistedPrompt,
    71→}: UseEditSettingsSyncProps): UseEditSettingsSyncReturn {
    72→  // Track if we've synced initial values from persistence to inpainting
    73→  const hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef = useRef(false);
    74→  const lastSyncedGenerationIdRef = useRef<string | null>(null);
    75→  // Track the last known good prompt to detect race-condition resets
    76→  const lastUserPromptRef = useRef<string>('');
    77→  // Debounce timer for prompt race-condition restoration
    78→  const promptSyncTimerRef = useRef<NodeJS.Timeout | null>(null);
    79→
    80→  // Reset sync tracking when generation changes
    81→  useEffect(() => {
    82→    if (actualGenerationId !== lastSyncedGenerationIdRef.current) {
    83→      hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current = false;
    84→      lastSyncedGenerationIdRef.current = actualGenerationId ?? null;
    85→      lastUserPromptRef.current = '';
    86→    }
    87→  }, [actualGenerationId]);
    88→
    89→  // Cleanup prompt restore timer on unmount
    90→  useEffect(() => {
    91→    return () => {
    92→      if (promptSyncTimerRef.current) clearTimeout(promptSyncTimerRef.current);
    93→    };
    94→  }, []);
    95→
    96→  // Initialize inpainting state from persisted/lastUsed settings (once per generation)
    97→  // IMPORTANT: Wait for isEditSettingsReady to ensure effective values are computed correctly
    98→  useEffect(() => {
    99→    if (
   100→      isEditSettingsReady &&
   101→      !hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current &&
   102→      actualGenerationId
   103→    ) {
   104→      hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current = true;
   105→
   106→      // Sync edit mode
   107→      if (persistedEditMode && persistedEditMode !== editMode) {
   108→        setEditMode(persistedEditMode);
   109→      }
   110→
   111→      // Sync numGenerations
   112→      if (persistedNumGenerations && persistedNumGenerations !== inpaintNumGenerations) {
   113→        setInpaintNumGenerations(persistedNumGenerations);
   114→      }
   115→
   116→      // Sync prompt (only if has persisted settings - otherwise leave empty)
   117→      if (hasPersistedSettings && persistedPrompt && persistedPrompt !== inpaintPrompt) {
   118→        setInpaintPrompt(persistedPrompt);
   119→        lastUserPromptRef.current = persistedPrompt;
   120→      }
   121→    }
   122→  }, [
   123→    isEditSettingsReady,
   124→    actualGenerationId,
   125→    hasPersistedSettings,
   126→    persistedEditMode,
   127→    persistedNumGenerations,
   128→    persistedPrompt,
   129→    editMode,
   130→    inpaintNumGenerations,
   131→    inpaintPrompt,
   132→    setEditMode,
   133→    setInpaintNumGenerations,
   134→    setInpaintPrompt,
   135→  ]);
   136→
   137→  // Sync changes FROM inpainting TO persistence (debounced via the persistence hook)
   138→  useEffect(() => {
   139→    if (!hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current || !isEditSettingsReady) return;
   140→
   141→    // Sync editMode changes
   142→    if (editMode !== persistedEditMode) {
   143→      setPersistedEditMode(editMode);
   144→    }
   145→  }, [editMode, persistedEditMode, setPersistedEditMode, isEditSettingsReady]);
   146→
   147→  useEffect(() => {
   148→    if (!hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current || !isEditSettingsReady) return;
   149→
   150→    // Sync numGenerations changes
   151→    if (inpaintNumGenerations !== persistedNumGenerations) {
   152→      setPersistedNumGenerations(inpaintNumGenerations);
   153→    }
   154→  }, [inpaintNumGenerations, persistedNumGenerations, setPersistedNumGenerations, isEditSettingsReady]);
   155→
   156→  // Sync prompt changes with race-condition protection:
   157→  // If inpaintPrompt is reset to empty but we had a user prompt, it's likely
   158→  // a race condition from hook re-initialization — restore from persistence.
   159→  useEffect(() => {
   160→    if (!hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current || !isEditSettingsReady) return;
   161→
   162→    if (inpaintPrompt === '' && lastUserPromptRef.current !== '' && persistedPrompt !== '') {
   163→      // Restore the prompt from persistence after a short delay
   164→      if (promptSyncTimerRef.current) clearTimeout(promptSyncTimerRef.current);
   165→      promptSyncTimerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
   166→        if (persistedPrompt) {
   167→          setInpaintPrompt(persistedPrompt);
   168→        }
   169→      }, 100);
   170→      return;
   171→    }
   172→
   173→    if (inpaintPrompt !== persistedPrompt) {
   174→      setPersistedPrompt(inpaintPrompt);
   175→      lastUserPromptRef.current = inpaintPrompt;
   176→    }
   177→  }, [inpaintPrompt, persistedPrompt, setPersistedPrompt, setInpaintPrompt, isEditSettingsReady]);
   178→
   179→  return {
   180→    hasInitializedFromPersistence: hasInitializedFromPersistenceRef.current,
   181→  };
   182→}
   183→
```
