   271→      const mappedProject = mapDbProjectToProject(updatedProject);
   272→
   273→      setProjects(prevProjects =>
   274→        sortProjectsByCreatedAt(
   275→          prevProjects.map(p => p.id === projectId ? mappedProject : p)
   276→        )
   277→      );
   278→      return true;
   279→    } catch (err: unknown) {
   280→      handleError(err, { context: 'ProjectContext', toastTitle: 'Failed to update project' });
   281→      return false;
   282→    } finally {
   283→      setIsUpdatingProject(false);
   284→    }
   285→  }, []);
   286→
   287→  const deleteProject = useCallback(async (projectId: string): Promise<boolean> => {
   288→    setIsDeletingProject(true);
   289→    try {
   290→      const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
   291→      if (!session) throw new Error('Not authenticated');
   292→
   293→      const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('delete-project', {
   294→        body: { projectId },
   295→      });
   296→
   297→      if (error) throw error;
   298→      if (data?.error) throw new Error(data.error);
   299→
   300→      // Filter outside updater so we can call the side-effect callback separately
   301→      // (React state updaters must be pure — no side effects)
   302→      const updated = projects.filter(p => p.id !== projectId);
   303→      setProjects(updated);
   304→      onProjectDeleted(updated);
   305→
   306→      return true;
   307→    } catch (err: unknown) {
   308→      handleError(err, { context: 'ProjectContext', toastTitle: 'Failed to delete project' });
   309→      return false;
   310→    } finally {
   311→      setIsDeletingProject(false);
   312→    }
   313→  }, [onProjectDeleted, projects]);
   314→
   315→  return {
   316→    projects,
   317→    isLoadingProjects,
   318→    fetchProjects,
   319→    addNewProject,
   320→    isCreatingProject,
   321→    updateProject,
   322→    isUpdatingProject,
   323→    deleteProject,
   324→    isDeletingProject,
   325→  };
   326→}

1→/**
     2→ * ImageEditContext — Composed provider for all image edit state.
     3→ *
     4→ * Splits state into three sub-contexts by concern:
     5→ *   - ImageEditCanvasContext: mode, brush, annotation, canvas, reposition, display
     6→ *   - ImageEditFormContext: prompts, strengths, LoRA, model, advanced settings
     7→ *   - ImageEditStatusContext: generation loading/success flags
     8→ *
     9→ * The split reduces re-renders: canvas components don't re-render when the user
    10→ * types in a prompt field, and form components don't re-render on brush strokes.
    11→ *
    12→ * For backward compatibility, ImageEditState and useImageEditSafe() still exist
    13→ * and return the full merged state. Components should migrate to the specific
    14→ * sub-context hooks (useImageEditCanvasSafe, useImageEditFormSafe,
    15→ * useImageEditStatusSafe) for optimal performance.
    16→ */
    17→
    18→import React, { useMemo } from 'react';
    19→import type { LoraMode } from '../hooks/editSettingsTypes';
    20→
    21→// Sub-contexts
    22→import {
    23→  ImageEditCanvasProvider,
    24→  useImageEditCanvasSafe,
    25→  type ImageEditCanvasState,
    26→  type ImageEditMode,
    27→} from './ImageEditCanvasContext';
    28→import {
    29→  ImageEditFormProvider,
    30→  useImageEditFormSafe,
    31→  type ImageEditFormState,
    32→} from './ImageEditFormContext';
    33→import {
    34→  ImageEditStatusProvider,
    35→  useImageEditStatusSafe,
    36→  type ImageEditStatusState,
    37→} from './ImageEditStatusContext';
    38→
    39→// Re-export sub-context types and hooks for direct consumption
    40→export type { ImageEditCanvasState, ImageEditFormState, ImageEditStatusState, ImageEditMode };
    41→export { useImageEditCanvasSafe, useImageEditFormSafe, useImageEditStatusSafe };
    42→export type { LoraMode };
    43→
    44→// ============================================================================
    45→// Composed Type (backward-compatible)
    46→// ============================================================================
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * Full image edit state, composed from the three sub-contexts.
    50→ * Consumers that need fields from only one concern should use the
    51→ * sub-context hooks directly for better performance.
    52→ */
    53→export type ImageEditState =
    54→  ImageEditCanvasState &
    55→  ImageEditFormState &
    56→  ImageEditStatusState;
    57→
    58→// ============================================================================
    59→// Composed Provider
    60→// ============================================================================
    61→
    62→interface ImageEditProviderProps {
    63→  children: React.ReactNode;
    64→  value: ImageEditState;
    65→}
    66→
    67→/**
    68→ * Provides all three sub-contexts from a single ImageEditState value.
    69→ * The value is split into sub-context slices via useMemo.
    70→ */
    71→export const ImageEditProvider: React.FC<ImageEditProviderProps> = ({

1→import { useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react';
     2→import { Project } from '@/types/project';
     3→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
     4→import { preloadingService } from '@/shared/lib/preloading';
     5→import { UserPreferences } from '@/shared/settings/userPreferences';
     6→import { determineProjectIdToSelect } from './useProjectCRUD';
     7→
     8→interface UseProjectSelectionOptions {
     9→  userId: string | null;
    10→  userPreferences: UserPreferences | undefined;
    11→  isLoadingPreferences: boolean;
    12→  updateUserSettings: (scope: 'user', patch: Partial<UserPreferences>) => Promise<void>;
    13→}
    14→
    15→/**
    16→ * Manages which project is selected, including:
    17→ * - Fast resume from localStorage
    18→ * - Cross-device sync from server preferences
    19→ * - Persistence to both localStorage and server
    20→ */
    21→export function useProjectSelection({
    22→  userId,
    23→  userPreferences,
    24→  isLoadingPreferences,
    25→  updateUserSettings,
    26→}: UseProjectSelectionOptions) {
    27→  // CROSS-DEVICE SYNC: Track if we had a localStorage value at startup
    28→  const hadLocalStorageValueRef = useRef<boolean>(false);
    29→  const hasAppliedServerPreferencesRef = useRef<boolean>(false);
    30→
    31→  // FAST RESUME: Try to restore selectedProjectId from localStorage immediately
    32→  const [selectedProjectId, setSelectedProjectIdState] = useState<string | null>(() => {
    33→    try {
    34→      const stored = localStorage.getItem('lastSelectedProjectId');
    35→      if (stored) {
    36→        hadLocalStorageValueRef.current = true;
    37→        return stored;
    38→      } else {
    39→        hadLocalStorageValueRef.current = false;
    40→      }
    41→    } catch (e) {
    42→      console.error('[ProjectContext:FastResume] localStorage access failed:', e);
    43→      hadLocalStorageValueRef.current = false;
    44→    }
    45→    return null;
    46→  });
    47→
    48→  // Keep a ref for synchronous access to latest preferences
    49→  const userPreferencesRef = useRef(userPreferences);
    50→  useEffect(() => {
    51→    userPreferencesRef.current = userPreferences;
    52→  }, [userPreferences]);
    53→
    54→  // CROSS-DEVICE SYNC: Reset sync flag when user logs out
    55→  useEffect(() => {
    56→    if (!userId) {
    57→      hasAppliedServerPreferencesRef.current = false;
    58→    }
    59→  }, [userId]);
    60→
    61→  // CROSS-DEVICE SYNC: When preferences load on a new device (no localStorage),
    62→  // update the selected project to match the server's lastOpenedProjectId
    63→  const applyCrossDeviceSync = useCallback((projects: Project[]) => {
    64→    if (hadLocalStorageValueRef.current) return;
    65→    if (hasAppliedServerPreferencesRef.current) return;
    66→    if (isLoadingPreferences || !userPreferences) return;
    67→    if (!projects.length) return;
    68→
    69→    const serverLastOpenedId = userPreferences.lastOpenedProjectId;
    70→
    71→    if (serverLastOpenedId && serverLastOpenedId !== selectedProjectId) {
    72→      const projectExists = projects.some(p => p.id === serverLastOpenedId);
    73→      if (projectExists) {
    74→        setSelectedProjectIdState(serverLastOpenedId);
    75→        try {
    76→          localStorage.setItem('lastSelectedProjectId', serverLastOpenedId);
    77→        } catch (e) {
    78→          handleError(e, { context: 'ProjectContext.crossDeviceSync', showToast: false });
    79→        }
    80→      }
    81→    }
    82→
    83→    hasAppliedServerPreferencesRef.current = true;
    84→  }, [isLoadingPreferences, userPreferences, selectedProjectId]);
    85→
    86→  const handleSetSelectedProjectId = useCallback((projectId: string | null) => {
    87→    preloadingService.onProjectChange(projectId);
    88→
    89→    setSelectedProjectIdState(projectId);
    90→
    91→    if (projectId) {
    92→      try {
    93→        localStorage.setItem('lastSelectedProjectId', projectId);
    94→      } catch (e) {
    95→        handleError(e, { context: 'ProjectContext.fastResume', showToast: false });
    96→      }
    97→      updateUserSettings('user', { lastOpenedProjectId: projectId });
    98→    } else {
    99→      try {
   100→        localStorage.removeItem('lastSelectedProjectId');
   101→      } catch (e) {
   102→        handleError(e, { context: 'ProjectContext.fastResume', showToast: false });
   103→      }
   104→      updateUserSettings('user', { lastOpenedProjectId: undefined });
   105→    }
   106→  }, [updateUserSettings]);
   107→
   108→  /** Called when projects are loaded — decides which project to select. */
   109→  const handleProjectsLoaded = useCallback((projects: Project[], isNewDefault: boolean) => {
   110→    if (isNewDefault) {
   111→      // Brand new default project: select it directly
   112→      handleSetSelectedProjectId(projects[0].id);
   113→    } else {
   114→      const lastOpenedProjectId = userPreferencesRef.current?.lastOpenedProjectId;
   115→      const projectIdToSelect = determineProjectIdToSelect(projects, selectedProjectId, lastOpenedProjectId);
   116→
   117→      if (projectIdToSelect !== selectedProjectId) {
   118→        handleSetSelectedProjectId(projectIdToSelect);
   119→      }
   120→    }
   121→  }, [selectedProjectId, handleSetSelectedProjectId]);
   122→
   123→  /** Called after a new project is created. */
   124→  const handleProjectCreated = useCallback((project: Project) => {
   125→    handleSetSelectedProjectId(project.id);
   126→  }, [handleSetSelectedProjectId]);
   127→
   128→  /** Called after a project is deleted — selects the next project. */
   129→  const handleProjectDeleted = useCallback((remainingProjects: Project[]) => {
   130→    const nextProjectId = determineProjectIdToSelect(remainingProjects, null, null);
   131→    setSelectedProjectIdState(nextProjectId);
   132→
   133→    // Also update localStorage for fast resume (avoid stale deleted ID on refresh)
   134→    try {
   135→      if (nextProjectId) {
   136→        localStorage.setItem('lastSelectedProjectId', nextProjectId);
   137→      } else {
   138→        localStorage.removeItem('lastSelectedProjectId');
   139→      }
   140→    } catch { /* localStorage unavailable */ }
   141→
   142→    if (nextProjectId) {
   143→      updateUserSettings('user', { lastOpenedProjectId: nextProjectId });
   144→    } else {
   145→      updateUserSettings('user', { lastOpenedProjectId: undefined });
   146→    }
   147→  }, [updateUserSettings]);
   148→
   149→  return {
   150→    selectedProjectId,
   151→    setSelectedProjectId: handleSetSelectedProjectId,
   152→    applyCrossDeviceSync,
   153→    handleProjectsLoaded,
   154→    handleProjectCreated,
   155→    handleProjectDeleted,
   156→    userPreferencesRef,
   157→  };
   158→}
   159→

1→/**
     2→ * useSharedLightboxState
     3→ *
     4→ * Consolidates hooks that are shared between ImageLightbox and VideoLightbox.
     5→ * This forms the foundation for splitting MediaLightbox into media-type-specific
     6→ * components while avoiding hook duplication.
     7→ *
     8→ * Included hooks (shared by both image and video):
     9→ * - Variants: useVariants, useVariantSelection, useVariantPromotion
    10→ * - Navigation: useLightboxNavigation, useSwipeNavigation
    11→ * - Star toggle: useStarToggle
    12→ * - References: useReferences, useJoinClips
    13→ * - Lineage: useGenerationLineage
    14→ * - Shot management: useShotPositioning, useShotCreation
    15→ * - Source generation: useSourceGeneration
    16→ * - Make main variant: useMakeMainVariant
    17→ * - Effective media: useEffectiveMedia
    18→ * - Layout mode: useLayoutMode
    19→ * - Button group props: useButtonGroupProps
    20→ *
    21→ * NOT included (media-type specific):
    22→ * - Image: useInpainting, useUpscale, useMagicEditMode, useRepositionMode, useImg2ImgMode
    23→ * - Video: useLightboxVideoMode, useVideoRegenerateMode
    24→ */

   252→// ============================================================================

   255→
   256→export function useSharedLightboxState(props: UseSharedLightboxStateProps): UseSharedLightboxStateReturn {
   257→  const {
   258→    // Core
   259→    media,
   260→    isVideo,
   261→    selectedProjectId,
   262→    isMobile,
   263→    isFormOnlyMode,
   264→    onClose,
   265→    readOnly,
   266→    variantFetchGenerationId,
   267→    initialVariantId,
   268→    starred,
   269→    onOpenExternalGeneration,
   270→    // Navigation
   271→    showNavigation,
   272→    hasNext = false,
   273→    hasPrevious = false,
   274→    handleSlotNavNext,
   275→    handleSlotNavPrev,
   276→    swipeDisabled,
   277→    // Shot management
   278→    shotId,
   279→    selectedShotId,

   286→    onShowSecondaryTick,
   287→    onOptimisticPositioned,
   288→    onOptimisticUnpositioned,
   289→    optimisticPositionedIds,
   290→    optimisticUnpositionedIds,
   291→    positionedInSelectedShot,
   292→    associatedWithoutPositionInSelectedShot,
   293→    // Layout
   294→    showTaskDetails,
   295→    isSpecialEditMode,
   296→    isInpaintMode,
   297→    isMagicEditMode,
   298→    // Button group
   299→    isCloudMode,
   300→    showDownload,
   301→    isDownloading,
   302→    // setIsDownloading intentionally not destructured — unused in this hook
   303→    onDelete,
   304→    isDeleting,
   305→    isUpscaling,
   306→    handleUpscale,
   307→    handleEnterMagicEditMode,
   308→    // Effective media
   309→    effectiveImageUrl,
   310→    imageDimensions,
   311→    projectAspectRatio,
   312→  } = props;
   313→
   314→  // ========================================
   315→  // VARIANTS
   316→  // ========================================
   317→
   318→  const variantsHook = useVariants({
   319→    generationId: variantFetchGenerationId,
   320→    enabled: !isFormOnlyMode,
   321→  });
   322→  const {
   323→    variants,
   324→    primaryVariant,
   325→    activeVariant,
   326→    isLoading: isLoadingVariants,
   327→    setActiveVariantId: rawSetActiveVariantId,
   328→    refetch: refetchVariants,
   329→    setPrimaryVariant,
   330→    deleteVariant,
   331→  } = variantsHook;
   332→
   333→  // Variant selection with mark-as-viewed
   334→  const { setActiveVariantId: baseSetActiveVariantId, isViewingNonPrimaryVariant } = useVariantSelection({
   335→    media,
   336→    rawSetActiveVariantId,
   337→    activeVariant,
   338→    variants,
   339→    initialVariantId,
   340→  });
   341→
   342→  // Ref to track intended active variant ID synchronously (for download race condition fix)
   343→  const intendedActiveVariantIdRef = useRef<string | null>(activeVariant?.id || null);
   344→
   345→  // Keep ref in sync when activeVariant changes
   346→  useEffect(() => {
   347→    if (activeVariant?.id && activeVariant.id !== intendedActiveVariantIdRef.current) {
   348→      intendedActiveVariantIdRef.current = activeVariant.id;
   349→    }
   350→  }, [activeVariant?.id]);
   351→
   352→  // Wrap setActiveVariantId to update ref synchronously
   353→  const setActiveVariantId = useCallback((variantId: string) => {
   354→    intendedActiveVariantIdRef.current = variantId;
   355→    baseSetActiveVariantId(variantId);
   356→  }, [baseSetActiveVariantId]);
   357→
   358→  // Variant promotion
   359→  // Note: media.id may be undefined in form-only mode, but promotion actions
   360→  // won't be triggered since there's no media to promote. Use empty string as fallback.
   361→  const {
   362→    promoteSuccess,
   363→    isPromoting,
   364→    handlePromoteToGeneration,
   365→    handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot,
   366→  } = useVariantPromotion({
   367→    selectedProjectId,
   368→  });
   369→
   370→  // ========================================
   371→  // NAVIGATION
   372→  // ========================================
   373→
   374→  const navigationHook = useLightboxNavigation({
   375→    onNext: handleSlotNavNext,
   376→    onPrevious: handleSlotNavPrev,
   377→    onClose,
   378→  });
   379→  const { safeClose, activateClickShield } = navigationHook;
   380→
   381→  const swipeNavigation = useSwipeNavigation({
   382→    onSwipeLeft: () => {
   383→      if (hasNext) handleSlotNavNext();
   384→    },
   385→    onSwipeRight: () => {
   386→      if (hasPrevious) handleSlotNavPrev();
   387→    },
   388→    disabled: swipeDisabled || readOnly || !showNavigation,
   389→    hasNext,
   390→    hasPrevious,
   391→    threshold: 50,
   392→    velocityThreshold: 0.3,
   393→  });
   394→
   395→  // ========================================
   396→  // STAR TOGGLE
   397→  // ========================================
   398→
   399→  const starToggleHook = useStarToggle({ media, starred, shotId });
   400→  const { localStarred, setLocalStarred, toggleStarMutation, handleToggleStar } = starToggleHook;
   401→
   402→  // ========================================
   403→  // REFERENCES & JOIN CLIPS
   404→  // ========================================
   405→
   406→  const referencesHook = useReferences({ media, selectedProjectId, isVideo, selectedShotId });
   407→  const {
   408→    isAddingToReferences,
   409→    addToReferencesSuccess,
   410→    handleAddToReferences,
   411→  } = referencesHook;
   412→
   413→  const {
   414→    isAddingToJoin,
   415→    addToJoinSuccess,
   416→    handleAddToJoin,
   417→    handleGoToJoin,
   418→  } = useJoinClips({ media, isVideo });
   419→
   420→  // ========================================
   421→  // LINEAGE
   422→  // ========================================
   423→
   424→  const lineageHook = useGenerationLineage({ media, enabled: !isFormOnlyMode });
   425→  const {
   426→    derivedItems,
   427→    derivedGenerations,
   428→    derivedPage,
   429→    derivedTotalPages,
   430→    paginatedDerived,
   431→    setDerivedPage,
   432→  } = lineageHook;
   433→
   434→  // ========================================
   435→  // SHOT MANAGEMENT
   436→  // ========================================
   437→
   438→  // Shot creation
   439→  const shotCreationHook = useShotCreation({
   440→    media,

   452→  } = shotCreationHook;
   453→
   454→  // Shot positioning
   455→  const computedPositionedInSelectedShot = useMemo(() => {
   456→    if (typeof positionedInSelectedShot === 'boolean') return positionedInSelectedShot;
   457→    return undefined;
   458→  }, [positionedInSelectedShot]);
   459→
   460→  const shotPositioningHook = useShotPositioning({
   461→    media,
   462→    selectedShotId,
   463→    allShots,
   464→    positionedInSelectedShot: computedPositionedInSelectedShot,
   465→    associatedWithoutPositionInSelectedShot,
   466→    optimisticPositionedIds,
   467→    optimisticUnpositionedIds,
   468→    onNavigateToShot,
   469→    onClose,
   470→    onAddToShot,
   471→    onAddToShotWithoutPosition,
   472→    onShowTick,
   473→    onShowSecondaryTick,
   474→    onOptimisticPositioned,
   475→    onOptimisticUnpositioned,
   476→  });
   477→  const {
   478→    isAlreadyPositionedInSelectedShot,
   479→    isAlreadyAssociatedWithoutPosition,
   480→    handleAddToShot,
   481→    handleAddToShotWithoutPosition,
   482→  } = shotPositioningHook;
   483→
   484→  // ========================================
   485→  // SOURCE GENERATION
   486→  // ========================================
   487→
   488→  const { sourceGenerationData, sourcePrimaryVariant } = useSourceGeneration({
   489→    media,
   490→    onOpenExternalGeneration,
   491→  });
   492→
   493→  // ========================================
   494→  // MAKE MAIN VARIANT
   495→  // ========================================
   496→
   497→  const canMakeMainVariantFromChild = !!sourceGenerationData && !!media.location;
   498→  const canMakeMainVariantFromVariant = isViewingNonPrimaryVariant && !!activeVariant?.location;
   499→  const canMakeMainVariant = canMakeMainVariantFromChild || canMakeMainVariantFromVariant;
   500→
   501→  const { isMakingMainVariant, handleMakeMainVariant } = useMakeMainVariant({
   502→    media,
   503→    sourceGenerationData,
   504→    canMakeMainVariantFromChild,
   505→    canMakeMainVariantFromVariant,
   506→    activeVariant,
   507→    setPrimaryVariant,
   508→    refetchVariants,
   509→    shotId,

   511→    onClose,
   512→  });
   513→
   514→  // ========================================
   515→  // EFFECTIVE MEDIA
   516→  // ========================================
   517→
   518→  const { effectiveVideoUrl, effectiveMediaUrl, effectiveImageDimensions } = useEffectiveMedia({
   519→    isVideo,
   520→    activeVariant,
   521→    effectiveImageUrl,
   522→    imageDimensions,
   523→    projectAspectRatio,

   525→
   526→  // ========================================

   528→  // ========================================
   529→
   530→  const layoutHook = useLayoutMode({

   535→    isInpaintMode,
   536→    isMagicEditMode,
   537→  });
   538→  const {
   539→    isTabletOrLarger,
   540→    isTouchLikeDevice,
   541→    shouldShowSidePanel,
   542→    isUnifiedEditMode,
   543→    isPortraitMode,

   545→
   546→  // ========================================
   547→  // BUTTON GROUP PROPS

   549→
   550→  const handleDelete = useCallback(() => {

   554→  // NOTE: handleDownload is NOT provided here - it requires media-specific logic
   555→  // (variant selection, content type, etc.) that only ImageLightbox/VideoLightbox have.
   556→  // Parent components MUST add handleDownload to buttonGroupProps.topRight.
   557→  const buttonGroupProps = useButtonGroupProps({

   559→    readOnly,
   560→    isSpecialEditMode,
   561→    selectedProjectId,
   562→    isCloudMode,
   563→    mediaId: media.id,
   564→    handleEnterMagicEditMode,
   565→    showDownload,
   566→    // handleDownload intentionally omitted - parent must provide
   567→    isDownloading,
   568→    onDelete,
   569→    handleDelete,
   570→    isDeleting,
   571→    onClose,
   572→    isUpscaling,
   573→    handleUpscale,

   100→

     5→
     6→interface UseTrainingDataUploadProps {

    20→export function useTrainingDataUpload({
    21→  selectedBatchId,
    22→  videos,

    28→  const [isUploading, setIsUploading] = useState(false);
    29→
    30→  /** Get the duration (in seconds) of a video file via a temporary <video> element. */
    31→  const getVideoDuration = (file: File): Promise<number> => {
    32→    return new Promise((resolve) => {
    33→      const video = document.createElement('video');
    34→      video.preload = 'metadata';
    35→      video.onloadedmetadata = () => {
    36→        resolve(video.duration);
    37→        URL.revokeObjectURL(video.src);
    38→      };
    39→      video.onerror = () => {
    40→        console.warn('Could not get video duration for:', file.name);
    41→        resolve(0);
    42→        URL.revokeObjectURL(video.src);
    43→      };
    44→      video.src = URL.createObjectURL(file);
    45→    });
    46→  };
    47→
    48→  /** Upload a single video file to storage + DB. Returns the new video's ID. */
    49→  const uploadVideoFile = async (file: File, userId: string): Promise<string> => {
    50→    const duration = await getVideoDuration(file);
    51→
    52→    const fileExt = file.name.split('.').pop();
    53→    const fileName = `${userId}/${Date.now()}.${fileExt}`;
    54→
    55→    const { error: uploadError } = await supabase.storage
    56→      .from('training-data')
    57→      .upload(fileName, file);
    58→
    59→    if (uploadError) {
    60→      console.error('[Upload] Storage upload error:', uploadError);
    61→      throw uploadError;
    62→    }
    63→
    64→    const { data, error } = await supabase
    65→      .from('training_data')
    66→      .insert({
    67→        user_id: userId,
    68→        batch_id: selectedBatchId!,
    69→        original_filename: file.name,
    70→        storage_location: fileName,

    72→        metadata: {

    74→          type: file.type,
    75→        },
    76→      })
    77→      .select()
    78→      .single();
    79→
    80→    if (error) {
    81→      console.error('[Upload] Database insert error:', error);
    82→      throw error;
    83→    }
    84→
    85→    setVideos(prev => [transformVideo(data), ...prev]);
    86→    return data.id;
    87→  };
    88→
    89→  /** Create a segment for a video, resolving null endTimeMs from the video's duration. */
    90→  const createSegmentForVideo = async (
    91→    videoId: string,
    92→    startTimeMs: number,
    93→    endTimeMs: number | null,
    94→    description: string,
    95→  ) => {
    96→    if (endTimeMs === null) {
    97→      const localVideo = videos.find(v => v.id === videoId);
    98→      if (localVideo?.duration) {
    99→        endTimeMs = Math.round(localVideo.duration * 1000);
   100→      } else {
   101→        const { data, error } = await supabase
   102→          .from('training_data')
   103→          .select('duration')
   104→          .eq('id', videoId)
   105→          .single();
   106→
   107→        if (!error && data?.duration) {
   108→          endTimeMs = Math.round(data.duration * 1000);
   109→        } else {
   110→          endTimeMs = 10000;
   111→        }
   112→      }
   113→    }
   114→
   115→    await createSegment(videoId, startTimeMs, endTimeMs, description);
   116→  };
   117→
   118→  /** Upload a single video file. Wraps uploadVideoFile with auth + batch checks. */
   119→  const uploadVideo = async (file: File): Promise<string> => {
   120→    setIsUploading(true);
   121→    try {
   122→      const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
   123→      if (!user) throw new Error('User not authenticated');
   124→
   125→      if (!selectedBatchId) {
   126→        throw new Error('Please select a batch first');
   127→      }
   128→
   129→      return await uploadVideoFile(file, user.id);
   130→    } catch (error) {
   131→      console.error('[Upload] Error uploading video:', error);
   132→      throw error;
   133→    } finally {
   134→      setIsUploading(false);
   135→    }
   136→  };
   137→
   138→  /** Upload multiple videos, optionally creating segments based on each file's split mode. */
   139→  const uploadVideosWithSplitModes = async (videoFiles: Array<{
   140→    file: File;

   142→    detectedScenes?: number[];
   143→  }>): Promise<void> => {

   149→      if (!selectedBatchId) {
   150→        throw new Error('Please select a batch first');
   151→      }

   153→      for (const videoFile of videoFiles) {

   155→
   156→        switch (videoFile.splitMode) {
   157→          case 'take-all':

   164→                const startTime = videoFile.detectedScenes[i];
   165→                const endTime = videoFile.detectedScenes[i + 1];
   166→                await createSegmentForVideo(
   167→                  videoId,
   168→                  Math.round(startTime * 1000),
   169→                  Math.round(endTime * 1000),
   170→                  `Auto-detected scene ${i + 1}`,
   171→                );
   172→              }
   173→            } else {
   174→              await createSegmentForVideo(videoId, 0, null, 'Auto-scene fallback (full video)');
   175→            }

   177→
   178→          case 'manual':
   179→            // Don't create any segments - user will do it manually
   180→            break;
   181→        }
   182→      }

   184→      // Refresh videos to ensure they're properly loaded

   194→      throw error;
   195→    } finally {
   196→      setIsUploading(false);
   197→    }
   198→  };

   205→}

1→import { ReactNode } from 'react';
     2→import { useAuth } from '@/shared/contexts/AuthContext';
     3→
     4→/**
     5→ * AuthGate prevents data-dependent providers from rendering before the
     6→ * initial auth check completes. This is NOT an auth wall -- once the
     7→ * auth state is known (logged in OR logged out), children render normally.
     8→ */
     9→export const AuthGate = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => {
    10→  const { isLoading } = useAuth();
    11→
    12→  if (isLoading) return null;
    13→
    14→  return <>{children}</>;
    15→};

     5→ * Debug hook to monitor ProjectContext state changes on mobile
     6→ * Enable by setting DEBUG_PROJECT_CONTEXT=true in localStorage

    14→

    16→    const debugInfo = {
    17→      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    18→      isMobile,
    19→      projectsCount: projects.length,
    20→      selectedProjectId: selectedProjectId || 'null',
    21→      isLoadingProjects,
    22→      userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
    23→    };

    25→    // Also log to a global debug array for inspection
    26→    if (!window.__projectDebugLog) {
    27→      window.__projectDebugLog = [];
    28→    }
    29→    window.__projectDebugLog.push(debugInfo);
    30→
    31→    // Keep only last 50 entries
    32→    if (window.__projectDebugLog.length > 50) {
    33→      window.__projectDebugLog = window.__projectDebugLog.slice(-50);
    34→    }
    35→  }, [projects, selectedProjectId, isLoadingProjects]);

1→import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
     2→import { isMobileUA } from '@/shared/hooks/use-mobile';
     3→
     4→interface UseMobileTimeoutFallbackOptions {
     5→  /** Whether the operation is currently in a loading state */
     6→  isLoading: boolean;
     7→  /** Called when the timeout fires while still loading (e.g. retry fetch, set defaults) */
     8→  onTimeout: () => void;
     9→  /** Timeout duration on mobile devices (default: 15000ms) */
    10→  mobileTimeoutMs?: number;
    11→  /** Timeout duration on desktop (default: 10000ms) */
    12→  desktopTimeoutMs?: number;
    13→  /** Whether the fallback is enabled (default: true) */
    14→  enabled?: boolean;
    15→}
    16→
    17→/**
    18→ * Shared mobile stall recovery hook.
    19→ *
    20→ * When `isLoading` becomes true, starts a timer (longer on mobile).
    21→ * If loading hasn't finished by the time the timer fires, calls `onTimeout`.
    22→ * Timer is cleared when loading finishes or the component unmounts.
    23→ *
    24→ * Replaces inline [MobileStallFix] patterns in ProjectContext and UserSettingsContext.
    25→ */
    26→export function useMobileTimeoutFallback({
    27→  isLoading,
    28→  onTimeout,
    29→  mobileTimeoutMs = 15000,
    30→  desktopTimeoutMs = 10000,
    31→  enabled = true,
    32→}: UseMobileTimeoutFallbackOptions): void {
    33→  const onTimeoutRef = useRef(onTimeout);
    34→  onTimeoutRef.current = onTimeout;
    35→
    36→  useEffect(() => {
    37→    if (!enabled || !isLoading) return;
    38→
    39→    const isMobile = isMobileUA();
    40→    const timeoutMs = isMobile ? mobileTimeoutMs : desktopTimeoutMs;
    41→
    42→    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    43→      onTimeoutRef.current();
    44→    }, timeoutMs);
    45→
    46→    return () => {
    47→      clearTimeout(timer);
    48→    };
    49→  }, [isLoading, enabled, mobileTimeoutMs, desktopTimeoutMs]);
    50→}
    51→

    19→ * - Cross-device sync when preferences + projects are both loaded

    23→export function useProjectDefaults({

+/**
+ * Shared billing utilities for edge functions
+ *
+ * Centralizes:
+ *  - Orchestrator/sub-task detection (extractOrchestratorRef, isSubTask)
+ *  - Sub-task query filter for Supabase `.or()` calls
+ *  - Cost calculation HTTP trigger
+ *
+ * Consumers: calculate-task-cost, update-task-status, complete_task
+ */
+
+// ===== Constants =====
+
+/** UUID v4 regex — used to distinguish real orchestrator FK refs from human-readable IDs */
+export const UUID_REGEX = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
+
+// ===== Orchestrator reference extraction =====
+
+/**
+ * Extract orchestrator_task_id from task params.
+ *
+ * Sub-tasks can store the orchestrator reference in multiple param paths
+ * depending on the task type and how they were created:
+ *  - params.orchestrator_task_id_ref          (travel_segment)
+ *  - params.orchestrator_details.orchestrator_task_id  (join_clips_segment)
+ *  - params.originalParams.orchestrator_details.orchestrator_task_id (legacy)
+ *  - params.orchestrator_task_id              (some legacy tasks)
+ *
+ * Returns the raw string value (may not be a valid UUID) or null.
+ */
+export function extractOrchestratorRef(params: any): string | null {
+  if (!params || typeof params !== 'object') return null;
+
+  return (
+    params.orchestrator_task_id_ref ||
+    params.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
+    params.originalParams?.orchestrator_details?.orchestrator_task_id ||
+    params.orchestrator_task_id ||
+    null
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * Determine whether a task is a sub-task of an orchestrator.
+ *
+ * A task is a sub-task when:
+ *  1. Its params contain an orchestrator reference (via any of the known paths)
+ *  2. That reference is a valid UUID (not a human-readable orchestrator ID)
+ *  3. The reference is NOT the task's own ID (orchestrators store their own ID
+ *     in params.orchestrator_details.orchestrator_task_id for children to copy)
+ *
+ * @param params  - task.params (object, not stringified)
+ * @param taskId  - the task's own ID, to guard against self-references
+ * @returns The orchestrator task ID if this is a sub-task, or null otherwise
+ */
+export function getSubTaskOrchestratorId(params: any, taskId: string): string | null {
+  const ref = extractOrchestratorRef(params);
+  if (!ref) return null;
+  if (!UUID_REGEX.test(ref)) return null;
+  if (ref === taskId) return null;
+  return ref;
+}
+
+// ===== Sub-task query filter =====
+
+/**
+ * Build a Supabase PostgREST `.or()` filter string that finds all tasks
+ * whose params reference the given orchestrator task ID.
+ *
+ * Covers all four param paths where a sub-task may store the reference.
+ *
+ * Usage:
+ *   supabase.from('tasks').select('...').or(buildSubTaskFilter(orchestratorId))
+ */
+export function buildSubTaskFilter(orchestratorTaskId: string): string {
+  return [
+    `params->>orchestrator_task_id_ref.eq.${orchestratorTaskId}`,
+    `params->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId}`,
+    `params->originalParams->orchestrator_details->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId}`,
+    `params->>orchestrator_task_id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId}`,
+  ].join(',');
+}
+
+// ===== Cost calculation trigger =====
+
+/**
+ * Trigger the calculate-task-cost edge function for a given task.
+ *
+ * This is a fire-and-forget HTTP call (errors are logged, not thrown).
+ *
+ * @param supabaseUrl - The Supabase project URL
+ * @param serviceKey  - The service role key for authentication
+ * @param taskId      - The task ID to calculate cost for
+ * @param logTag      - Optional log tag prefix (default: 'CostCalc')
+ */
+export async function triggerCostCalculation(
+  supabaseUrl: string,
+  serviceKey: string,
+  taskId: string,
+  logTag: string = 'CostCalc'
+): Promise<void> {
+  try {
+    console.log(`[${logTag}] Triggering cost calculation for ${taskId}...`);
+    const costResp = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/functions/v1/calculate-task-cost`, {
+      method: "POST",
+      headers: {
+        "Authorization": `Bearer ${serviceKey}`,
+        "Content-Type": "application/json"
+      },
+      body: JSON.stringify({ task_id: taskId })
+    });
+
+    if (costResp.ok) {
+      const costData = await costResp.json();
+      if (costData.skipped) {
+        console.log(`[${logTag}] Cost calculation skipped: ${costData.reason}`);
+      } else if (typeof costData.cost === 'number') {
+        console.log(`[${logTag}] Cost calculation successful: $${costData.cost.toFixed(3)}`);
+      }
+    } else {
+      const errTxt = await costResp.text();
+      console.error(`[${logTag}] Cost calculation failed: ${errTxt}`);
+    }
+  } catch (costErr) {
+    console.error(`[${logTag}] Error triggering cost calculation:`, costErr);
+  }
+}

## 3. Behavioral Correctness

### 3a. useEditSettingsSync prompt race-condition protection
**Rating: MILD**

At `/src/shared/components/MediaLightbox/hooks/useEditSettingsSync.ts`, lines 159-171:

```typescript
if (inpaintPrompt === '' && lastUserPromptRef.current !== '' && persistedPrompt !== '') {
  // Restore the prompt from persistence after a short delay
  promptSyncTimerRef.current = setTimeout(() => {
    if (persistedPrompt) {
      setInpaintPrompt(persistedPrompt);
    }
  }, 100);
  return;
}
```

**The concern**: If a user intentionally clears the prompt (types text, then selects all and deletes), this would fight them and restore the old prompt 100ms later.

**However**, the protection requires ALL THREE conditions:
1. `inpaintPrompt === ''` (current is empty)
2. `lastUserPromptRef.current !== ''` (we had a non-empty prompt)
3. `persistedPrompt !== ''` (persistence has a non-empty prompt)

When a user intentionally clears the prompt, the sequence is:
1. User types "hello" -> `lastUserPromptRef` = "hello", `persistedPrompt` = "hello" (synced)
2. User clears to "" -> `inpaintPrompt` = "", `lastUserPromptRef` = "hello", `persistedPrompt` = "hello"
3. Race condition fires, restores "hello" after 100ms

**This IS a real issue** -- the user would see their cleared prompt get restored. The code assumes any empty->nonempty transition is a race condition, but it could also be intentional user action.

The saving grace is that the 100ms timeout fires quickly, and when the prompt is restored, the next effect cycle will sync it back. A user rapidly clearing and then typing something new would win because:
- Step 3 restores "hello"
- Step 4: user types "new prompt" -> `lastUserPromptRef` = "new prompt" -> persistence syncs

But if the user just wants an empty prompt and stops typing, they'd see it re-appear briefly. The practical impact is **mild** because:
- The inpaint prompt is typically populated before generating (you rarely want to send an empty prompt)
- The 100ms delay makes it feel like a flicker at worst
- The user can clear again and it will stay (because persistence also gets cleared on the second attempt since `persistedPrompt` was updated to the restored value, then cleared again)

Wait, actually no -- let me trace more carefully:
1. User clears -> fires restore from persistence (100ms delay)
2. Restore sets `inpaintPrompt` = "hello"
3. Effect re-runs: `inpaintPrompt` = "hello" !== `persistedPrompt` = "hello" -> no change, but `lastUserPromptRef` = "hello"
4. User clears again -> fires restore again (infinite loop!)

**This could loop**: each time the user clears, it restores. The user can never clear the prompt while persistence has a value. This is a **MILD** issue because the prompt is functional (it works for all non-empty values) but has this edge case where clearing is blocked.

### 3b. useProjectCRUD deleteProject closure
**Rating: SAFE**

At `/src/shared/hooks/useProjectCRUD.ts`, line 302:
```typescript
const updated = projects.filter(p => p.id !== projectId);
setProjects(updated);
onProjectDeleted(updated);
```

The `projects` variable comes from `useState`, and the dependency array at line 313 is `[onProjectDeleted, projects]`. This means `deleteProject` will always have the latest `projects` reference because React will recreate the callback when `projects` changes. Correct.

### 3c. useDebouncedSettingsSave flush-on-entity-change
**Rating: SAFE**

At `/src/shared/hooks/useDebouncedSettingsSave.ts`, lines 177-236:

The `useEffect` captures `entityId` at the top of the effect, and the cleanup function (which runs when `entityId` changes) correctly:
1. Clears any pending timeout
2. Checks if `pendingSettingsRef.current` matches the entity being left
3. If so, fires a flush (either custom mode or React Query mode)
4. Clears pending refs

The dependency array is `[entityId, scope, toolId, isCustomMode, projectId, queryClient]` -- all correct for re-running when the entity changes. The cleanup will fire with the *previous* entity's values because React captures them in the closure.

**One subtle note**: the `projectId` in the dependency array for the `queryKeys.settings.tool()` call on line 214 captures `projectId` from the *current* render, not the leaving entity's project. But since the flush is about the *entity being left* (which uses `pendingForEntity` from refs), and the query key uses `projectId` only for cache invalidation of the correct tool settings scope, this is fine -- if projectId changed simultaneously with entityId, the invalidation would target the new project, but the actual save goes to the correct entity via `id: pendingForEntity`. SAFE.

    11→  return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {

    22→// Verify Stripe webhook signature
    23→async function verifyStripeSignature(payload: string, signature: string, secret: string): Promise<boolean> {
    24→  const elements = signature.split(',');
    25→  const timestamp = elements.find(element => element.startsWith('t='))?.split('=')[1];
    26→  const signatures = elements.filter(element => element.startsWith('v1='));
    27→  
    28→  if (!timestamp || signatures.length === 0) {
    29→    return false;
    30→  }
    31→  
    32→  const payloadForSigning = `${timestamp}.${payload}`;
    33→  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    34→    'raw',
    35→    new TextEncoder().encode(secret),
    36→    { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
    37→    false,
    38→    ['sign']
    39→  );
    40→  
    41→  const signature_bytes = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, new TextEncoder().encode(payloadForSigning));
    42→  const signature_hex = Array.from(new Uint8Array(signature_bytes))
    43→    .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))
    44→    .join('');
    45→    
    46→  return signatures.some(sig => sig.split('=')[1] === signature_hex);
    47→}

   273→              if (autoTopupLedgerError.code === '23505') {
   274→                logger.info('Auto-topup duplicate detected via constraint', { paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id });
   275→                break;
   276→              }
   277→              logger.error('Error creating auto-top-up ledger entry', { error: autoTopupLedgerError.message });
   278→            } else {
   279→              logger.info('Auto-top-up payment processed', {
   280→                user_id: userId,
   281→                paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id,
   282→                topupAmount: parseInt(topupAmount),
   283→                dollarAmount: parseInt(topupAmount) / 100,
   284→              });
   285→            }
   286→          }
   287→        }
   288→        break;
   289→
   290→      case 'payment_intent.payment_failed':
   291→        // Handle failed auto-top-up payments
   292→        const failedPaymentIntent = event.data.object;
   293→        const failedMetadata = failedPaymentIntent.metadata || {};
   294→        
   295→        if (failedMetadata.autoTopup === 'true') {
   296→          const { userId } = failedMetadata;
   297→          
   298→          if (userId) {
   299→            logger.error('Auto-top-up payment failed', {
   300→              user_id: userId,
   301→              paymentIntentId: failedPaymentIntent.id,
   302→              errorCode: failedPaymentIntent.last_payment_error?.code,
   303→              errorMessage: failedPaymentIntent.last_payment_error?.message,
   304→            });
   305→
   306→            // On certain failure types, disable auto-top-up to prevent repeated failures
   307→            const errorCode = failedPaymentIntent.last_payment_error?.code;
   308→            if (errorCode === 'card_declined' || errorCode === 'expired_card') {
   309→              const { error: disableError } = await supabaseAdmin
   310→                .from('users')
   311→                .update({ auto_topup_enabled: false })
   312→                .eq('id', userId);
   313→
   314→              if (disableError) {
   315→                logger.error('Error disabling auto-top-up after payment failure', { error: disableError.message, user_id: userId });
   316→              } else {
   317→                logger.info('Auto-top-up disabled for user due to payment failure', { user_id: userId, errorCode });
   318→              }
   319→            }
   320→          }
   321→        }
   322→        break;
   323→
   324→      case 'invoice.payment_succeeded':
   325→        // Handle recurring subscription payments if needed in the future
   326→        logger.info('Invoice payment succeeded (not implemented yet)');
   327→        break;
   328→
   329→      case 'invoice.payment_failed':
   330→        // Handle failed payments if needed
   331→        logger.info('Invoice payment failed (not implemented yet)');
   332→        break;
   333→
   334→      default:
   335→        logger.info('Unhandled event type', { eventType: event.type });
   336→        break;
   337→    }
   338→
   339→    await logger.flush();
   340→    return jsonResponse({ received: true });
   341→
   342→  } catch (error) {
   343→    logger.error('Error processing Stripe webhook', { error: error.message });
   344→    await logger.flush();
   345→    return jsonResponse({ error: 'Internal server error' }, 500);
   346→  }
   347→});

1→// deno-lint-ignore-file
     2→/**
     3→ * System Logger for Edge Functions
     4→ * 
     5→ * Logs to both console (for immediate visibility) AND system_logs table (for persistence/querying).
     6→ * Uses a buffer pattern to batch database writes for efficiency.
     7→ * 
     8→ * Usage:
     9→ *   const logger = new SystemLogger(supabaseAdmin, 'my-function-name');
    10→ *   logger.info('Processing request', { task_id, shot_id });
    11→ *   logger.error('Something failed', { task_id, error: err.message });
    12→ *   await logger.flush(); // Call before returning response
    13→ */
    14→
    15→type LogLevel = 'DEBUG' | 'INFO' | 'WARNING' | 'ERROR' | 'CRITICAL';
    16→
    17→interface LogContext {
    18→  task_id?: string;
    19→  shot_id?: string;
    20→  user_id?: string;
    21→  [key: string]: any;
    22→}
    23→
    24→interface BufferedLog {
    25→  timestamp: string;
    26→  source_type: string;
    27→  source_id: string;
    28→  log_level: LogLevel;
    29→  message: string;
    30→  task_id: string | null;
    31→  metadata: Record<string, any>;
    32→}
    33→
    34→export class SystemLogger {
    35→  private supabaseAdmin: any;
    36→  private functionName: string;
    37→  private logPrefix: string;
    38→  private logBuffer: BufferedLog[] = [];
    39→  private defaultTaskId: string | null = null;
    40→
    41→  constructor(supabaseAdmin: any, functionName: string, defaultTaskId?: string) {
    42→    this.supabaseAdmin = supabaseAdmin;
    43→    this.functionName = functionName;
    44→    this.logPrefix = `[${functionName.toUpperCase()}]`;
    45→    this.defaultTaskId = defaultTaskId || null;
    46→  }
    47→
    48→  /**
    49→   * Set a default task_id that will be used for all subsequent logs
    50→   * Useful when you learn the task_id after construction
    51→   */
    52→  setDefaultTaskId(taskId: string | null) {
    53→    this.defaultTaskId = taskId;
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  private addToBuffer(level: LogLevel, message: string, context?: LogContext) {
    57→    const { task_id, ...metadata } = context || {};
    58→    
    59→    this.logBuffer.push({
    60→      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    61→      source_type: 'edge_function',
    62→      source_id: this.functionName,
    63→      log_level: level,
    64→      message,
    65→      task_id: task_id || this.defaultTaskId,
    66→      metadata
    67→    });
    68→  }
    69→
    70→  debug(message: string, context?: LogContext) {
    71→    console.log(`${this.logPrefix} ${message}`, context ? JSON.stringify(context) : '');
    72→    this.addToBuffer('DEBUG', message, context);
    73→  }
    74→
    75→  info(message: string, context?: LogContext) {
    76→    console.log(`${this.logPrefix} ${message}`, context ? JSON.stringify(context) : '');
    77→    this.addToBuffer('INFO', message, context);
    78→  }
    79→
    80→  warn(message: string, context?: LogContext) {
    81→    console.warn(`${this.logPrefix} ⚠️ ${message}`, context ? JSON.stringify(context) : '');
    82→    this.addToBuffer('WARNING', message, context);
    83→  }
    84→
    85→  error(message: string, context?: LogContext) {
    86→    console.error(`${this.logPrefix} ❌ ${message}`, context ? JSON.stringify(context) : '');
    87→    this.addToBuffer('ERROR', message, context);
    88→  }
    89→
    90→  critical(message: string, context?: LogContext) {
    91→    console.error(`${this.logPrefix} 🔥 CRITICAL: ${message}`, context ? JSON.stringify(context) : '');
    92→    this.addToBuffer('CRITICAL', message, context);
    93→  }
    94→
    95→  /**
    96→   * Flush all buffered logs to the database
    97→   * Call this before returning your response!
    98→   */
    99→  async flush(): Promise<{ inserted: number; errors: number }> {
   100→    if (this.logBuffer.length === 0) {
   101→      return { inserted: 0, errors: 0 };
   102→    }
   103→
   104→    try {
   105→      const { data, error } = await this.supabaseAdmin
   106→        .rpc('func_insert_logs_batch', { logs: this.logBuffer });
   107→
   108→      if (error) {
   109→        console.error(`${this.logPrefix} Failed to flush ${this.logBuffer.length} logs to database:`, error.message);
   110→        // Don't clear buffer on error - logs are lost but at least console has them
   111→        return { inserted: 0, errors: this.logBuffer.length };
   112→      }
   113→
   114→      const result = data || { inserted: this.logBuffer.length, errors: 0 };
   115→      const bufferSize = this.logBuffer.length;
   116→      this.logBuffer = []; // Clear buffer after successful flush
   117→      
   118→      console.log(`${this.logPrefix} Flushed ${bufferSize} logs to database`);
   119→      return { inserted: result.inserted || bufferSize, errors: result.errors || 0 };
   120→    } catch (e: any) {
   121→      console.error(`${this.logPrefix} Exception flushing logs:`, e?.message || e);
   122→      return { inserted: 0, errors: this.logBuffer.length };
   123→    }
   124→  }
   125→
   126→  /**
   127→   * Get the current buffer size (useful for debugging)
   128→   */
   129→  getBufferSize(): number {
   130→    return this.logBuffer.length;
   131→  }
   132→}
   133→
   134→

   163→

   177→
   178→interface ImageGenerationFormProviderProps {

    51→export function getClientIp(req: Request): string {

    54→  if (cfIp) return cfIp;
    55→  
    56→  // Standard proxy headers
    57→  const forwardedFor = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for');
    58→  if (forwardedFor) {
    59→    // Take first IP (original client)

    62→

    64→  if (realIp) return realIp;
    65→  
    66→  // Fallback - shouldn't happen in production

    68→}

    91→  
    92→  try {
    93→    // Use upsert with atomic increment via RPC function
    94→    // This handles race conditions properly
    95→    const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.rpc('check_rate_limit', {
    96→      p_key: key,
    97→      p_window_seconds: config.windowSeconds,
    98→      p_max_requests: config.maxRequests
    99→    });
   100→    
   101→    if (error) {
   102→      // If the RPC doesn't exist yet, fall through to allow (fail open)
   103→      console.warn(`${logPrefix} Rate limit check failed (allowing request):`, error.message);
   104→      return {
   105→        allowed: true,
   106→        remaining: config.maxRequests,
   107→        resetAt: new Date(now.getTime() + config.windowSeconds * 1000)
   108→      };
   109→    }
   110→    
   111→    const result = data as { allowed: boolean; count: number; reset_at: string };
   112→    const resetAt = new Date(result.reset_at);
   113→    const remaining = Math.max(0, config.maxRequests - result.count);
   114→    
   115→    if (!result.allowed) {
   116→      const retryAfter = Math.ceil((resetAt.getTime() - now.getTime()) / 1000);
   117→      console.warn(`${logPrefix} Rate limit exceeded for ${key}: ${result.count}/${config.maxRequests}`);
   118→      return {
   119→        allowed: false,
   120→        remaining: 0,
   121→        resetAt,
   122→        retryAfter
   123→      };
   124→    }
   125→    
   126→    return {
   127→      allowed: true,
   128→      remaining,
   129→      resetAt
   130→    };
   131→  } catch (err) {
   132→    // Fail open - don't block requests if rate limiting fails
   133→    console.error(`${logPrefix} Rate limit error (allowing request):`, err);
   134→    return {
   135→      allowed: true,
   136→      remaining: config.maxRequests,
   137→      resetAt: new Date(now.getTime() + config.windowSeconds * 1000)
   138→    };
   139→  }
   140→}
   141→
   142→/**
   143→ * Create rate limit headers for response
   144→ */
   145→export function rateLimitHeaders(result: RateLimitResult, config: RateLimitConfig): Record<string, string> {
   146→  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
   147→    'X-RateLimit-Limit': config.maxRequests.toString(),
   148→    'X-RateLimit-Remaining': result.remaining.toString(),
   149→    'X-RateLimit-Reset': Math.floor(result.resetAt.getTime() / 1000).toString(),
   150→  };
   151→  
   152→  if (result.retryAfter) {
   153→    headers['Retry-After'] = result.retryAfter.toString();
   154→  }
   155→  
   156→  return headers;
   157→}
   158→
   159→/**
   160→ * Create a 429 Too Many Requests response
   161→ */
   162→export function rateLimitResponse(result: RateLimitResult, config: RateLimitConfig): Response {
   163→  return new Response(
   164→    JSON.stringify({
   165→      error: 'Too many requests',
   166→      retryAfter: result.retryAfter,
   167→      message: `Rate limit exceeded. Please wait ${result.retryAfter} seconds before retrying.`
   168→    }),
   169→    {
   170→      status: 429,
   171→      headers: {
   172→        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
   173→        'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
   174→        ...rateLimitHeaders(result, config)
   175→      }
   176→    }
   177→  );
   178→}
   179→
   180→
   181→
   182→
   183→
   184→

    27→export interface TaskContext {

    37→
    38→/**

    43→async function fetchTaskContext(
    44→  supabase: any,
    45→  taskId: string
    46→): Promise<TaskContext | null> {
    47→  const { data: task, error } = await supabase
    48→    .from("tasks")

   118→export async function completeTaskHandler(req: Request, deps: CompleteTaskDeps = {}): Promise<Response> {

   293→      status: "Complete",

   318→    // 14) Calculate cost (service role only)
   319→    if (isServiceRole) {

   322→
   323→    // 15) Return success

   325→    const responseData = {

   331→

    31→// Special cost calculation for video_enhance task

    33→function calculateVideoEnhanceCost(taskParams: any): { cost: number; breakdown: any } {
    34→  let totalCost = 0;

    42→    const filmCost = VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FILM_COST_PER_SECOND * result.interpolation_compute_seconds;
    43→    totalCost += filmCost;
    44→    breakdown.interpolation = {
    45→      compute_seconds: result.interpolation_compute_seconds,
    46→      cost_per_second: VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FILM_COST_PER_SECOND,
    47→      cost: Math.round(filmCost * 1000000) / 1000000,

    54→    const upscaleCost = VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL * megapixels;

    33→  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    34→    'raw',
    35→    new TextEncoder().encode(secret),

    44→    .join('');
    45→    
    46→  return signatures.some(sig => sig.split('=')[1] === signature_hex);
    47→}

Now I have the full picture. Here's my analysis:

**`complete_task`**: Accepts both service-role (internal workers) and user JWT/PAT auth. Rate limiting should only apply to non-service-role callers. Workers (service-role) should not be rate limited as they are internal and self-regulating. For user callers, this is a task completion -- moderate rate limit is appropriate.

**`calculate-task-cost`**: Service-role only (line 148 explicitly checks `authHeader.slice(7) !== serviceKey`). Rate limiting does **not** make sense here -- it's only called internally by other edge functions/workers.

**`delete-project`**: User-facing with JWT auth. Needs rate limiting. A destructive operation that triggers cascading deletes -- should use a conservative limit.

   262→            let skipInsert = false;
   263→            try {
   264→              const { data: existingAutoTopup, error: checkError } = await supabaseAdmin
   265→                .from('credits_ledger')
   266→                .select('id')
   267→                .eq('type', 'auto_topup')
   268→                .eq('metadata->>stripe_payment_intent_id', paymentIntent.id)
   269→                .limit(1)
   270→                .maybeSingle();
   271→
   272→              if (checkError) {
   273→                logger.warn('Auto-topup idempotency check failed, proceeding with insert', { error: checkError.message });
   274→              } else if (existingAutoTopup) {
   275→                logger.info('Auto-topup webhook already processed (idempotency check)', { paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id as string });
   276→                skipInsert = true;
   277→              }
   278→            } catch (checkErr: unknown) {
   279→              logger.warn('Auto-topup idempotency check exception, proceeding with insert', { error: String(checkErr) });
   280→            }
   281→
   282→            if (skipInsert) {
   283→              break;
   284→            }
   285→
   286→            // Insert auto-top-up credit into ledger.
   287→            // The unique partial index guarantees no double-crediting even if two
   288→            // webhooks race past the fast-path check above.
   289→            const { error: autoTopupLedgerError } = await supabaseAdmin
   290→              .from('credits_ledger')
   291→              .insert({
   292→                user_id: userId,
   293→                amount: parseInt(topupAmount), // Already in cents
   294→                type: 'auto_topup',
   295→                metadata: {
   296→                  stripe_payment_intent_id: paymentIntent.id,
   297→                  amount_paid: paymentIntent.amount_received,
   298→                  currency: paymentIntent.currency,
   299→                  dollar_amount: parseInt(topupAmount) / 100,
   300→                  original_balance: parseInt(originalBalance || '0'),
   301→                  auto_topup_trigger: true,
   302→                },
   303→              });
   304→
   305→            if (autoTopupLedgerError) {
   306→              // Unique constraint violation = duplicate webhook (race with fast-path check).
   307→              // This is expected and safe — return success since the credit was already applied.
   308→              if (autoTopupLedgerError.code === '23505') {
   309→                logger.info('Auto-topup duplicate detected via unique constraint', { paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id as string });
   310→                break;
   311→              }
   312→              logger.error('Error creating auto-top-up ledger entry', { error: autoTopupLedgerError.message });
   313→            } else {
   314→              logger.info('Auto-top-up payment processed', {
   315→                user_id: userId,
   316→                paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id as string,
   317→                topupAmount: parseInt(topupAmount),
   318→                dollarAmount: parseInt(topupAmount) / 100,
   319→              });
   320→            }
   321→          }
   322→        }
   323→        break;
   324→
   325→      case 'payment_intent.payment_failed':
   326→        // Handle failed auto-top-up payments
   327→        const failedPaymentIntent = event.data.object;
   328→        const failedMetadata = (failedPaymentIntent.metadata ?? {}) as PaymentIntentMetadata;
   329→
   330→        if (failedMetadata.autoTopup === 'true') {
   331→          const { userId } = failedMetadata;
   332→
   333→          if (userId) {
   334→            const lastPaymentError = failedPaymentIntent.last_payment_error as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
   335→            logger.error('Auto-top-up payment failed', {
   336→              user_id: userId,
   337→              paymentIntentId: failedPaymentIntent.id as string,
   338→              errorCode: lastPaymentError?.code as string,
   339→              errorMessage: lastPaymentError?.message as string,
   340→            });
   341→
   342→            // On certain failure types, disable auto-top-up to prevent repeated failures
   343→            const errorCode = lastPaymentError?.code as string | undefined;
   344→            if (errorCode === 'card_declined' || errorCode === 'expired_card') {
   345→              const { error: disableError } = await supabaseAdmin
   346→                .from('users')
   347→                .update({ auto_topup_enabled: false })
   348→                .eq('id', userId);
   349→
   350→              if (disableError) {
   351→                logger.error('Error disabling auto-top-up after payment failure', { error: disableError.message, user_id: userId });
   352→              } else {
   353→                logger.info('Auto-top-up disabled for user due to payment failure', { user_id: userId, errorCode });
   354→              }
   355→            }
   356→          }
   357→        }
   358→        break;
   359→
   360→      case 'invoice.payment_succeeded':
   361→        // Handle recurring subscription payments if needed in the future
   362→        logger.info('Invoice payment succeeded (not implemented yet)');
   363→        break;
   364→
   365→      case 'invoice.payment_failed':
   366→        // Handle failed payments if needed
   367→        logger.info('Invoice payment failed (not implemented yet)');
   368→        break;
   369→
   370→      default:
   371→        logger.info('Unhandled event type', { eventType: event.type });
   372→        break;
   373→    }
   374→
   375→    await logger.flush();
   376→    return jsonResponse({ received: true });
   377→
   378→  } catch (error: unknown) {
   379→    logger.error('Error processing Stripe webhook', { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
   380→    await logger.flush();
   381→    return jsonResponse({ error: 'Internal server error' }, 500);
   382→  }
   383→});

   259→            // The unique partial index on (metadata->>'stripe_payment_intent_id')
   260→            // WHERE type = 'auto_topup' is the actual atomicity guarantee

   262→            let skipInsert = false;
   263→            try {

   265→                .from('credits_ledger')

   267→                .eq('type', 'auto_topup')
   268→                .eq('metadata->>stripe_payment_intent_id', paymentIntent.id)
   269→                .limit(1)
   270→                .maybeSingle();
   271→
   272→              if (checkError) {
   273→                logger.warn('Auto-topup idempotency check failed, proceeding with insert', { error: checkError.message });
   274→              } else if (existingAutoTopup) {
   275→                logger.info('Auto-topup webhook already processed (idempotency check)', { paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id as string });
   276→                skipInsert = true;
   277→              }
   278→            } catch (checkErr: unknown) {
   279→              logger.warn('Auto-topup idempotency check exception, proceeding with insert', { error: String(checkErr) });
   280→            }
   281→
   282→            if (skipInsert) {
   283→              break;
   284→            }
   285→
   286→            // Insert auto-top-up credit into ledger.
   287→            // The unique partial index guarantees no double-crediting even if two
   288→            // webhooks race past the fast-path check above.
   289→            const { error: autoTopupLedgerError } = await supabaseAdmin
   290→              .from('credits_ledger')
   291→              .insert({
   292→                user_id: userId,
   293→                amount: parseInt(topupAmount), // Already in cents
   294→                type: 'auto_topup',
   295→                metadata: {
   296→                  stripe_payment_intent_id: paymentIntent.id,
   297→                  amount_paid: paymentIntent.amount_received,
   298→                  currency: paymentIntent.currency,
   299→                  dollar_amount: parseInt(topupAmount) / 100,
   300→                  original_balance: parseInt(originalBalance || '0'),
   301→                  auto_topup_trigger: true,
   302→                },
   303→              });
   304→
   305→            if (autoTopupLedgerError) {
   306→              // Unique constraint violation = duplicate webhook (race with fast-path check).
   307→              // This is expected and safe — return success since the credit was already applied.
   308→              if (autoTopupLedgerError.code === '23505') {
   309→                logger.info('Auto-topup duplicate detected via unique constraint', { paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id as string });
   310→                break;
   311→              }
   312→              logger.error('Error creating auto-top-up ledger entry', { error: autoTopupLedgerError.message });
   313→            } else {
   314→              logger.info('Auto-top-up payment processed', {
   315→                user_id: userId,
   316→                paymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id as string,
   317→                topupAmount: parseInt(topupAmount),
   318→                dollarAmount: parseInt(topupAmount) / 100,
   319→              });
   320→            }
   321→          }
   322→        }
   323→        break;
   324→
   325→      case 'payment_intent.payment_failed':
   326→        // Handle failed auto-top-up payments
   327→        const failedPaymentIntent = event.data.object;

   330→        if (failedMetadata.autoTopup === 'true') {

   333→          if (userId) {

   337→              paymentIntentId: failedPaymentIntent.id as string,
   338→              errorCode: lastPaymentError?.code as string,
   339→              errorMessage: lastPaymentError?.message as string,
   340→            });
   341→
   342→            // On certain failure types, disable auto-top-up to prevent repeated failures
   343→            const errorCode = lastPaymentError?.code as string | undefined;
   344→            if (errorCode === 'card_declined' || errorCode === 'expired_card') {
   345→              const { error: disableError } = await supabaseAdmin
   346→                .from('users')
   347→                .update({ auto_topup_enabled: false })
   348→                .eq('id', userId);
   349→
   350→              if (disableError) {
   351→                logger.error('Error disabling auto-top-up after payment failure', { error: disableError.message, user_id: userId });
   352→              } else {
   353→                logger.info('Auto-top-up disabled for user due to payment failure', { user_id: userId, errorCode });
   354→              }
   355→            }
   356→          }
   357→        }
   358→        break;
   359→
   360→      case 'invoice.payment_succeeded':
   361→        // Handle recurring subscription payments if needed in the future
   362→        logger.info('Invoice payment succeeded (not implemented yet)');
   363→        break;
   364→
   365→      case 'invoice.payment_failed':
   366→        // Handle failed payments if needed
   367→        logger.info('Invoice payment failed (not implemented yet)');
   368→        break;
   369→
   370→      default:
   371→        logger.info('Unhandled event type', { eventType: event.type });
   372→        break;
   373→    }
   374→
   375→    await logger.flush();
   376→    return jsonResponse({ received: true });
   377→
   378→  } catch (error: unknown) {
   379→    logger.error('Error processing Stripe webhook', { error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
   380→    await logger.flush();
   381→    return jsonResponse({ error: 'Internal server error' }, 500);

   383→});

## Changes made

The `// @ts-nocheck` directive was removed. This was the last remaining instance in the entire codebase (the only other hits are in task planning markdown files, not source code).

### 2. Added three minimal interfaces (lines 8-31)
Three interfaces were added to type the Stripe webhook payloads:

- **`StripeEvent`** -- Models the shape of any Stripe webhook event: `{ type: string, data: { object: Record<string, unknown> } }`. Using `Record<string, unknown>` for `data.object` since Stripe objects vary by event type and we don't import the Stripe SDK.

- **`CheckoutSessionMetadata`** -- Models the metadata fields set during checkout creation: `userId`, `amount`, `autoTopupEnabled`, `autoTopupAmount`, `autoTopupThreshold`. All string fields (Stripe metadata values are always strings).

- **`PaymentIntentMetadata`** -- Models the metadata for auto-top-up payment intents: `autoTopup`, `userId`, `originalBalance`, `topupAmount`.

### 3. Typed `jsonResponse` parameter (line 34)
Changed `body: any` to `body: Record<string, unknown>`. Every call site passes an object literal with string keys, so this is the correct narrowing.

### 4. Added type assertion for `JSON.parse` (line 119)
`JSON.parse(body)` is now `JSON.parse(body) as StripeEvent`. This gives the parsed event object a known shape.

### 5. Typed metadata extractions with assertions (lines 129, 252, 328)
- `session.metadata` cast via `(session.metadata ?? {}) as CheckoutSessionMetadata`
- `paymentIntent.metadata` cast via `(paymentIntent.metadata ?? {}) as PaymentIntentMetadata`
- `failedPaymentIntent.metadata` cast via `(failedPaymentIntent.metadata ?? {}) as PaymentIntentMetadata`

### 6. Added `as` assertions for `Record<string, unknown>` property access
Where values from `event.data.object` (typed as `Record<string, unknown>`) are used in contexts that need specific types:
- `session.payment_intent as string | undefined` (line 148)
- `session.customer as string` (line 175)

- `session.amount_total as number` (lines 141, 241)
- `paymentIntent.id as string` (lines 275, 309, 316)
- `failedPaymentIntent.id as string` (line 337)
- `failedPaymentIntent.last_payment_error as Record<string, unknown> | undefined` (line 334)
- `lastPaymentError?.code as string | undefined` (line 343)

### 7. Typed all catch clauses with `unknown` (lines 179, 204, 278, 378)
All `catch (error)` and `catch (checkErr)` clauses now use `: unknown`. Error message access was changed from `error.message` to the safe pattern `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)`. The `checkErr` variables already used `String(checkErr)` so those just needed the `: unknown` annotation.

---

## Summary

### Changes Made

**1. `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/complete_task/index.ts`**
- Added import of `checkRateLimit`, `rateLimitResponse`, and `RATE_LIMITS` from `../_shared/rateLimit.ts`
- Added rate limiting after authentication (step 4b), but **only for non-service-role callers**. Workers that call `complete_task` use the service-role key and are not rate limited, since they are internal and self-regulating. User-facing callers (JWT/PAT auth) are rate limited using `RATE_LIMITS.userAction` (60 requests per minute per user).

**2. `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/delete-project/index.ts`**
- Added import of `checkRateLimit` and `rateLimitResponse` from `../_shared/rateLimit.ts`
- Added rate limiting after authentication with a custom config of **10 requests per minute per user** -- a conservative limit appropriate for this destructive operation that triggers cascading deletes with an extended timeout.

**3. `calculate-task-cost` -- intentionally NOT modified**
- This function is **service-role only** (line 148 explicitly checks `authHeader.slice(7) !== serviceKey` and rejects non-service-role callers with 401). It is only called internally by other edge functions/workers (e.g., `complete_task` calls it via `triggerCostCalculationIfNotSubTask`). Rate limiting internal service-to-service calls would be counterproductive -- it could cause billing failures for legitimate task completions.

### Design Decisions

- **Same pattern as `ai-prompt`**: Both new rate limiters use the shared `checkRateLimit` / `rateLimitResponse` utilities from `_shared/rateLimit.ts`, keying on `user.id` (not IP).
- **Fail-open behavior preserved**: The shared `checkRateLimit` function already handles errors by failing open (allowing the request through if the rate limit RPC fails), so no additional error handling was needed.
- **Logger integration**: Both functions log a warning via `SystemLogger` when rate limits are exceeded, then flush before returning the 429 response.
- **No non-rate-limiting logic changed**: All existing functionality remains untouched.

   335→  // Ensure the `promptIdCounter` is always ahead of any existing numeric IDs.
   336→  // This prevents duplicate IDs which caused multiple prompts to update together.
   337→  useEffect(() => {
   338→    let nextId = prompts.reduce((max, p) => {
   339→      const match = /^prompt-(\d+)$/.exec(p.id || "");
   340→      if (match) {
   341→        const num = parseInt(match[1], 10) + 1;
   342→        return num > max ? num : max;
   343→      }
   344→      return max;
   345→    }, 1);
   346→
   347→    // Resolve any duplicate IDs on the fly by assigning new ones.
   348→    const seen = new Set<string>();
   349→    let hadDuplicates = false;
   350→    const dedupedPrompts = prompts.map(prompt => {
   351→      if (!seen.has(prompt.id)) {
   352→        seen.add(prompt.id);
   353→        return prompt;
   354→      }
   355→      hadDuplicates = true;
   356→      // Duplicate found - give it a fresh ID.
   357→      const newId = `prompt-${nextId++}`;
   358→      seen.add(newId);
   359→      return { ...prompt, id: newId };
   360→    });
   361→
   362→    if (hadDuplicates) {
   363→      setPrompts(dedupedPrompts);
   364→    }
   365→
   366→    if (nextId > promptIdCounter.current) {
   367→      promptIdCounter.current = nextId;
   368→    }

   304→      const match = /^prompt-(\d+)$/.exec(p.id || "");
   305→      if (match) {

   307→        return num > max ? num : max;

   347→    };

   351→      output_location: publicUrl,
   352→      has_thumbnail: !!thumbnailUrl
   353→    });
   354→    await logger.flush();
   355→
   356→    return new Response(JSON.stringify(responseData), {
   357→      status: 200,
   358→      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
   359→    });
   360→
   361→  } catch (error: any) {
   362→    logger.critical("Unexpected error", {

   365→      stack: error?.stack?.substring(0, 500)

   368→    await logger.flush();
   369→    return new Response(`Internal error: ${error?.message}`, { status: 500 });
   370→  }
   371→}

1→// deno-lint-ignore-file
